admin.accountsPanel.bannedState.usage: On the admin Accounts page: an account’s state when it is banned, used to sort the State column.

admin.accountsPanel.changesSaved.usage: Short message that pops up on the admin Accounts page once changes to an account have been saved.

Their API keys and share links are revoked at once, so anything using one stops working. Shared playlists stay, marked as a removed profile's. Nothing leaves the library, and this cannot be undone.
admin.accountsPanel.deleteBody.usage: On the admin Accounts page: body of the dialog asking whether to delete an account. {name} is its name.

admin.accountsPanel.deleteTitle.usage: On the admin Accounts page: heading of the dialog asking whether to delete an account.

admin.accountsPanel.deletedWho.usage: Short message that pops up on the admin Accounts page once an account has been deleted. {name} is its name.

admin.accountsPanel.devicesTab.usage: In the dialog opened with Edit account on the admin Accounts page: tab listing where the account is signed in.

admin.accountsPanel.displayTab.usage: In the dialog opened with Edit account on the admin Accounts page: tab for the account’s name, address and picture.

admin.accountsPanel.editAccount.usage: On the admin Accounts page: menu item that opens the dialog for changing an account.

admin.accountsPanel.editWho.usage: Heading of the dialog opened with Edit account on the admin Accounts page. {name} is the account’s name.

admin.accountsPanel.keepFrom.usage: In the dialog opened with Edit account on the admin Accounts page: read out by screen readers for a library button the account may see; pressing it hides the library. {library} is the library, {name} the account.

admin.accountsPanel.newPassword.usage: In the dialog opened with Edit account on the admin Accounts page: label of the field for the new password.

admin.accountsPanel.noAccounts.usage: On the admin Accounts page: shown in place of the table when there are no accounts.

admin.accountsPanel.noLibraries.usage: In the dialog opened with Edit account on the admin Accounts page: shown on the Libraries tab when no libraries exist.

admin.addWebhookDialog.title.usage: Heading of the dialog for a new webhook, and the button in it that makes the webhook.

client.describeTriggerInZone.weekly.usage: In a job's schedule, beside a time set in the server's time zone: the same moment in the viewer's own time zone. {day} is a day of the week such as Monday; {time} is a 24-hour clock time such as 04:00.

client.describeWhen.daysAgo.one.usage: In watch history, when something was watched: one day ago.

client.describeWhen.daysAgo.other.usage: In watch history, when something was watched: so many days ago, within the week.

client.describeWhen.hoursAgo.one.usage: In watch history, when something was watched: one hour ago.

client.describeWhen.hoursAgo.other.usage: In watch history, when something was watched: so many hours ago, under a day.

client.describeWhen.justNow.usage: In watch history, when something was watched: less than a minute ago.

client.describeWhen.minutesAgo.one.usage: In watch history, when something was watched: one minute ago. "min" is short for minutes.

client.describeWhen.minutesAgo.other.usage: In watch history, when something was watched: so many minutes ago. "min" is short for minutes.

client.describeWhen.yesterday.usage: In watch history, when something was watched: the day before.

client.describeWhy.asItIs.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, when the film is sent exactly as it is.

client.describeWhy.audio.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, one reason the stream is being converted. {detail} is the reason itself, such as "Client does not support the hevc video codec". This is about the sound.

client.describeWhy.container.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, one reason the stream is being converted. {detail} is the reason itself, such as "Client does not support the hevc video codec". This is about the file format.

client.describeWhy.subtitles.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, one reason the stream is being converted. {detail} is the reason itself, such as "Client does not support the hevc video codec". This is about subtitles drawn into the picture.

client.describeWhy.video.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, one reason the stream is being converted. {detail} is the reason itself, such as "Client does not support the hevc video codec". This is about the picture.

client.detectClientLabel.browser.usage: In the list of devices signed in to an account, and the sessions an administrator sees, the name of a web browser: one that could not be told apart.

client.detectClientLabel.browserOn.usage: In the list of devices signed in to an account, and the sessions an administrator sees, the name of a web browser: {browser} is its name, such as Firefox; {os} is the operating system, such as macOS.

client.fetchHousehold.couldNotSend.value: That picture could not be sent.
client.fetchHousehold.couldNotSend.usage: An error on the household set-up step for choosing the household's picture: the picture never reached the server.

client.fetchHousehold.couldNotUse.value: That picture could not be used.
client.fetchHousehold.couldNotUse.usage: An error on the household set-up step for choosing the household's picture: the server would not take it, and gave no reason.

client.fetchShares.gone.usage: Shown to somebody opening a share link that has ended, when the server gave no reason.

client.groupIntoRails.everything.usage: The title of a row of films on a page of the library: the only row, holding everything in the library.

client.groupIntoRails.films.usage: The title of a row of films on a page of the library: the films that are not part of a series, after a row for each series.

client.groupPermissions.account.usage: In the role editor, the heading over one group of permissions, those about accounts.

client.groupPermissions.administrator.usage: In the role editor, the heading over one group of permissions: the one that grants everything.

client.groupPermissions.download.usage: In the role editor, the heading over one group of permissions, those about downloads.

client.groupPermissions.jobs.usage: In the role editor, the heading over one group of permissions, those about jobs.

client.groupPermissions.library.usage: In the role editor, the heading over one group of permissions, those about libraries.

client.groupPermissions.media.usage: In the role editor, the heading over one group of permissions, those about media.

client.groupPermissions.requests.usage: In the role editor, the heading over one group of permissions, those about requests.

client.groupPermissions.server.usage: In the role editor, the heading over one group of permissions, those about server.

client.groupPermissions.sharing.usage: In the role editor, the heading over one group of permissions, those about sharing.

client.groupPermissions.streaming.usage: In the role editor, the heading over one group of permissions, those about streaming.

client.homeRows.continueWatching.usage: The title of a row on the home page: things this viewer started and has not finished.

client.homeRows.criticallyAcclaimed.usage: The title of a row on the home page: things critics rated highly.

client.homeRows.fromThe.usage: The title of a row on the home page: things from one decade. {decade} is the year it starts, such as 1990, giving "From the 1990s".

client.homeRows.pickedForYou.usage: The title of a row on the home page: things chosen for this viewer from what they watch.

client.homeRows.recentlyAdded.usage: The title of a row on the home page: what arrived in the library lately.

client.howTheFileSounds.hiResLossless.usage: A badge beside the song playing, in the words Apple Music uses: the file is lossless at more than 48 kHz.

client.howTheFileSounds.lossless.usage: A badge beside the song playing, in the words Apple Music uses: the file is lossless, up to 24-bit at 48 kHz.

client.howToFillIt.addOne.usage: Under the heading of an empty page of the library, saying what to do about it: there are no libraries yet, and this person can add one. "One" is a library.

client.howToFillIt.askToAdd.value: Ask the server admin to add one.
client.howToFillIt.askToAdd.usage: Under the heading of an empty page of the library, saying what to do about it: there are no libraries yet, and somebody else has to add one. "One" is a library.

client.howToFillIt.askToScanAll.value: Ask the server admin to scan your libraries.
client.howToFillIt.askToScanAll.usage: Under the heading of an empty page of the library, saying what to do about it: every library is empty, and somebody else has to scan them.

client.howToFillIt.askToScanOne.value: Ask the server admin to scan it.
client.howToFillIt.askToScanOne.usage: Under the heading of an empty page of the library, saying what to do about it: the library being looked at is empty, and somebody else has to scan it.

client.howToFillIt.scanAll.value: Scan your libraries, or add files to them.
client.howToFillIt.scanAll.usage: Under the heading of an empty page of the library, saying what to do about it: every library is empty, and this person can scan them.

client.howToFillIt.scanOne.value: Scan it, or add files to its folder.
client.howToFillIt.scanOne.usage: Under the heading of an empty page of the library, saying what to do about it: the library being looked at is empty, and this person can scan it.

client.listenLabel.again.usage: The button in an audiobook's dialog that starts it playing, for a book already heard to the end.

client.listenLabel.carryOn.usage: The button in an audiobook's dialog that starts it playing, for a book somebody is part way through.

client.listenLabel.listen.usage: The button in an audiobook's dialog that starts it playing, for a book not started yet.

client.listeningChoices.endOfChapter.usage: In the audiobook player's sleep timer list: stop playing when the chapter playing now ends.

client.listeningChoices.minutes.one.usage: In the audiobook player's sleep timer list: stop playing after this many minutes, when that is one.

client.listeningChoices.minutes.other.usage: In the audiobook player's sleep timer list: stop playing after this many minutes.

client.listeningChoices.off.usage: In the audiobook player's sleep timer list: no sleep timer.

client.logRanges.everything.usage: In the menu of how far back the log and job history reach: everything the server still keeps.

client.logRanges.last15Minutes.usage: In the menu of how far back the log and job history reach: only records from this recent stretch of time.

client.logRanges.last24Hours.usage: In the menu of how far back the log and job history reach: only records from this recent stretch of time.

client.logRanges.last6Hours.usage: In the menu of how far back the log and job history reach: only records from this recent stretch of time.

client.logRanges.last7Days.usage: In the menu of how far back the log and job history reach: only records from this recent stretch of time.

client.logRanges.lastHour.usage: In the menu of how far back the log and job history reach: only records from this recent stretch of time.

client.logsAsText.heading.usage: The first line of a log copied or downloaded from the Logs view, naming what the file is.

client.logsAsText.warning.value:
These lines quote file paths, which disclose the layout of the library and the
titles on the disk. Read what you are about to send before sending it.
client.logsAsText.warning.usage: At the top of a log copied or downloaded from the Logs view, warning that it names files before somebody sends it on. The line break is where the text wraps in the file.

client.nameSeason.numbered.usage: The name of a season of a programme, in its list of seasons: {number} is which season, such as 2.

client.nameSeason.other.usage: The name of a season of a programme, in its list of seasons: episodes nobody could place in a season.

client.nameSeason.specials.usage: The name of a season of a programme, in its list of seasons: the extra episodes outside the numbered seasons.

client.nameTheStanding.arriving.usage: A badge on a title in search results, saying where it stands: it has downloaded and is on its way into the library.

client.nameTheStanding.awaitingApproval.usage: A badge on a title in search results, saying where it stands: it was requested and nobody has approved it yet.

client.nameTheStanding.downloading.usage: A badge on a title in search results, saying where it stands: it is downloading now.

client.nameTheStanding.inLibrary.usage: A badge on a title in search results, saying where it stands: it is already in the library.

client.nameTheStanding.refused.usage: A badge on a title in search results, saying where it stands: the request for it was turned down.

client.nameTheStanding.requested.usage: A badge on a title in search results, saying where it stands: somebody has asked for it.

client.nameTheStanding.stuck.usage: A badge on a title in search results, saying where it stands: fetching it failed.

client.readRefusal.couldNotBeDone.value: That could not be done. Try again in a moment.
client.readRefusal.couldNotBeDone.usage: An error shown when the server refused a change, such as approving a request, without saying why.

client.readServerAddress.empty.value: Enter the address of your Valence server.
client.readServerAddress.empty.usage: An error under the field for the address of the Valence server to connect to: nothing was typed.

client.readServerAddress.notAnAddress.value: That does not look like a web address.
client.readServerAddress.notAnAddress.usage: An error under the field for the address of the Valence server to connect to: what was typed cannot be read as an address.

client.readServerAddress.scheme.value: A Valence server is reached over http or https.
client.readServerAddress.scheme.usage: An error under the field for the address of the Valence server to connect to: the address starts with something other than http:// or https://.

client.releaseTypeNames.album.several.usage: The name of a kind of music release, for several of them, such as a heading over a group of releases or a choice of which kinds to request: Albums.

client.releaseTypeNames.album.single.usage: The name of a kind of music release, for one of them, such as beside a single match: one album.

client.releaseTypeNames.compilation.seve.usage: The name of a kind of music release, for several of them, such as a heading over a group of releases or a choice of which kinds to request: Compilations.

client.releaseTypeNames.compilation.sing.usage: The name of a kind of music release, for one of them, such as beside a single match: one compilation.

client.releaseTypeNames.ep.several.usage: The name of a kind of music release, for several of them, such as a heading over a group of releases or a choice of which kinds to request: EPs.

client.releaseTypeNames.ep.single.usage: The name of a kind of music release, for one of them, such as beside a single match: one EP.

client.releaseTypeNames.live.several.usage: The name of a kind of music release, for several of them, such as a heading over a group of releases or a choice of which kinds to request: live recordings.

client.releaseTypeNames.live.single.usage: The name of a kind of music release, for one of them, such as beside a single match: a live recording.

client.releaseTypeNames.single.several.usage: The name of a kind of music release, for several of them, such as a heading over a group of releases or a choice of which kinds to request: Singles.

client.releaseTypeNames.single.single.usage: The name of a kind of music release, for one of them, such as beside a single match: one single.

client.saidOpened.times.one.usage: In a list of share links, how often one has been opened, when it has no limit and was opened once.

client.saidOpened.times.other.usage: In a list of share links, how often one has been opened, when it has no limit.

client.saidOpened.timesOf.one.usage: In a list of share links, how often one has been opened, against a limit of one opening. {opened} is how many times it was opened.

client.saidOpened.timesOf.other.usage: In a list of share links, how often one has been opened, against its limit. {opened} is how many times it was opened; {count} is the limit.

client.saidWhen.unknown.usage: In lists such as the devices signed in, in place of a date and time that could not be read. It fills the same place as a date such as "12 Oct 2026, 14:05".

client.seasonStandingNames.askable.usage: Beside a season in the list of seasons that can be requested: nobody has asked for it.

client.seasonStandingNames.library.usage: Beside a season in the list of seasons that can be requested: all of it is in the library.

client.seasonStandingNames.partly.usage: Beside a season in the list of seasons that can be requested: some of its episodes are in the library.

client.seasonStandingNames.requested.usage: Beside a season in the list of seasons that can be requested: somebody has asked for it.

client.serverProblem.answered.usage: An error shown when the server refused something without saying why. {status} is an HTTP status number such as 500.

client.serverProblem.unreachable.value: The server could not be reached.
client.serverProblem.unreachable.usage: An error shown when something asked of the server got no answer at all, such as saving a change on an admin page.

client.shareCaps.anybody.usage: In the dialog for sharing a link, a choice of how many people may open it: any number of people.

client.shareCaps.five.usage: In the dialog for sharing a link, a choice of how many people may open it: five people.

client.shareCaps.onePerson.usage: In the dialog for sharing a link, a choice of how many people may open it: one person.

client.shareCaps.two.usage: In the dialog for sharing a link, a choice of how many people may open it: two people.

client.shareLasts.day.usage: In the dialog for sharing a link, a choice of how long it keeps working: one day.

client.shareLasts.month.usage: In the dialog for sharing a link, a choice of how long it keeps working: one month.

client.shareLasts.threeDays.usage: In the dialog for sharing a link, a choice of how long it keeps working: three days.

client.shareLasts.untilWithdrawn.usage: In the dialog for sharing a link, a choice of how long it keeps working: until the person sharing it takes it back.

client.shareLasts.week.usage: In the dialog for sharing a link, a choice of how long it keeps working: one week.

client.shareStanding.live.usage: A badge in a list of share links, saying how one stands: it still works.

client.shareStanding.ranOut.usage: A badge in a list of share links, saying how one stands: its time is up.

client.shareStanding.usedUp.usage: A badge in a list of share links, saying how one stands: it has been opened as many times as it allowed.

client.shareStanding.withdrawn.usage: A badge in a list of share links, saying how one stands: somebody took it back.

client.signInAsProfile.wrongPassword.usage: An error after choosing a face to sign in as and typing its password or PIN, when it was wrong.

client.signingIn.unreachable.usage: An error while signing in, or adding a passkey, when the server did not answer. "Valence" is the product's name.

client.startPlaybackSession.refused.value: Valence asked for something the server would not accept ({status}).
client.startPlaybackSession.refused.usage: An error over the player when a film will not start: the server refused without saying why. {status} is an HTTP status number such as 400.

client.startPlaybackSession.unreachable.usage: An error over the player when a film will not start: the server did not answer.

client.startPlaybackSession.unreadable.value: The server sent a response Valence could not read.
client.startPlaybackSession.unreadable.usage: An error over the player when a film will not start: the server's answer made no sense to the app.

client.statusLook.attention.usage: A badge on something the server is working through, such as a request or a job: somebody needs to look at it.

client.statusLook.done.usage: A badge on something the server is working through, such as a request or a job: it is finished.

client.statusLook.failed.usage: A badge on something the server is working through, such as a request or a job: it failed.

client.statusLook.queued.usage: A badge on something the server is working through, such as a request or a job: it is waiting its turn.

client.statusLook.working.usage: A badge on something the server is working through, such as a request or a job: work on it is under way.

client.stillWatchingChoices.never.usage: In profile settings, the choice of never asking "Are you still watching?", beside choices of after 2, 3, 4 or 6 episodes in a row.

client.theVersionsOf.another.usage: In a title's detail dialog, in the choice of which version of it to play: another cut of it whose file does not say what it is.

client.theVersionsOf.original.usage: In a title's detail dialog, in the choice of which version of it to play: the title as it was released.

client.untilWhen.openedEnough.value: Until it has been opened enough times
client.untilWhen.openedEnough.usage: In a list of share links, what keeps a working one open: it works until it has been opened as many times as it allows.

client.untilWhen.runsOut.usage: In a list of share links, what keeps a working one open: it stops working at a set time. {when} is a date and time such as "12 Oct 2026, 14:05".

client.untilWhen.withdrawn.usage: In a list of share links, what keeps a working one open: it works until somebody takes it back.

client.useFetchWhatThisDeviceAsked.hereB.value: It is ready to watch offline.
client.useFetchWhatThisDeviceAsked.hereB.usage: A notification from the operating system when a download has finished: the line under its title.

client.useFetchWhatThisDeviceAsked.hereT.usage: A notification from the operating system when a download has finished: its title. {title} is the name of the film or episode.

client.useHomeRows.byName.usage: The title of a row far down the home page, drawn from one genre. {genre} is the genre's name, such as Comedy. This row holds the whole genre in alphabetical order.

client.useHomeRows.genreFromThe.usage: The title of a row far down the home page, drawn from one genre. {genre} is the genre's name, such as Comedy. This row holds the genre's films from one decade; {decade} is the year it starts, such as 1990.

client.useHomeRows.newIn.usage: The title of a row far down the home page, drawn from one genre. {genre} is the genre's name, such as Comedy. This row holds the newest of the genre.

client.useLibraryFilters.decade.usage: The heading of one group in the filter menu on a page of the library: filter by the decade something came out in.

client.useLibraryFilters.genre.usage: The heading of one group in the filter menu on a page of the library: filter by genre.

client.useLibraryFilters.rating.usage: The heading of one group in the filter menu on a page of the library: filter by the critics' rating.

client.useLibraryFilters.yourRating.usage: The heading of one group in the filter menu on a page of the library: filter by the stars this viewer gave.

client.useWatchParty.removed.value: {name} removed you from the watch party.
client.useWatchParty.removed.usage: A notice when whoever runs a watch party has removed this viewer from it. {name} is their name.

client.waysToDownloadAProgramme.choose.usage: In a programme's download menu, one way to download it: pick which episodes, in a list that opens next.

client.waysToDownloadAProgramme.episodes.usage: How many episodes a download choice in a programme's download menu holds, when that is one.
How many episodes a download choice in a programme's download menu holds.

client.waysToDownloadAProgramme.everyEpi.usage: In a programme's download menu, one way to download it: all of a programme that has one season. {episodes} is how many episodes, such as "8 episodes".

client.waysToDownloadAProgramme.everySea.usage: In a programme's download menu, one way to download it: every season of the programme. {episodes} is how many episodes, such as "24 episodes".

client.waysToDownloadAProgramme.theSeaso.usage: In a programme's download menu, one way to download it: the season on screen. {season} is its name, such as "Season 2"; {episodes} is how many episodes, such as "8 episodes".

client.whereItFalls.numbers.usage: On an episode's card, before its title: which season and episode it is. "S" is short for season and "E" for episode; {season} and {episode} are numbers, the episode sometimes a range such as 1–2.

common.cancel.usage: Closes a dialog or form without doing what it asked about.

common.close.usage: Closes a dialog or panel that has nothing to confirm.

common.delete.usage: Deletes something, or confirms deleting it in a dialog that has just asked.

common.episodesLeft.one.usage: On a programme's card: how many episodes this viewer has still to watch, when that is one.

common.episodesLeft.other.usage: On a programme's card: how many episodes this viewer has still to watch.

common.loading.usage: Read out by screen readers while something is being fetched.

common.nothingMatches.usage: Shown in place of results when a search finds nothing. {query} is what was typed.

common.save.usage: Saves the changes made in a form or dialog.

common.search.usage: Names the search tool, or the field somebody types a search into.

common.tryAgain.usage: Repeats something that failed, such as loading a page.

common.valence.usage: The product's name. Normally left untranslated.

core.compareToOriginal.eighth.value: about an eighth of the original
core.compareToOriginal.eighth.usage: Beside a download quality in the menu of qualities: says the copy would be an eighth of the original file.

core.compareToOriginal.fifth.value: about a fifth of the original
core.compareToOriginal.fifth.usage: Beside a download quality in the menu of qualities: says the copy would be a fifth of the original file.

core.compareToOriginal.half.value: about half the size of the original
core.compareToOriginal.half.usage: Beside a download quality in the menu of qualities: says the copy would be half the size of the original file.

core.compareToOriginal.ninth.value: about a ninth of the original
core.compareToOriginal.ninth.usage: Beside a download quality in the menu of qualities: says the copy would be a ninth of the original file.

core.compareToOriginal.quarter.value: about a quarter of the original
core.compareToOriginal.quarter.usage: Beside a download quality in the menu of qualities: says the copy would be a quarter of the original file.

core.compareToOriginal.sameSize.value: about the same size as the original
core.compareToOriginal.sameSize.usage: Beside a download quality in the menu of qualities: says the copy would be the same size of the original file.

core.compareToOriginal.seventh.value: about a seventh of the original
core.compareToOriginal.seventh.usage: Beside a download quality in the menu of qualities: says the copy would be a seventh of the original file.

core.compareToOriginal.sixth.value: about a sixth of the original
core.compareToOriginal.sixth.usage: Beside a download quality in the menu of qualities: says the copy would be a sixth of the original file.

core.compareToOriginal.smallFraction.value: a small fraction of the original — about a {times}th
core.compareToOriginal.smallFraction.usage: Beside a download quality in the menu of qualities, for a copy more than ten times smaller than the original file. {times} is how many times smaller, such as 15, read as "a fifteenth".

core.compareToOriginal.tenth.value: about a tenth of the original
core.compareToOriginal.tenth.usage: Beside a download quality in the menu of qualities: says the copy would be a tenth of the original file.

core.compareToOriginal.third.value: about a third of the original
core.compareToOriginal.third.usage: Beside a download quality in the menu of qualities: says the copy would be a third of the original file.

core.describeAirDate.aired.usage: Under an episode, on a programme's page and in the Coming up row on the home page: when an episode that has already been shown first aired. {date} is a date such as 2 Jan 2021.

core.describeAirDate.inDays.one.usage: Under an episode, on a programme's page and in the Coming up row on the home page: the episode is first shown in {count} day.

core.describeAirDate.inDays.other.usage: Under an episode, on a programme's page and in the Coming up row on the home page: the episode is first shown in {count} days, at most a fortnight away.

core.describeAirDate.on.usage: Under an episode, on a programme's page and in the Coming up row on the home page: the day an episode more than a fortnight away is first shown. {date} is a date such as 12 Oct 2026.

core.describeAirDate.today.usage: Under an episode, on a programme's page and in the Coming up row on the home page: the episode is first shown today.

core.describeAirDate.tomorrow.usage: Under an episode, on a programme's page and in the Coming up row on the home page: the episode is first shown tomorrow.

core.describeAudioTrack.numbered.usage: In the player's menu of sound tracks, the name of a track the file gives no language or title for. {position} is which track it is, counting from one.

core.describeChannels.mono.usage: In the player's menu of sound tracks, part of a track's name: the track has one channel.

core.describeChannels.quad.usage: In the player's menu of sound tracks, part of a track's name: the track has four channels, one in each corner.

core.describeChannels.stereo.usage: In the player's menu of sound tracks, part of a track's name: the track has two channels.

core.describeCodecTrade.av1.value: The smallest of the three, and the least widely played. A device that cannot decode it converts on every play — which trades disk once for processor for ever.
core.describeCodecTrade.av1.usage: In the dialog for re-encoding media, under each codec offered: what choosing the AV1 codec would mean. "The three" are the three codecs offered.

core.describeCodecTrade.h264.value: Played by everything, including a fifteen year old television. The largest of the three for the same picture.
core.describeCodecTrade.h264.usage: In the dialog for re-encoding media, under each codec offered: what choosing the H.264 codec would mean. "The three" are the three codecs offered.

core.describeCodecTrade.hevc.value: About half the size of H.264 for the same picture, and played by most things made since about 2016. Anything older converts it on every play.
core.describeCodecTrade.hevc.usage: In the dialog for re-encoding media, under each codec offered: what choosing the HEVC codec would mean.

core.describeGuest.aGuest.usage: In the list of who is watching, the name given to somebody watching on a share link when nobody knows whose link it is.

core.describeGuest.whose.usage: In the list of who is watching, the name given to somebody watching on a share link. {whose} is the possessive of the name of whoever made the link, such as "Dan’s".

core.describeKeeping.failed.value: That could not be fetched to this device.
core.describeKeeping.failed.usage: Under a download's title in the Downloads list: the file could not be copied to this device, when the server gave no reason.

core.describeKeeping.fetching.usage: Under a download's title in the Downloads list: the file is being copied to this device. {amount} is how far it has got, as a percentage such as 40% or as "1.2 GB so far".

core.describeKeeping.fetchingAt.usage: Under a download's title in the Downloads list: the file is being copied to this device. {amount} is how far it has got, as a percentage such as 40% or as "1.2 GB so far"; {speed} is how much arrives each second, such as 5 MB.

core.describeKeeping.here.usage: Under a download's title in the Downloads list: the file is on this device. {bytes} is its size, such as 1.2 GB.

core.describeKeeping.pausedAt.value: Paused at {amount}. What is here is kept.
core.describeKeeping.pausedAt.usage: Under a download's title in the Downloads list: copying the file was paused. {amount} is how far it got, as a percentage such as 40% or a size such as 1.2 GB.

core.describeKeeping.soFar.usage: Fills {amount} in "Fetching — {amount}." while the full size of a download is not known yet. {bytes} is how much has arrived, such as 1.2 GB.

core.describeQualityMeaning.original.value: Exactly what is on the server. The best it gets, and by far the largest.
core.describeQualityMeaning.original.usage: In the menu of download qualities, under the choice of the original file, unconverted: what it would look like.

core.describeQualityMeaning.p1080.value: About what a streaming service gives you. Looks great on a TV or a laptop.
core.describeQualityMeaning.p1080.usage: In the menu of download qualities, under the choice of a copy at 1080p: what it would look like.

core.describeQualityMeaning.p144.value: For when space is very tight.
core.describeQualityMeaning.p144.usage: In the menu of download qualities, under the choice of a copy at 144p: what it would look like.

core.describeQualityMeaning.p1440.value: Sharper than most streaming services. Only worth it on a big screen.
core.describeQualityMeaning.p1440.usage: In the menu of download qualities, under the choice of a copy at 1440p: what it would look like.

core.describeQualityMeaning.p2160.value: Every pixel the film has, on a screen large enough to show them.
core.describeQualityMeaning.p2160.usage: In the menu of download qualities, under the choice of a copy at 2160p: what it would look like.

core.describeQualityMeaning.p240.value: For when space is very tight.
core.describeQualityMeaning.p240.usage: In the menu of download qualities, under the choice of a copy at 240p: what it would look like.

core.describeQualityMeaning.p360.value: For when space is tight and you mostly want to follow along.
core.describeQualityMeaning.p360.usage: In the menu of download qualities, under the choice of a copy at 360p: what it would look like.

core.describeQualityMeaning.p480.value: Noticeably softer, still perfectly watchable. Good for a long flight.
core.describeQualityMeaning.p480.usage: In the menu of download qualities, under the choice of a copy at 480p: what it would look like.

core.describeQualityMeaning.p720.value: Hard to tell apart from 1080p on a phone or a tablet.
core.describeQualityMeaning.p720.usage: In the menu of download qualities, under the choice of a copy at 720p: what it would look like.

core.describeTimeToGo.days.one.usage: Beside a download that is still being prepared or fetched, in the Downloads list: roughly how long is left, when that is one day.

core.describeTimeToGo.days.other.usage: Beside a download that is still being prepared or fetched, in the Downloads list: roughly how long is left, in days.

core.describeTimeToGo.hours.usage: Beside a download that is still being prepared or fetched, in the Downloads list: roughly how long is left. {hours} is a number of hours; "h" is short for hours.

core.describeTimeToGo.hoursAndMinutes.usage: Beside a download that is still being prepared or fetched, in the Downloads list: roughly how long is left, such as "about 1 h 5 min left". "h" and "min" are short for hours and minutes.

core.describeTimeToGo.minutes.usage: Beside a download that is still being prepared or fetched, in the Downloads list: roughly how long is left. {minutes} is a number of minutes; "min" is short for minutes.

core.describeTimeToGo.underAMinute.usage: Beside a download that is still being prepared or fetched, in the Downloads list: less than a minute is left.

core.describeTranscodeReuse.fresh.value: No — this transcode is being made now
core.describeTranscodeReuse.fresh.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, and an administrator's statistics for a session, answering whether the converted stream was already made: none of it existed, and it is being converted now.

core.describeTranscodeReuse.none.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, and an administrator's statistics for a session, answering whether the converted stream was already made: the file is played as it is, so nothing is being converted. "n/a" means not applicable.

core.describeTranscodeReuse.partial.value: Partly — resumed where an earlier session stopped
core.describeTranscodeReuse.partial.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, and an administrator's statistics for a session, answering whether the converted stream was already made: part of it already existed and the conversion carries on from there.

core.describeTranscodeReuse.shared.value: Shared — another viewer’s transcode of exactly this
core.describeTranscodeReuse.shared.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, and an administrator's statistics for a session, answering whether the converted stream was already made: another viewer's conversion of the same thing is being shared.

core.describeTranscodeReuse.whole.value: Yes — the whole transcode was already made
core.describeTranscodeReuse.whole.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, and an administrator's statistics for a session, answering whether the converted stream was already made: the whole converted stream already existed.

core.negotiatePlayback.anamorphic.value: Source has {aspect} pixels and the client shows every picture square
core.negotiatePlayback.anamorphic.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the picture is handled: the file's pixels are not square, and this device cannot stretch them. {aspect} is a pixel shape such as 4/3.

core.negotiatePlayback.audioCodecUnsuppo.value: Client does not support the {codec} audio codec
core.negotiatePlayback.audioCodecUnsuppo.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the sound is handled: this device cannot decode it, so it is converted. {codec} is an audio codec such as truehd.

core.negotiatePlayback.audioPlays.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the sound is handled: this device plays it as it is. {codec} is an audio codec; {channels} is a number such as 6.

core.negotiatePlayback.audioProfileUnsup.value: Client does not decode the {profile} profile of {codec}
core.negotiatePlayback.audioProfileUnsup.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the sound is handled: this device cannot decode that variant of the codec. {profile} is a profile name such as HE-AAC; {codec} is an audio codec.

core.negotiatePlayback.bitDepthUnsupport.value: Client does not support {codec} at {bits} bits
core.negotiatePlayback.bitDepthUnsupport.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the picture is handled: this device cannot decode that codec at that colour depth. {codec} is a video codec; {bits} is a number such as 10.

core.negotiatePlayback.bitrateTooHigh.value: Source bitrate {kbps}kbps exceeds the client limit of {ceiling}kbps
core.negotiatePlayback.bitrateTooHigh.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the picture is handled: the file needs more bandwidth than this device allows. {kbps} and {ceiling} are numbers; "kbps" is kilobits per second.

core.negotiatePlayback.containerPairUnsu.value: Client does not play {codec} with this sound in the {container} container
core.negotiatePlayback.containerPairUnsu.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the file's container is handled: this device cannot play this picture and sound together in that file format. {codec} is a video codec such as hevc; {container} is a file format such as mkv.

core.negotiatePlayback.containerPlays.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the file's container is handled: this device plays it as it is. {container} is a file format name such as mkv or mp4. "Client" is the app or browser being watched on.

core.negotiatePlayback.containerUnsuppor.value: Client does not support the {container} container
core.negotiatePlayback.containerUnsuppor.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the file's container is handled: this device cannot play that file format, so it is repackaged. {container} is a file format name such as mkv.

core.negotiatePlayback.frameRateTooHigh.value: Source runs at {rate}fps and the client tops out at {ceiling}fps
core.negotiatePlayback.frameRateTooHigh.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the picture is handled: the file has more frames a second than this device shows. {rate} and {ceiling} are frame rates; "fps" is frames per second.

core.negotiatePlayback.interlaced.value: Source is interlaced and the client cannot deinterlace it
core.negotiatePlayback.interlaced.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the picture is handled: the file is interlaced, which this device cannot display.

core.negotiatePlayback.levelTooHigh.value: Client decodes {codec} to level {ceiling} and the source is level {level}
core.negotiatePlayback.levelTooHigh.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the picture is handled: the file needs a more capable decoder than this device has. {codec} is a video codec; {ceiling} and {level} are codec level numbers such as 51.

core.negotiatePlayback.noAudio.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the sound is handled: the file has no sound at all.

core.negotiatePlayback.noSubtitleAsked.value: No subtitle was asked for, and none is forced in the language being heard
core.negotiatePlayback.noSubtitleAsked.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how subtitles are handled: none is shown, because the viewer chose none and none must be shown for this language.

core.negotiatePlayback.noSubtitles.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how subtitles are handled: the file has none.

core.negotiatePlayback.notSegmentable.value: The source cannot be cut into segments a player can start at
core.negotiatePlayback.notSegmentable.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the picture is handled: the file has to be converted to be streamed in pieces.

core.negotiatePlayback.qualityCompresses.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the sound is handled: the viewer chose a lower quality, which compresses the sound. {kbps} is a number; "kbps" is kilobits per second.

core.negotiatePlayback.qualityLimitsBitr.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the picture is handled: the viewer chose a lower quality, which caps the bitrate. {kbps} is a number; "kbps" is kilobits per second.

core.negotiatePlayback.qualityLimitsReso.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the picture is handled: the viewer chose a lower quality, which caps the picture size. {width} and {height} are sizes in pixels.

core.negotiatePlayback.rangeUnsupported.value: Client does not support the {range} video range
core.negotiatePlayback.rangeUnsupported.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the picture is handled: this device cannot show that brightness range. {range} is a range such as HDR10 or DolbyVision.

core.negotiatePlayback.rotated.value: Source is rotated {degrees} degrees and the client cannot turn it back
core.negotiatePlayback.rotated.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the picture is handled: the video is stored turned, and this device cannot turn it upright. {degrees} is a number such as 90.

core.negotiatePlayback.sampleRateTooHigh.value: Track is {rate}Hz and the client tops out at {ceiling}Hz
core.negotiatePlayback.sampleRateTooHigh.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the sound is handled: the track has a higher sample rate than this device plays. {rate} and {ceiling} are numbers; "Hz" is hertz.

core.negotiatePlayback.subtitlesBurnedIn.value: {format} is image based and cannot be converted, so it must be burned in
core.negotiatePlayback.subtitlesBurnedIn.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how subtitles are handled: they are pictures, so they are drawn into the video. {format} is a subtitle format such as pgs.

core.negotiatePlayback.subtitlesRendered.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how subtitles are handled: this device draws them itself. {format} is a subtitle format such as subrip.

core.negotiatePlayback.subtitlesSidecar.value: Client does not render {format}, delivering as a WebVTT sidecar instead
core.negotiatePlayback.subtitlesSidecar.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how subtitles are handled: they are converted to WebVTT and sent beside the video. {format} is a subtitle format such as ass.

core.negotiatePlayback.tooManyReferenceF.value: Source keeps {frames} reference frames and the client manages {ceiling}
core.negotiatePlayback.tooManyReferenceF.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the picture is handled: the file keeps more reference frames than this device's decoder can. {frames} and {ceiling} are numbers.

core.negotiatePlayback.videoCodecUnsuppo.value: Client does not support the {codec} video codec
core.negotiatePlayback.videoCodecUnsuppo.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the picture is handled: this device cannot decode it, so it is converted. {codec} is a video codec such as hevc.

core.negotiatePlayback.videoPlays.value: Client direct plays {codec} at this bitrate, resolution and range
core.negotiatePlayback.videoPlays.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, the reason given for how the picture is handled: this device plays it as it is. {codec} is a video codec such as h264.

core.planReencodeSpec.noAudioEncoder.value: This server has no encoder for {codec} audio.
core.planReencodeSpec.noAudioEncoder.usage: Shown against a re-encode that cannot start, in the Encoding list. {codec} is an audio codec such as opus.

core.planReencodeSpec.noVideoEncoder.value: This server has no encoder for {codec} video.
core.planReencodeSpec.noVideoEncoder.usage: Shown against a re-encode that cannot start, in the Encoding list. {codec} is a video codec such as av1.

core.planToSessionSpec.cannotBurnImageSu.value: This server cannot burn in image subtitles, so they will not appear. Its FFmpeg build is missing the overlay filter.
core.planToSessionSpec.cannotBurnImageSu.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, beside "From the server": a warning about this stream. FFmpeg is a software name, and "overlay" is the name of one of its filters.

core.planToSessionSpec.cannotBurnTextSub.value: This server cannot burn in text subtitles, so they will not appear. Its FFmpeg build is missing the subtitles filter.
core.planToSessionSpec.cannotBurnTextSub.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, beside "From the server": a warning about this stream. FFmpeg is a software name, and "subtitles" is the name of one of its filters.

core.planToSessionSpec.cannotToneMap.value: This server cannot tone map {range} to SDR, so the stream keeps its original range instead of being converted. A client that colour manages will show it correctly; one that does not will show it washed out. Its FFmpeg build is missing the zscale or libplacebo filter.
core.planToSessionSpec.cannotToneMap.usage: In the player's Stats for nerds panel, beside "From the server": a warning about this stream. {range} is a brightness range such as HDR10. FFmpeg, zscale and libplacebo are software names.

core.planToSessionSpec.noEncoder.value: This server has no working encoder for {codec}.
core.planToSessionSpec.noEncoder.usage: Shown in the player when a film cannot start because the server cannot convert it. {codec} is a video codec such as h264.

desktop.aDiscordActivity.artistsAnd.usage: On Discord, the artists of a song, when there are several. {rest} is every name but the last, separated by commas; {last} is the last name.

desktop.aDiscordActivity.browsing.usage: On Discord, the activity status while somebody is in the desktop app but not playing anything.

desktop.aDiscordActivity.episode.usage: On Discord, which episode of a programme is playing. {season} and {episode} are numbers.

desktop.aDiscordActivity.paused.usage: On Discord, in the activity status, when what is playing is paused; also the tooltip on the small badge over a song’s cover.

desktop.aDiscordActivity.pausedWith.usage: On Discord, the line under what is playing when it is paused. {state} is the rest of that line, such as the episode or who else is watching.

desktop.aDiscordActivity.playing.usage: On Discord, the tooltip on the small badge over a song’s cover while it plays.

desktop.aDiscordActivity.viewOnTmdb.usage: Button on the Discord activity that opens the film or programme on The Movie Database website. TMDB is a name, normally left as is.

desktop.aDiscordActivity.withOthers.one.usage: On Discord, saying one other person is watching together in a watch party.

desktop.aDiscordActivity.withOthers.othe.usage: On Discord, saying how many other people are watching together in a watch party.

desktop.aHeldFile.notHeld.usage: Error body when the window asks for a downloaded file by an address that does not name one. Rarely seen.

desktop.aHeldFile.notHolding.value: This client is not holding that.
desktop.aHeldFile.notHolding.usage: Error body when the window asks for a downloaded file this computer does not have. Rarely seen.

desktop.describeThisDesktop.forDesktop.usage: How this computer is named in the list of devices signed in, when its operating system is not known.

desktop.describeThisDesktop.onSystem.usage: How this computer is named in the list of devices signed in. {os} is its operating system, such as macOS or Windows.

desktop.keepADownload.noFile.usage: Why a download to this computer failed: the server answered with nothing.

desktop.keepADownload.serverAnswered.usage: Why a download to this computer failed: the server answered with an error. {status} is the HTTP status number, such as 404.

desktop.keepADownload.shortFile.value: The server sent {bytes} of the {whole} bytes it said the file was.
desktop.keepADownload.shortFile.usage: Why a download to this computer failed: it stopped short. {bytes} is how many bytes arrived and {whole} how many there should have been.

desktop.serveTheApplication.hostUnreacha.usage: Error shown when the desktop app could not reach a web address it passes requests on to. {host} is that site’s name.

desktop.serveTheApplication.noServerChos.value: No Valence has been chosen yet.
desktop.serveTheApplication.noServerChos.usage: Error shown when something is asked of the server before the desktop app has been pointed at one.

desktop.serveTheApplication.pagesUnreada.value: This client's own pages could not be read from {served}.
desktop.serveTheApplication.pagesUnreada.usage: Error shown while the desktop app is being developed, when its own pages could not be fetched. {served} is where they were looked for.

desktop.serveTheApplication.serverUnreac.value: Valence could not be reached at {server}.
desktop.serveTheApplication.serverUnreac.usage: Error shown when the server stopped answering. {server} is its address.

desktop.serveTheApplication.stoppedWaiti.usage: Error given when a page gave up on a request before the server answered. Rarely seen.

desktop.theApplicationMenu.changeServer.usage: Menu item that lets somebody point the desktop app at a different server.

desktop.theApplicationMenu.file.usage: Name of the File menu in the desktop app’s menu bar.

desktop.theApplicationMenu.onTheWeb.usage: Item in the Help menu that opens the project’s web page.

desktop.theApplicationMenu.view.usage: Name of the View menu in the desktop app’s menu bar.

desktop.theHeldLibrary.couldNotFinish.value: This client could not finish keeping it.
desktop.theHeldLibrary.couldNotFinish.usage: Why a download to this computer failed, when nothing more is known.

desktop.theHeldLibrary.noServerChosen.value: No Valence has been chosen yet.
desktop.theHeldLibrary.noServerChosen.usage: Why a download to this computer failed: the desktop app has not been pointed at a server.

desktop.theWindowsOwnMenu.changeServer.usage: Item in the menu from right-clicking the desktop app’s window, which lets somebody point it at a different server.

phone.aBook.audiobookChapters.usage: Heading over the list of chapters to listen to, on the page of a book that has chapters to read as well.

phone.aBook.chapterCount.one.usage: Among the facts under a book's title: how many chapters it has, when that is one.

phone.aBook.chapterCount.other.usage: Among the facts under a book's title: how many chapters it has.

phone.aBook.chapterRead.usage: Beside one chapter in a book's list of chapters: this profile has finished reading it.

phone.aBook.chapters.usage: Heading over the list of a book's chapters on its page.

phone.aBook.continueReading.usage: Button on a book's page that opens it where this profile stopped reading.

phone.aBook.couldNotRead.value: That book could not be read.
phone.aBook.couldNotRead.usage: Error shown in place of a book's page when the book could not be fetched from the server.

phone.aBook.finished.usage: Under the buttons on a book's page: this profile has read the whole book.

phone.aBook.nothingInIt.value: Nothing in this book yet. Scanning the library again may find it.
phone.aBook.nothingInIt.usage: Shown on a book's page when it has nothing to read or hear yet.

phone.aBook.onPage.usage: Beside one chapter in a book's list of chapters: the page this profile has read up to. {page} is the page number.

phone.aBook.onPageOf.usage: Beside one chapter in a book's list of chapters: the page this profile has read up to. {page} is the page number, {count} how many pages the chapter has.

phone.aBook.pageCount.one.usage: Beside one chapter in a book's list of chapters: how many pages it has, when that is one.

phone.aBook.pageCount.other.usage: Beside one chapter in a book's list of chapters: how many pages it has.

phone.aBook.percentRead.usage: Beside one chapter in a book's list of chapters: how far into it this profile has read. {percent} is a whole number from 0 to 100.

phone.aBook.read.usage: Button on a book's page that opens it from the first page, when nobody has started it.

phone.aBook.readAgain.usage: Button on a book's page, once it has been finished, that opens it from the first page.

phone.aBook.readChapter.usage: Read out by screen readers for one chapter in a book's list of chapters; pressing it opens that chapter. {title} is the chapter's name.

phone.aBook.share.usage: Button on a book's page that opens a sheet for sharing the book with somebody.

phone.aCatalogueList.couldNotRead.usage: Error shown at the top of a full list of titles to ask for (opened with See all) when the list failed to load.

phone.aChapterToHear.listenFrom.usage: Read out by screen readers for one chapter in an audiobook's list of chapters; pressing it plays the book from there. {title} is the chapter's name.

phone.aChoiceOfEpisodes.download.one.usage: Button along the foot of the episode-picking sheet that downloads what was picked, when that is one episode.

phone.aChoiceOfEpisodes.download.other.usage: Button along the foot of the episode-picking sheet that downloads the episodes picked.

phone.aChoiceOfEpisodes.letGoOfSeason.usage: Read out by screen readers for a season's heading in the episode-picking sheet once all its episodes are picked; it un-picks them. {season} is the season's name, such as “Season 2”.

phone.aChoiceOfEpisodes.onThisPhone.usage: Under an episode in the episode-picking sheet that is already downloaded to this phone.

phone.aChoiceOfEpisodes.pickSeason.usage: Read out by screen readers for a season's heading in the episode-picking sheet, which picks all its episodes. {season} is the season's name, such as “Season 2”.

phone.aChoiceOfEpisodes.pickSome.usage: Button along the foot of the episode-picking sheet, disabled, before any episode has been picked.

phone.aChoiceOfEpisodes.title.usage: Heading of the sheet for picking which episodes of a programme to download.

phone.aComingTrack.more.usage: Read out by screen readers for the menu button beside a song in the queue. {title} is the song.

phone.aComingTrack.playNow.usage: Read out by screen readers for a song in the queue; pressing plays it straight away. {title} is the song.

phone.aDevicesSheet.noOthers.value: No other Valence is open on this profile. Open Valence on a computer, a television or another phone and it will be here.
phone.aDevicesSheet.noOthers.usage: Shown in the list of devices when no other device is open on this profile. Valence is the product's name.

phone.aDevicesSheet.notPlaying.usage: Under another device's name in the list of devices, when nothing is playing on it.

phone.aDevicesSheet.pausedOn.usage: Under another device's name in the list of devices, when it is paused. {title} is the song or title it is paused on.

phone.aDevicesSheet.playOn.usage: Read out by screen readers for a row in the list of devices; picking it moves the music there. {name} is the device's name.

phone.aDevicesSheet.playing.usage: Under another device's name in the list of devices, when it is playing something. {title} is the song or title playing.

phone.aDevicesSheet.thisIPhone.usage: Under the name of the phone in the list of devices, saying it is the one in the person's hand.

phone.aDevicesSheet.title.usage: Heading of a sheet listing the devices the music could play on.

phone.aFeature.moreInfo.usage: Button on the large featured title at the top of the Home tab that opens its page.

phone.aFeature.play.usage: Button on the large featured title at the top of the Home tab that plays it from the start.

phone.aFeature.resume.usage: Button on the large featured title at the top of the Home tab that plays it from where this profile stopped. {at} is how far in that was, such as 1h 12m.

phone.aFeature.series.usage: Among the facts on the large featured title at the top of the Home tab, in place of a running time: it is a television series.

phone.aHomeShelf.comingUp.usage: Heading of the row on the Home tab of episodes about to be shown on television.

phone.aHomeShelf.episodeAirs.usage: Under a programme in the Coming up row: which episode is next and when it airs. S is short for season and E for episode. {season} and {episode} are numbers, {when} a day such as Tomorrow.

phone.aMissingEpisode.episode.usage: Name shown for an episode missing from the library whose title is not known. {number} is its number in the season.

phone.aMissingEpisode.notHere.usage: Under an episode in a programme's list that the library does not have.

phone.aMissingEpisode.notHereAirs.usage: Under an episode in a programme's list that the library does not have. {when} is when it aired or airs, such as “12 March 2024”.

phone.aMusicHead.play.usage: Button at the top of an album, artist or playlist page that plays it from the start.

phone.aMusicHead.shuffle.usage: Button at the top of an album, artist or playlist page that plays its songs in a random order.

phone.aPageReader.chapters.usage: Heading over the list of chapters in the reader's contents and settings panel.

phone.aPageReader.coverAlone.usage: Switch in the reader's settings panel, when two pages are shown at once, that shows the cover by itself; also read out by screen readers for the switch.

phone.aPageReader.coverAloneDetail.value: Pairs the pages after it as the printed book does.
phone.aPageReader.coverAloneDetail.usage: Explains the Cover on its own switch: the pages after the cover are paired as in the printed book.

phone.aPageReader.goToAPage.usage: Read out by screen readers for the slider along the bottom of the reader that moves to any page of the chapter.

phone.aPageReader.howMany.usage: Read out by screen readers for the row of choices of one or two pages at a time.

phone.aPageReader.leftToRight.usage: Choice in the reader's settings panel for a book of page images, such as a comic: the pages turn from left to right.

phone.aPageReader.next.usage: Shown after the last page of a chapter, naming the chapter that follows. {title} is that chapter's name.

phone.aPageReader.noPages.value: This chapter has no pages to show.
phone.aPageReader.noPages.usage: Shown in the reader in place of a chapter of page images that has no pages.

phone.aPageReader.onePage.usage: Choice in the reader's settings panel for a book of page images: show one page at a time.

phone.aPageReader.onePageHere.usage: Read out by screen readers for the page shown in the reader; tapping it turns the page or shows the controls. {page} is its number.

phone.aPageReader.pageOf.usage: Along the bottom of the reader: the page shown. {page} is its number, {count} how many pages the chapter has.

phone.aPageReader.pagesAtOnce.usage: Heading in the reader's settings panel over the choice of one or two pages at a time.

phone.aPageReader.pagesOf.usage: Along the bottom of the reader when two pages are shown side by side. {first} and {last} are the page numbers shown, {count} how many pages the chapter has.

phone.aPageReader.pagesTurn.usage: Heading in the reader's settings panel over the choice of which way the pages turn.

phone.aPageReader.readOn.usage: Button after the last page of a chapter that opens the next chapter.

phone.aPageReader.rightToLeft.usage: Choice in the reader's settings panel for a book of page images: the pages turn from right to left, as manga do.

phone.aPageReader.twoPages.usage: Choice in the reader's settings panel for a book of page images: show two pages side by side.

phone.aPageReader.twoPagesHere.usage: Read out by screen readers for two pages shown side by side in the reader; tapping them turns the page or shows the controls. {first} and {second} are the page numbers.

phone.aPageReader.twoPagesTurns.value: Two pages at once turns the phone on its side.
phone.aPageReader.twoPagesTurns.usage: Explains, under the choice of how many pages at once, that showing two pages turns the screen to landscape.

phone.aPageReader.whichWay.usage: Read out by screen readers for the row of choices of which way the reader's pages turn.

phone.aPerson.born.usage: On a person's page: the date they were born. {when} is the date, already written out.

phone.aPerson.episodes.usage: Heading of the row of single TV episodes a person appears in, on that person's page.

phone.aPerson.films.usage: Heading of the row of films a person appears in, on that person's page.

phone.aPerson.more.usage: Button under a shortened biography on a person's page that shows the whole of it.
