screens.artistsView.noneFollowedTitle.usage: Heading shown on the artists page, when showing followed artists, if this person follows none.

screens.artistsView.reading.usage: Read out by screen readers while the artists page is loading.

screens.artistsView.whichLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the row of choices between every artist and followed artists.

screens.askableDialog.cancelDetail.value: It will not be fetched, and whatever it had started downloading is deleted. You can request it again whenever you like.
screens.askableDialog.cancelDetail.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Explanation in the dialog asking whether to withdraw a request.

screens.askableDialog.cancelRequest.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Button that withdraws the viewer's own request, and the confirm button of the dialog that asks whether to.

screens.askableDialog.cancelTitle.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Heading of the dialog asking whether to withdraw a request. {title} is what was requested.

screens.askableDialog.cancelUnnamedTitle.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Heading of the dialog asking whether to withdraw a request, when the title's name is not known.

screens.askableDialog.cast.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Read out by screen readers as the name of the section listing the cast.

screens.askableDialog.chooseQualityUnnam.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Stands in for the title's name in the quality chooser when the name is not known, as in “Request this”.

screens.askableDialog.couldNotReadWhat.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Names what could not be loaded, in a message saying it could not be read.

screens.askableDialog.couldNotRequest.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Error shown when the request was refused and the server gave no reason.

screens.askableDialog.coverOf.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Read out by screen readers for the artwork of an artist or album. {title} is its name.

screens.askableDialog.howMuchArrived.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Read out by screen readers for the progress bar of a download. {title} is what is downloading.

screens.askableDialog.noYear.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Shown under an album in an artist's list when its release year is unknown.

screens.askableDialog.playSample.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Read out by screen readers for the button that plays a short preview of an album. {album} is the album's name.

screens.askableDialog.reading.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Read out by screen readers while the title's details are loading.

screens.askableDialog.request.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Main button that requests the film, series or album.

screens.askableDialog.requestAlbum.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Button beside one album in an artist's list that requests just that album.

screens.askableDialog.requested.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Badge beside an album in an artist's list once it has been requested.

screens.askableDialog.stopSample.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Read out by screen readers for the button that stops a short preview of an album. {album} is the album's name.

screens.askableDialog.trailerOf.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Read out by screen readers as the name of the trailer player. {title} is the film or series.

screens.askableDialog.trailerUnnamed.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Read out by screen readers as the name of the trailer player when the title's name is not known.

screens.askableDialog.unnamedLabel.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Read out by screen readers as the dialog's name while the title is still loading.

screens.askableDialog.watchArtist.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Main button for an artist: requests their releases and keeps fetching new ones.

screens.askableDialog.watchTrailer.usage: In the dialog for a film, series, artist or album that can be requested. Button that plays the title's trailer.

screens.askableMusicTile.coverOf.usage: Read out by screen readers for the artwork of an album or artist that can be asked for. {title} is the album's or artist's name.

screens.askableResults.artistsNotInLibra.value: Artists not in your library yet
screens.askableResults.artistsNotInLibra.usage: Title of the row under the search results of artists that match but can only be asked for.

screens.askableResults.notInLibrary.usage: Title of the row under the search results of films and series that match but can only be asked for.

screens.audiobookBar.backSeconds.one.usage: Button in the audiobook player that jumps back in the book, read out by screen readers and shown as a tooltip. {count} is how many seconds, when that is one.

screens.audiobookBar.backSeconds.other.usage: Button in the audiobook player that jumps back in the book, read out by screen readers and shown as a tooltip. {count} is how many seconds.

screens.audiobookBar.forwardSeconds.one.usage: Button in the audiobook player that jumps forward in the book, read out by screen readers and shown as a tooltip. {count} is how many seconds, when that is one.

screens.audiobookBar.forwardSeconds.othe.usage: Button in the audiobook player that jumps forward in the book, read out by screen readers and shown as a tooltip. {count} is how many seconds.

screens.audiobookBar.listeningTo.usage: Read out by screen readers: names the small player in the corner of the page that shows the audiobook playing.

screens.audiobookBar.openPlayer.usage: Button in the small audiobook player that opens its panel with chapters, speed and sleep timer.

screens.audiobookBar.pause.usage: Button in the audiobook player that pauses the book playing.

screens.audiobookBar.play.usage: Button in the audiobook player that carries on playing the book.

screens.audiobookBar.stopListening.usage: Button in the small audiobook player that stops the book and closes the player.

screens.audiobookPanel.atEndOfChapter.value: At the end of this chapter
screens.audiobookPanel.atEndOfChapter.usage: Choice in the sleep timer menu of the audiobook panel: stop the book when this chapter ends.

screens.audiobookPanel.chapters.usage: Read out by screen readers: names the list of the audiobook's chapters in the audiobook panel.

screens.audiobookPanel.endOfChapter.usage: On the sleep timer menu button in the audiobook panel, while the book is set to stop at the end of this chapter.

screens.audiobookPanel.inMinutes.one.usage: Choice in the sleep timer menu of the audiobook panel: stop the book after this long. {count} is the minutes, when that is one.

screens.audiobookPanel.inMinutes.other.usage: Choice in the sleep timer menu of the audiobook panel: stop the book after this long. {count} is the minutes.

screens.audiobookPanel.nextChapter.usage: Button in the audiobook panel that goes to the next chapter.

screens.audiobookPanel.previousChapter.usage: Button in the audiobook panel that goes to the chapter before.

screens.audiobookPanel.sleep.usage: On the sleep timer menu button in the audiobook panel, while no timer is set.

screens.audiobookPanel.sleepMinutes.one.usage: On the sleep timer menu button in the audiobook panel, short for how many minutes until the book stops. {count} is the minutes, when that is one.

screens.audiobookPanel.sleepMinutes.othe.usage: On the sleep timer menu button in the audiobook panel, short for how many minutes until the book stops. {count} is the minutes.

screens.audiobookPanel.sleepOff.usage: Choice in the sleep timer menu of the audiobook panel that sets no timer.

screens.audiobookPanel.sleepTimer.usage: Names the menu in the audiobook panel for choosing when the book stops playing by itself, and heads its list.

screens.audiobookPanel.speed.usage: Names the menu in the audiobook panel for choosing how fast the book plays, and heads its list.

screens.audiobookPanel.whereTheBookIs.usage: Read out by screen readers: names the slider showing how far through the whole audiobook it is, which can be dragged to move.

screens.bookDialog.aBook.usage: Read out by screen readers as the name of a book's dialog while the book is still loading.

screens.bookDialog.about.usage: Heading in a book's dialog over what the book is about.

screens.bookDialog.audiobook.usage: Small line above a book's title in its dialog, saying it is an audiobook.

screens.bookDialog.chapterCount.one.usage: Small line above a comic's title in its dialog, saying it has a single chapter.

screens.bookDialog.chapterCount.other.usage: Small line above a comic's title in its dialog, saying how many chapters it has. {count} is the number.

screens.bookDialog.chapters.usage: Heading in a book's dialog over the list of its chapters.

screens.bookDialog.continueReading.usage: Main button in a book's dialog, when it has been started: opens it where the reader left off.

screens.bookDialog.ebook.usage: Small line above a book's title in its dialog, saying it is an ebook.

screens.bookDialog.ebookAndAudiobook.usage: Small line above a book's title in its dialog, saying it can be both read and listened to.

screens.bookDialog.finished.usage: Beside the progress bar in a book's dialog, once the book has been read to the end.

screens.bookDialog.howFarThrough.usage: Read out by screen readers: names the bar in a book's dialog showing how much of it has been read.

screens.bookDialog.keep.usage: Button in a book's dialog that adds the book to this profile's kept books.

screens.bookDialog.moreToDo.value: More to do with this book
screens.bookDialog.moreToDo.usage: Read out by screen readers: names the bar of buttons along the bottom of a book's dialog.

screens.bookDialog.noOverview.value: Nothing is written about this book yet.
screens.bookDialog.noOverview.usage: Shown under About in a book's dialog when the book has no description.

screens.bookDialog.read.usage: Main button in a book's dialog, when it has not been started: opens it in the reader.

screens.bookDialog.readAgain.usage: Main button in a book's dialog, when it has been read to the end: opens it from the start.

screens.bookDialog.share.usage: Button in a book's dialog that makes a link to hand the book to somebody else.

screens.bookDialog.stopKeeping.usage: Button in a book's dialog that takes the book out of this profile's kept books.

screens.bookDialog.thatBook.usage: Names what failed to load in a message such as “That book could not be read”, shown in a book's dialog.

screens.bookRail.thatShelf.usage: Names what failed to load in a message such as “That shelf could not be read”, shown on the Books page in place of a library's row of books.

screens.bookRow.audiobook.usage: Under a book on a shelf of books, when it is an audiobook and nobody is named as its author.

screens.bookRow.chapterCount.one.usage: Under a comic on a shelf of books: how many chapters it has, when that is one.

screens.bookRow.chapterCount.other.usage: Under a comic on a shelf of books: how many chapters it has. {count} is the number.

screens.bookRow.ebook.usage: Under a book on a shelf of books, when it is an ebook and nobody is named as its author.

screens.bookRow.seriesBooks.one.usage: Under a series on a shelf of books, where the series is gathered into one card: how many books it holds, when that is one.

screens.bookRow.seriesBooks.other.usage: Under a series on a shelf of books, where the series is gathered into one card: how many books it holds.

screens.bookRow.seriesPosition.usage: Above a book on a shelf showing one series in order: its place in the series. {position} is the number.

screens.bookShelf.addLibrary.usage: Button on the Books page, shown to an administrator when there are no book libraries, that opens the libraries settings.

screens.bookShelf.noLibrariesAddOne.usage: On the Books page under “No book libraries yet”, for an administrator.

screens.bookShelf.noLibrariesAskAdmin.value: Ask the server admin to add one.
screens.bookShelf.noLibrariesAskAdmin.usage: On the Books page under “No book libraries yet”, for somebody who may not add libraries.

screens.bookShelf.noLibrariesTitle.usage: Heading on the Books page when the server has no libraries of books.

screens.bookShelf.nothingToReadAskAdmin.value: Ask the server admin to scan it.
screens.bookShelf.nothingToReadAskAdmin.usage: On the Books page under “Nothing to read yet”, for somebody who may not scan libraries. “It” is the library.

screens.bookShelf.nothingToReadScan.value: Scan it, or add files to its folder.
screens.bookShelf.nothingToReadScan.usage: On the Books page under “Nothing to read yet”, for an administrator. “It” is the library.

screens.bookShelf.nothingToReadTitle.usage: Heading on the Books page when the book libraries exist but hold no books.

screens.bookShelf.scanIt.usage: Button on the Books page, shown to an administrator when the book libraries are empty, that opens the libraries settings to scan them.

screens.booksDiscover.noneFoundDetail.value: Try the title, or the author, another way.
screens.booksDiscover.noneFoundDetail.usage: Shown under “No books found” when a book search finds nothing.

screens.booksDiscover.noneFoundTitle.usage: Heading shown in place of results when a book search finds nothing.

screens.booksDiscover.nothingDetail.value: Open Library could not be reached, or has nothing to suggest just now. You can still search for a book.
screens.booksDiscover.nothingDetail.usage: Shown under “No books to ask for”. Open Library is the name of an online book catalogue; normally left untranslated.

screens.booksDiscover.nothingTitle.usage: Heading on the Books tab of the Requests page when there are no suggestions.

screens.booksDiscover.reading.value: Reading what books there are to ask for
screens.booksDiscover.reading.usage: Read out by screen readers while the suggested books are being fetched.

screens.booksDiscover.searchLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the search field on the Books tab of the Requests page.

screens.booksDiscover.searchPlaceholder.value: Search for a book or an author
screens.booksDiscover.searchPlaceholder.usage: Placeholder text in the search field on the Books tab of the Requests page.

screens.booksDiscover.searching.usage: Read out by screen readers while a book search is running.

screens.booksDiscover.theBooks.usage: Fills the gap in the sentence “{what} could not be read…”, shown when searching for books failed. Starts the sentence.

screens.booksDiscover.whatBooks.value: What books there are to ask for
screens.booksDiscover.whatBooks.usage: Fills the gap in the sentence “{what} could not be read…”, shown when the suggested books could not be fetched. Starts the sentence.

screens.booksPage.heading.usage: Heading of the Books page, read out by screen readers.

screens.browseArea.addLibrary.usage: Button under “No libraries yet” on a browse page, shown to administrators, that opens the form for adding a library.

screens.browseArea.books.usage: Heading of the row of kept books on the Favourites page.

screens.browseArea.everything.usage: In the order menu at the top of the Films and Shows pages. Choice that shows every title, watched or not.

screens.browseArea.favourites.empty.usage: Heading shown in place of the grid when there are no titles the viewer has favourited yet.

screens.browseArea.favourites.filter.usage: Read out by screen readers for the button that opens the filter menu on the page listing titles the viewer has favourited.

screens.browseArea.favourites.order.usage: Read out by screen readers for the menu that changes the order of the page listing titles the viewer has favourited.

screens.browseArea.favourites.reading.usage: Read out by screen readers while the page listing titles the viewer has favourited loads.

screens.browseArea.favourites.title.usage: Name of the page listing titles the viewer has favourited: its hidden heading for screen readers, and the name of what could not be loaded if it fails.

screens.browseArea.films.empty.usage: Heading shown in place of the grid when there are no films yet.

screens.browseArea.films.filter.usage: Read out by screen readers for the button that opens the filter menu on the page listing films.

screens.browseArea.films.order.usage: Read out by screen readers for the menu that changes the order of the page listing films.

screens.browseArea.films.reading.usage: Read out by screen readers while the page listing films loads.

screens.browseArea.films.title.usage: Name of the page listing films: its hidden heading for screen readers, and the name of what could not be loaded if it fails.

screens.browseArea.new.empty.usage: Heading shown in place of the grid when there are no newly added and popular titles yet.

screens.browseArea.new.filter.usage: Read out by screen readers for the button that opens the filter menu on the page listing newly added and popular titles.

screens.browseArea.new.order.usage: Read out by screen readers for the menu that changes the order of the page listing newly added and popular titles.

screens.browseArea.new.reading.usage: Read out by screen readers while the page listing newly added and popular titles loads.

screens.browseArea.new.title.usage: Name of the page listing newly added and popular titles: its hidden heading for screen readers, and the name of what could not be loaded if it fails.

screens.browseArea.noLibraries.usage: Heading shown on a browse page when the server has no libraries at all.

screens.browseArea.onlyUnwatched.value: Only what you have not watched
screens.browseArea.onlyUnwatched.usage: In the order menu at the top of the Films and Shows pages. Choice that hides titles the viewer has already watched.

screens.browseArea.order.added.usage: In the order menu at the top of the Films and Shows pages. Choice that puts the newest additions to the library first; also shown on the menu's button when chosen.

screens.browseArea.order.rating.usage: In the order menu at the top of the Films and Shows pages. Choice that orders by rating, best first; also shown on the menu's button when chosen.

screens.browseArea.order.released.usage: In the order menu at the top of the Films and Shows pages. Choice that orders by when each was released; also shown on the menu's button when chosen.

screens.browseArea.order.size.usage: In the order menu at the top of the Films and Shows pages. Choice that orders by file size; also shown on the menu's button when chosen.

screens.browseArea.order.title.usage: In the order menu at the top of the Films and Shows pages. Choice that orders alphabetically by title; also shown on the menu's button when chosen.

screens.browseArea.orderGroup.usage: In the order menu at the top of the Films and Shows pages. Heading of the group of ways to order the page.

screens.browseArea.scanIt.usage: Button on an empty browse page, shown to administrators, that scans the library for new files.

screens.browseArea.showGroup.usage: In the order menu at the top of the Films and Shows pages. Heading of the group choosing whether to show everything or only what is unwatched. “Show” is a verb here.

screens.browseArea.shows.empty.usage: Heading shown in place of the grid when there are no TV programmes yet.

screens.browseArea.shows.filter.usage: Read out by screen readers for the button that opens the filter menu on the page listing TV programmes.

screens.browseArea.shows.order.usage: Read out by screen readers for the menu that changes the order of the page listing TV programmes.

screens.browseArea.shows.reading.usage: Read out by screen readers while the page listing TV programmes loads.

screens.browseArea.shows.title.usage: Name of the page listing TV programmes: its hidden heading for screen readers, and the name of what could not be loaded if it fails.

screens.captionSettings.backgroundColour.usage: Label over the row of colours for the box behind the captions.

screens.captionSettings.edge.usage: Label over the row of choices for the outline or shadow around caption letters.

screens.captionSettings.edgeNone.usage: Choice of caption edge in the player's caption settings: no outline or shadow around the letters.

screens.captionSettings.edgeOutline.usage: Choice of caption edge in the player's caption settings: a thin outline around the letters.

screens.captionSettings.edgeRaised.usage: Choice of caption edge in the player's caption settings: letters that look raised off the picture.

screens.captionSettings.edgeShadow.usage: Choice of caption edge in the player's caption settings: a shadow below the letters.

screens.captionSettings.font.usage: Label over the row of caption font choices.

screens.captionSettings.fontCasual.usage: Choice of caption font in the player's caption settings: an informal, handwriting-like font.

screens.captionSettings.fontMono.usage: Choice of caption font in the player's caption settings: a font whose letters are all the same width.

screens.captionSettings.fontSans.usage: Choice of caption font in the player's caption settings: a plain font without serifs.

screens.captionSettings.fontSerif.usage: Choice of caption font in the player's caption settings: a font with serifs.

screens.captionSettings.heading.usage: Name of the caption settings panel in the player, read out by screen readers.

screens.captionSettings.opacity.usage: Name of the caption background opacity slider, read out by screen readers.

screens.captionSettings.opacityValue.usage: Label over the slider for how see-through the box behind the captions is, with its value now. {opacity} is a percentage from 0 to 100.

screens.captionSettings.preview.usage: Read out by screen readers on the sample caption that shows how the chosen style looks.

screens.captionSettings.previewText.usage: Sample caption text in the caption settings, drawn in the chosen style. Any short, ordinary phrase in the language will do.

screens.captionSettings.reset.usage: Button in the caption settings that puts every caption choice back as it was to begin with.

screens.captionSettings.size.usage: Name of the caption size slider, read out by screen readers.

screens.captionSettings.sizeValue.usage: Label over the caption size slider, with the size chosen now. {size} is a percentage of the normal size, such as 100.

screens.captionSettings.textColour.usage: Label over the row of colours for the caption letters.

screens.castGrid.about.usage: Read out by screen readers for a performer's card in the Cast row, which opens their page. {name} is the performer.

screens.castGrid.heading.usage: Heading of the row of performers in a title's detail dialog.

screens.catalogueBrowser.filterFilms.usage: Button opening the filters for the list of films that can be asked for.

screens.catalogueBrowser.filterSeries.usage: Button opening the filters for the list of TV series that can be asked for.

screens.catalogueGrid.catalogueEmpty.usage: Shown under “Nothing to ask for here” when no filters are set.

screens.catalogueGrid.gridLabel.value: What there is to ask for
screens.catalogueGrid.gridLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the grid of films or series that can be asked for.

screens.catalogueGrid.noneMatch.value: Nothing in the catalogue matches those filters.
screens.catalogueGrid.noneMatch.usage: Shown under “Nothing to ask for here” when filters are set.

screens.catalogueGrid.nothingTitle.usage: Heading shown in place of a list of films or series to ask for when it is empty.

screens.catalogueGrid.reading.value: Reading what there is to ask for
screens.catalogueGrid.reading.usage: Read out by screen readers while a list of films or series to ask for is being fetched.

screens.catalogueGrid.readingMore.usage: Read out by screen readers while the next page of the list is fetched, at its bottom.

screens.catalogueGrid.whatThereIs.value: What there is to ask for
screens.catalogueGrid.whatThereIs.usage: Fills the gap in the sentence “{what} could not be read…”, shown when a list of films or series to ask for could not be fetched. Starts the sentence.

screens.chapterList.chapters.usage: Read out by screen readers: names the list of a book's chapters in its dialog.

screens.chapterList.howFarThrough.usage: Read out by screen readers: names the bar showing how much of a chapter has been read. {title} is the chapter's name.

screens.chapterList.isRead.usage: Read out by screen readers for the tick beside a chapter that has been read to the end.

screens.chapterList.pageCount.one.usage: Under a chapter in a book's chapter list: how many pages it has, when that is one.

screens.chapterList.pageCount.other.usage: Under a chapter in a book's chapter list: how many pages it has. {count} is the number.

screens.chapterList.percentRead.usage: Beside a chapter in a book's chapter list: how much of it has been read. {percent} is a whole number from 1 to 99.

screens.chapterList.readChapter.usage: Read out by screen readers for a chapter in a book's chapter list: opens that chapter. {title} is the chapter's name.

screens.chapterList.reflows.usage: Under a chapter in a book's chapter list, instead of a page count, when its text reflows to fit the screen.

screens.chooseEpisodes.dialogLabel.usage: What screen readers call the dialog for picking which of a show's episodes to keep on this device. {title} is the show's title.

screens.chooseEpisodes.download.one.usage: The confirm button of the dialog for picking episodes to keep, when one is picked.

screens.chooseEpisodes.download.other.usage: The confirm button of the dialog for picking episodes to keep: how many will be downloaded.

screens.chooseEpisodes.onThisDevice.usage: Under an episode in the dialog for picking episodes to keep, when it is already kept on this device.

screens.chooseEpisodes.pickSome.usage: The confirm button of the dialog for picking episodes to keep, while none are picked.

screens.chooseEpisodes.title.usage: Title of the dialog for picking which of a show's episodes to keep on this device.

screens.chooseQualityDialog.detail.value: We’ll fetch the best release that fits.
screens.chooseQualityDialog.detail.usage: In the dialog that asks which quality to request a title at, opened from a title's Request button when the server offers several. Text under the heading, before the list of qualities.

screens.chooseQualityDialog.heading.usage: In the dialog that asks which quality to request a title at, opened from a title's Request button when the server offers several. Heading. {title} is what is being requested.

screens.chooseQualityDialog.label.usage: In the dialog that asks which quality to request a title at, opened from a title's Request button when the server offers several. Read out by screen readers as the dialog's name. {title} is what is being requested.

screens.comingUp.heading.usage: Heading of the row on the home page showing the next episodes due to air of programmes the viewer follows.

screens.comingUp.subtitle.usage: Under a programme's poster in the Coming up row on the home page. {season} and {episode} are numbers (S and E abbreviate season and episode); {when} says when it airs, such as “Tomorrow”.

screens.confirmHiding.confirm.usage: Confirm button of the dialog asking whether to hide a title from the viewer.

screens.confirmHiding.title.usage: Heading of the dialog asking whether to hide a title from the viewer, opened from Hide this in a title's detail dialog, shown before the title is known.

screens.connectToServer.addressLabel.usage: Label of the field for typing a server's address.

screens.connectToServer.addressPlacehold.usage: Example address in the server address field. Keep it a web address; example.com is reserved for examples.

screens.connectToServer.connect.usage: Button that connects the desktop app to the address typed.

screens.connectToServer.copyright.usage: Small line at the foot of the screen when there is no build information to show.

screens.connectToServer.couldNotReach.value: Valence at {address} could not be reached. Check that it is running.
screens.connectToServer.couldNotReach.usage: Error under the address field when the server the app was last pointed at did not answer. {address} is that server's address.

screens.connectToServer.foundHere.usage: Heading above servers found running on this computer.

screens.connectToServer.foundNearby.usage: Heading above servers found on the local network.

screens.connectToServer.heading.usage: Heading of the screen where the desktop app is pointed at a server. Valence is the product's name; each server is 'a Valence'.

screens.connectToServer.lede.value: The address you would open in a browser.
screens.connectToServer.lede.usage: Text under the heading, explaining which address to type.

screens.connectToServer.looking.usage: The Connect button's text while the app checks that the server answers.

screens.connectToServer.nothingAnswered.value: Nothing answered at {address}. Check the address and that Valence is running.
screens.connectToServer.nothingAnswered.usage: Error under the address field when nothing answered at the address typed. {address} is that address.

screens.connectToServer.recent.usage: Heading above servers this app connected to before.

screens.continueListening.heading.usage: Heading of the row of audiobooks this person is partway through.

screens.continueReading.title.usage: Heading of the row on the Books page of books this viewer has started and not finished.

screens.decideForSomebody.allow.usage: Choice for one account: may watch this title whatever their age limit says.

screens.decideForSomebody.deny.usage: Choice for one account: may never watch this title.

screens.decideForSomebody.detail.value: Whatever age limit each account has. A denial always wins.
screens.decideForSomebody.detail.usage: Text under the heading: these choices override age limits, and a denial beats any allowance.

screens.decideForSomebody.label.usage: Screen-reader name of the panel where an administrator decides which accounts may watch one title.

screens.decideForSomebody.nobody.value: There is nobody to decide about. Administrators see everything, and taking something out of your own browsing is what hiding it does.
screens.decideForSomebody.nobody.usage: Shown when there are no other non-administrator accounts.

screens.decideForSomebody.rowLabel.usage: Screen-reader name of the Allow / Their limit / Deny choice on one account's row. {title} is the title; {name} is the account's name.

screens.decideForSomebody.theirLimit.usage: Choice for one account: no exception, so their usual age limit decides.

screens.decideForSomebody.title.usage: Heading of that panel. {title} is the film or programme's title.

screens.describeBrowsing.comingFilms.usage: Heading of the Requests page when it lists films not yet released that can be requested.

screens.describeBrowsing.comingSeries.usage: Heading of the Requests page when it lists TV series not yet released that can be requested.

screens.describeBrowsing.popularFilms.usage: Heading of the Requests page when it lists every popular film that can be requested.

screens.describeBrowsing.popularSeries.usage: Heading of the Requests page when it lists every popular TV series that can be requested.

screens.describeBrowsing.studioFilms.usage: Heading of the Requests page when it lists one studio's films. {studio} is the studio's name.

screens.describeBrowsing.studioSeries.usage: Heading of the Requests page when it lists one studio's TV series. {studio} is the studio's name.

screens.describeBrowsing.trendingFilms.usage: Heading of the Requests page when it lists every trending film that can be requested.

screens.describeBrowsing.trendingSeries.usage: Heading of the Requests page when it lists every trending TV series that can be requested.

screens.describeBrowsing.unnamedStudioFi.usage: Heading of the Requests page when it lists one studio's films and the studio's name is not known yet.

screens.describeBrowsing.unnamedStudioSe.usage: Heading of the Requests page when it lists one studio's TV series and the studio's name is not known yet.

screens.describeCatalogueCard.inLibrary.usage: Badge on a card for a title that can be requested, saying it is already in the library.

screens.describeCatalogueCard.watched.usage: Read out by screen readers for the tick in the corner of a card, saying the viewer has seen it to the end.

screens.describeDownloadCost.days.one.usage: In the Requests list, under a request that has finished downloading. How long it took, when that was one day.

screens.describeDownloadCost.days.other.usage: In the Requests list, under a request that has finished downloading. How long it took, in days.

screens.describeDownloadCost.hours.usage: In the Requests list, under a request that has finished downloading. How long it took, in whole hours (abbreviated). {hours} is a number.

screens.describeDownloadCost.hoursAndMin.usage: In the Requests list, under a request that has finished downloading. How long it took, in hours and minutes (abbreviated). {hours} and {minutes} are numbers.

screens.describeDownloadCost.minutes.usage: In the Requests list, under a request that has finished downloading. How long it took, in minutes (abbreviated). {minutes} is a number.

screens.describeDownloadCost.sizeAndTime.usage: In the Requests list, under a request that has finished downloading. How large it was and how long it took. {size} is a size such as 1.4 GB, {time} a duration such as 12 min.

screens.describeDownloadCost.sizeOnly.usage: In the Requests list, under a request that has finished downloading. How large it was, when how long it took is not known. {size} is a size such as 1.4 GB.

screens.describeDownloadCost.timeOnly.usage: In the Requests list, under a request that has finished downloading. How long it took, when its size is not known. {time} is a duration such as 12 min.

screens.describeDownloadCost.underAMinut.usage: In the Requests list, under a request that has finished downloading. How long it took, when that was less than a minute. Fills {time} in the download summary.

screens.describeDownloadProgress.doneOfS.usage: Under a downloading request: how much has arrived out of the whole. {done} and {size} are amounts of data such as “2.0 GB”.

screens.describeDownloadProgress.timeLef.usage: Under a downloading request: how long until it finishes. {time} is a length of time such as “12 min”, which may be drawn as a rolling number.

screens.describeJobStatus.running.usage: Badge on a piece of background work on the admin Jobs page, while it is running.

screens.describeJobStatus.stopping.usage: Badge on a piece of background work on the admin Jobs page, after it has been asked to stop and before it has.

screens.describeLogLevel.debug.usage: Name of the least serious level of server log record, on the admin logs view's filters, tags and graph.

screens.describeLogLevel.errors.usage: Name of the most serious level of server log record, on the admin logs view's filters, tags and graph.

screens.describeLogLevel.info.usage: Name of the level of server log record that is ordinary information, on the admin logs view's filters, tags and graph.

screens.describeLogLevel.warnings.usage: Name of the level of server log record that is a warning, on the admin logs view's filters, tags and graph.

screens.describePasskeyUnavailability.ne.value: Passkeys need a secure connection. Reach Valence over HTTPS, or on localhost, to add one.
screens.describePasskeyUnavailability.ne.usage: On the Security tab of the account dialog, when the page was not opened over a secure connection. HTTPS and localhost are technical terms; keep them.

screens.describePasskeyUnavailability.no.usage: On the Security tab of the account dialog, in place of the passkeys controls, when passkeys cannot be used at all.

screens.describePasskeyUnavailability.no.value: This browser does not support passkeys.
screens.describePasskeyUnavailability.no.usage: On the Security tab of the account dialog, when this browser cannot use passkeys.

screens.describePlaying.episodeCode.usage: Short code for which episode is playing, shown in the player's title such as "S2E5". {season} is the season number and {episode} the episode number or range, such as "5" or "5–6".

screens.describeProblem.brokenHeadline.usage: Heading of the page shown in place of one that failed for any other reason.

screens.describeProblem.brokenReason.value: Something on this page went wrong. The rest of Valence is still running, so try it again or go somewhere else.
screens.describeProblem.brokenReason.usage: Explanation under the heading of the page shown when a page failed for any other reason. Valence is the product's name.

screens.describeProblem.notAllowedHeadli.value: You are not allowed to see this page
screens.describeProblem.notAllowedHeadli.usage: Heading of the page shown in place of one this account may not open.

screens.describeProblem.notAllowedReason.value: Ask whoever runs this Valence to give you access, or sign in as somebody who has it.
screens.describeProblem.notAllowedReason.usage: Explanation under the heading of the page shown when this account may not open a page. Valence is the product's name.

screens.describeProblem.notFoundHeadline.value: This page could not be found
screens.describeProblem.notFoundHeadline.usage: Heading of the page shown for an address that leads nowhere.

screens.describeProblem.notFoundReason.value: It may have been moved or removed. Go back to the start and look for it from there.
screens.describeProblem.notFoundReason.usage: Explanation under the heading of the page shown for an address that leads nowhere.

screens.describeProblem.unreachableHeadl.usage: Heading of the page shown in place of one that failed because the server did not answer. Valence is the product's name.

screens.describeProblem.unreachableReaso.value: The server may be restarting, or this device may be offline. Check the connection and try again.
screens.describeProblem.unreachableReaso.usage: Explanation under the heading of the page shown when the server did not answer.

screens.describeProblem.updatedHeadline.usage: Heading of the page shown in place of one that failed because the app was updated while it was open. Valence is the product's name.

screens.describeProblem.updatedReason.value: This page belongs to an older version than the one now running. Loading it again fetches the new one.
screens.describeProblem.updatedReason.usage: Explanation under the heading of the page shown when the app was updated while it was open.

screens.describeRequestFilters.askedBy.usage: A heading in the filter menu of the Requests list. Its choices are the people who made the requests.

screens.describeRequestFilters.goneLibra.usage: A choice in the Library group of the Requests filter menu, for requests whose library has since been deleted.

screens.describeRequestFilters.kind.usage: A heading in the filter menu of the Requests list. Its choices are the kinds of thing requested: film, series, artist, album, book.

screens.describeRequestFilters.library.usage: A heading in the filter menu of the Requests list. Its choices are the libraries the requests are for.

screens.describeRequestFilters.noQuality.usage: A choice in the Quality group of the Requests filter menu, for requests with no quality profile.

screens.describeRequestFilters.quality.usage: A heading in the filter menu of the Requests list. Its choices are the quality profiles the requests are fetched at.

screens.describeRequestFilters.whereItIs.usage: A heading in the filter menu of the Requests list. Its choices are how far each request has got, such as downloading or in the library.

screens.describeRunSubject.everyLibrary.usage: In the Subject column of the job runs table: a library job that ran over all the libraries.

screens.describeRunSubject.everything.usage: In the Subject column of the job runs table: a job that was not about anything in particular.

screens.describeRunSubject.removedLibrar.value: A library that has been removed
screens.describeRunSubject.removedLibrar.usage: In the Subject column of the job runs table: the run was about a library that no longer exists.

screens.describeRunSubject.requests.usage: In the Subject column of the job runs table: a job that worked on viewers' media requests.

screens.describeRunSubject.theCatalogue.usage: In the Subject column of the job runs table: a job that worked on the catalogue of titles.

screens.describeRunSubject.thisServer.usage: In the Subject column of the job runs table: a job that worked on the server itself.

screens.describeSessionDelivery.directPl.value: Direct play — the original file, handed over untouched
screens.describeSessionDelivery.directPl.usage: Longer explanation of the DirectPlay badge, in a session's details on the admin Sessions page.
Badge on a session card on the admin Sessions page: the viewer is being sent the original file untouched. A technical term; keep it short.

screens.describeSessionDelivery.directSt.value: Direct stream — the original picture, with the sound converted
screens.describeSessionDelivery.directSt.usage: Longer explanation of the DirectStream badge, in a session's details on the admin Sessions page.
Badge on a session card on the admin Sessions page: the original picture is sent, with only the sound converted. A technical term; keep it short.

screens.describeSessionDelivery.remuxDet.value: Remux — the original picture and sound, rewrapped for this client
screens.describeSessionDelivery.remuxDet.usage: Longer explanation of the Remux badge, in a session's details on the admin Sessions page.

screens.describeSessionDelivery.remuxLab.usage: Badge on a session card on the admin Sessions page: the original picture and sound are being rewrapped in a different container. A technical term; keep it short.

screens.describeSessionDelivery.transcod.value: Transcoding — the server is converting the picture on the fly
screens.describeSessionDelivery.transcod.usage: Longer explanation of the Transcoding badge, in a session's details on the admin Sessions page.
Badge on a session card on the admin Sessions page: the server is converting the picture as it plays.

screens.describeShareEnding.expiredDetai.value: It was made to last a while, and that while is over. Whoever sent it can send another.
screens.describeShareEnding.expiredDetai.usage: Shown to a guest opening a share link that has run out of time, under the sentence saying the link no longer works. “It” is the link.

screens.describeShareEnding.spentDetail.value: It was made to be opened a set number of times, and it has been. Whoever sent it can send another.
screens.describeShareEnding.spentDetail.usage: Shown to a guest opening a share link that has been opened as many times as it allowed, under the sentence saying the link no longer works. “It” is the link.

screens.describeShareEnding.withdrawnDet.value: Somebody stopped it working. Whoever sent it can send another.
screens.describeShareEnding.withdrawnDet.usage: Shown to a guest opening a share link that was switched off, under the sentence saying the link no longer works. “It” is the link.

screens.detectDeviceProfile.browser.usage: Name given to a web browser in the list of devices someone is signed in on, when nothing better is known.

screens.deviceApproval.allowed.value: Done. The television should be watching in a moment — you can close this.
screens.deviceApproval.allowed.usage: Shown once the television has been let in.

screens.deviceApproval.asking.value: A television is asking to sign in as you. Only say yes if it is the one in front of you.
screens.deviceApproval.asking.usage: Shown once a real code has been typed, above the buttons that allow or refuse it.

screens.deviceApproval.checking.usage: Read out by screen readers while the typed code is checked.

screens.deviceApproval.codeLabel.usage: Label of the field for typing the code a television shows.

screens.deviceApproval.continue.usage: Button that checks the typed television code.

screens.deviceApproval.heading.usage: Heading of the page where somebody lets a television sign in as them.

screens.deviceApproval.lede.value: A television showed you a code. Type it here and {name} will let it in as you.
screens.deviceApproval.lede.usage: Text under the heading. {name} is what this server is called, normally 'Valence'.

screens.deviceApproval.no.value: No, I did not ask for this
screens.deviceApproval.no.usage: Button that refuses the television's request.

screens.deviceApproval.refused.value: Turned down. Nothing was signed in, and the code on that screen is now useless.
screens.deviceApproval.refused.usage: Shown once the television's request has been refused.

screens.deviceApproval.wrongCode.value: That code has run out, or there is no television waiting on it.
screens.deviceApproval.wrongCode.usage: Error under the code field when the code is not valid.

screens.deviceApproval.yes.usage: Button that lets the television sign in.

screens.deviceList.actionsFor.usage: Screen-reader name of the menu button on a row of the devices table. {name} is the device's name.

screens.deviceList.deviceHeader.usage: Column header in the table of devices this account is signed in on: the device's name.

screens.deviceList.empty.value: Nothing is signed in, which cannot be true of the thing you are reading this on. Try again in a moment.
screens.deviceList.empty.usage: Shown in the devices table when the server reports no signed-in devices, which should never happen.

screens.deviceList.endOneBody.value: {name} will be signed out and whoever is using it has to sign in again.
screens.deviceList.endOneBody.usage: Body of the dialog confirming one device should be signed out. {name} is the device's name.

screens.deviceList.endOneConfirm.usage: Confirm button of the dialog that signs one device out.

screens.deviceList.endOneTitle.usage: Title of the dialog confirming that one device should be signed out.

screens.deviceList.endRestBody.one.value: {count} other device will be signed out. This one stays as it is.
screens.deviceList.endRestBody.one.usage: Body of the dialog signing out every other device, when there is one other. {count} is the number.

screens.deviceList.endRestBody.other.value: {count} other devices will be signed out. This one stays as it is.
screens.deviceList.endRestBody.other.usage: Body of the dialog signing out every other device. {count} is how many other devices there are.

screens.deviceList.endRestConfirm.usage: Confirm button of the dialog that signs every other device out.

screens.deviceList.endRestTitle.usage: Title of the dialog confirming every other device should be signed out.

screens.deviceList.heading.usage: Heading of the card listing every device this account is signed in on.

screens.deviceList.loading.usage: Read out by screen readers while the list of signed-in devices loads.

screens.deviceList.signOutEverywhereElse.usage: Button on the devices card that signs out every device except the one in use.

screens.deviceList.signThisOut.usage: Menu item on a device in the devices table that signs that device out.

screens.deviceList.signedInHeader.usage: Column header in the table of signed-in devices: when each device signed in.

screens.deviceList.tableLabel.usage: Screen-reader name of the table listing the devices this account is signed in on.

screens.deviceList.thisOne.usage: Badge beside the device the person is using right now, in the list of their signed-in devices.

screens.devicesPanel.controlling.usage: Under This device in the devices panel, when this device is controlling music playing on another. {device} is the other device’s name.

screens.devicesPanel.noOtherDevices.value: Open Valence on another device, signed in as you, and it will be here.
screens.devicesPanel.noOtherDevices.usage: Shown in the devices panel when no other device is signed in as this person. Valence is the product’s name.

screens.devicesPanel.notPlaying.usage: Under another device in the devices panel, when it is not playing anything.

screens.devicesPanel.otherDevices.usage: Heading of the list of this person’s other signed-in devices in the devices panel.

screens.devicesPanel.pausedOnTitle.usage: Under another device in the devices panel: the song it is paused on. {title} is the song.

screens.devicesPanel.playHere.usage: Button in the devices panel that moves the music playing elsewhere onto this device.

screens.devicesPanel.playOn.usage: Button for one of the other devices in the devices panel; it moves the music there. {device} is that device’s name.

screens.devicesPanel.playingHere.usage: Under This device in the devices panel, when music is playing on this device.

screens.devicesPanel.playingTitle.usage: Under another device in the devices panel: what it is playing. {title} is the song.

screens.devicesPanel.readyToPlay.usage: Under This device in the devices panel, when nothing is playing yet.

screens.devicesPanel.thisDevice.usage: In the panel for playing music on another device: names the device this person is using.

screens.discoverShelves.reading.value: Reading what there is to ask for
screens.discoverShelves.reading.usage: Read out by screen readers while the Discover tab of the Requests page is being fetched.

screens.discoverShelves.whatThereIs.value: What there is to ask for
screens.discoverShelves.whatThereIs.usage: Fills the gap in the sentence “{what} could not be read…”, shown when the Discover tab of the Requests page could not be fetched. Starts the sentence.

screens.downloadDialog.about.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Beside a quality when downloading several episodes, whose total can only be estimated. {size} is a size such as 1.4 GB.

screens.downloadDialog.converted.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Note beside a quality that the server has to convert the file to make.

screens.downloadDialog.couldNotStart.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Error notice shown when asking for the download failed.

screens.downloadDialog.fits.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Says the download fits. {size} is how large it is and {free} how much room this device has, both sizes such as 1.4 GB.

screens.downloadDialog.heading.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Heading of the dialog.

screens.downloadDialog.howLarge.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Read out by screen readers as the name of the list of qualities to choose between.

screens.downloadDialog.label.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Read out by screen readers as the dialog's name. {title} is the film or series, and may be empty.

screens.downloadDialog.nothing.value: Nothing can be prepared for this yet.
screens.downloadDialog.nothing.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Shown when there is no size on offer to download.

screens.downloadDialog.prepare.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Confirm button that asks the server to prepare the download of a film.

screens.downloadDialog.queue.one.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Confirm button that asks the server to prepare the download of one episode.

screens.downloadDialog.queue.other.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Confirm button that asks the server to prepare the downloads of several episodes.

screens.downloadDialog.seriesDetail.one.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Under the heading when downloading one episode of a series. {title} is the series.

screens.downloadDialog.seriesDetail.othe.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Under the heading when downloading several episodes of a series. {title} is the series.

screens.downloadDialog.sizeUnknown.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Beside a quality when how large the download would be is not known.

screens.downloadDialog.started.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Notice shown once the server has started preparing the download.

screens.downloadDialog.startedDetail.value: Valence can be closed in the meantime. You will get a notification when it is ready, and it comes to this device the next time Valence is open.
screens.downloadDialog.startedDetail.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Text under “The server is preparing it” in the notice shown once the download has started.

screens.downloadDialog.tight.value: {size} of the {free} free on this device.
screens.downloadDialog.tight.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Under “That is most of what is left”. {size} is how large the download is and {free} how much room this device has.

screens.downloadDialog.tightTitle.value: That is most of what is left
screens.downloadDialog.tightTitle.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Heading of the warning shown when the download would use most of the room on this device.

screens.downloadDialog.willNotFit.value: It needs {size}, and this device has {free} free.
screens.downloadDialog.willNotFit.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Under “That will not fit”. {size} is how large the download is and {free} how much room this device has.

screens.downloadDialog.willNotFitTitle.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Heading of the warning shown when the download is larger than the room on this device.

screens.downloadDialog.working.value: Working out what this would cost
screens.downloadDialog.working.usage: In the desktop app's dialog for downloading a film or episodes to this device. Read out by screen readers while the sizes on offer are worked out.

screens.downloadList.deleteHere.value: Delete {title} from this device and the server
screens.downloadList.deleteHere.usage: In the Downloads dialog, under a download in the list. Read out by screen readers for the bin button, when a copy is on this device. {title} is the download.

screens.downloadList.deleteHereDetail.value: It is removed from this device and from the server. How far you got through it is kept.
screens.downloadList.deleteHereDetail.usage: Explanation in the dialog asking whether to delete a download that is on this device.

screens.downloadList.deleteServer.usage: In the Downloads dialog, under a download in the list. Read out by screen readers for the bin button, when no copy is on this device. {title} is the download.

screens.downloadList.deleteServerDetail.value: The server stops keeping its copy. A device that already has one keeps its own.
screens.downloadList.deleteServerDetail.usage: Explanation in the dialog asking whether to delete a download that is not on this device.

screens.downloadList.deleteTitle.usage: Heading of the dialog asking whether to delete a download, opened from its bin button in the Downloads dialog. {title} is the download.

screens.downloadList.deleteUnnamedTitle.usage: Heading of the dialog asking whether to delete a download, opened from its bin button in the Downloads dialog, before it is known which.

screens.downloadList.done.usage: In the Downloads dialog, under a download in the list. One part of the progress line while it is prepared. {done} is how far along, such as 40%.

screens.downloadList.empty.value: Nothing prepared yet. Ask for something from its page and it will appear here.
screens.downloadList.empty.usage: Shown in the Downloads dialog when nothing has been downloaded.

screens.downloadList.failed.usage: In the Downloads dialog, under a download in the list. Says the server failed to prepare it, when it gave no reason.

screens.downloadList.pause.usage: In the Downloads dialog, under a download in the list. Read out by screen readers for the button that pauses a download. {title} is the download.

screens.downloadList.paused.value: Paused at {done}. What is done is kept.
screens.downloadList.paused.usage: In the Downloads dialog, under a download in the list. Says it has been paused. {done} is how far it had got, such as 40%.

screens.downloadList.preparing.usage: In the Downloads dialog, under a download in the list. Progress line while the server prepares it. {details} is how far along, how fast and how long is left, separated by “ · ”.

screens.downloadList.preparingElsewhere.value: The server prepares these by itself, and each goes to the device it was asked for on. You will get a notification when each is ready.
screens.downloadList.preparingElsewhere.usage: Note at the top of the Downloads dialog in a browser while anything is being prepared.

screens.downloadList.preparingHere.value: The server prepares these by itself, so Valence can be closed in the meantime. You will get a notification when each is ready, and it comes to this device the next time Valence is open.
screens.downloadList.preparingHere.usage: Note at the top of the Downloads dialog in the desktop app while anything is being prepared.

screens.downloadList.preparingLabel.usage: In the Downloads dialog, under a download in the list. Read out by screen readers for its progress bar. {title} is what is being prepared.

screens.downloadList.rate.usage: In the Downloads dialog, under a download in the list. One part of the progress line while it is prepared: how fast. {rate} is a size such as 2 MB; “/s” means per second.

screens.downloadList.readyElsewhere.value: Ready on the device that asked.
screens.downloadList.readyElsewhere.usage: In the Downloads dialog, under a download in the list. In a browser: says the server has prepared it for the device it was asked for on.

screens.downloadList.readyElsewhereSized.value: Ready on the device that asked — {size}.
screens.downloadList.readyElsewhereSized.usage: In the Downloads dialog, under a download in the list. In a browser: says the server has prepared it for the device it was asked for on. {size} is its size such as 1.4 GB.

screens.downloadList.readyOf.one.usage: In the Downloads dialog, beside the name of a series with one episode downloading. {ready} is how many are ready.

screens.downloadList.readyOf.other.usage: In the Downloads dialog, beside the name of a series: how many of its downloaded episodes are ready. {ready} is how many are ready, {count} how many there are.

screens.downloadList.readyToKeep.value: Ready to keep on this device.
screens.downloadList.readyToKeep.usage: In the Downloads dialog, under a download in the list. Says the server has prepared it and it can be kept on this computer.

screens.downloadList.readyToKeepSized.value: Ready to keep on this device — {size}.
screens.downloadList.readyToKeepSized.usage: In the Downloads dialog, under a download in the list. Says the server has prepared it and it can be kept on this computer. {size} is its size such as 1.4 GB.

screens.downloadList.resume.usage: In the Downloads dialog, under a download in the list. Read out by screen readers for the button that resumes a paused download. {title} is the download.

screens.downloadList.waiting.usage: In the Downloads dialog, under a download in the list. Says it is queued behind others.

screens.downloadList.waitingFrom.usage: In the Downloads dialog, under a download in the list. Says it is queued to carry on. {done} is how far it had got, such as 40%.

screens.downloadList.yours.usage: In the Downloads dialog, names what could not be loaded, in a message saying it could not be read.

screens.downloadsDialog.browserDetail.value: What you have asked for on your other devices, and how far along each is.
screens.downloadsDialog.browserDetail.usage: In the Downloads dialog, opened from Downloads in the top bar. Text under the heading in a browser, which cannot keep files.

screens.downloadsDialog.goOffline.usage: In the Downloads dialog, opened from Downloads in the top bar. Name of the switch, in the desktop app, that shows only what is kept on this device.

screens.downloadsDialog.goOfflineDetail.value: Show only what is on this device. Worth turning on before you lose the connection rather than after.
screens.downloadsDialog.goOfflineDetail.usage: In the Downloads dialog, opened from Downloads in the top bar. Description of the Go offline switch in the desktop app.

screens.downloadsDialog.heading.usage: In the Downloads dialog, opened from Downloads in the top bar. Heading of the dialog, also read out by screen readers as its name.

screens.downloadsDialog.keepableDetail.value: Once one is on this device it is yours until you delete it.
screens.downloadsDialog.keepableDetail.usage: In the Downloads dialog, opened from Downloads in the top bar. Text under the heading in the desktop app.

screens.emptyLibrary.askAdmin.value: Ask the server admin to scan it.
screens.emptyLibrary.askAdmin.usage: Shown on the home page in place of the rows when there is nothing to show. Text under the heading, for somebody who cannot scan it themselves.

screens.emptyLibrary.libraryEmpty.usage: Shown on the home page in place of the rows when there is nothing to show. Heading when the chosen library is empty but others are not. {library} is its name.

screens.finishOnAnotherDevice.waiting.usage: Read out by screen readers while the television waits for setup to be finished on the phone.

screens.groupReleases.other.usage: Heading over an artist's releases whose type (album, single and so on) is not known, in the artist's request dialog.

screens.hiddenPanel.loading.usage: Read out by screen readers while the list of hidden things loads.

screens.hiddenPanel.noLibraries.usage: Shown in place of the library buttons when the server has no libraries.

screens.hiddenPanel.programmeBadge.usage: Badge on an entry in the list of hidden things, saying a whole programme (TV series) was hidden.

screens.hiddenPanel.tableLabel.usage: Screen-reader name of the table of hidden things.

screens.historyPanel.finished.usage: Badge on a history entry that was watched or read to the end.

screens.historyPanel.goneFromLibrary.usage: Stands in for the title of something watched that has since been removed from the library.

screens.historyPanel.loading.usage: Read out by screen readers while the viewing history loads.

screens.historyPanel.showMore.usage: Button at the foot of the history that loads older entries.

screens.historyPanel.viewing.usage: Under a film in the history. {when} is when it was watched, such as 'Yesterday'; {duration} is how long, such as '1h 20m'.

screens.jobHistory.empty.usage: Shown in the job runs table when nothing matches the search and filters.

screens.jobHistory.failedStat.usage: Label of a count above the job runs table: how many runs failed.

screens.jobHistory.oldestFirst.usage: Option in the menu that orders the list of job runs: earliest first.

screens.jobHistory.statsLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the strip of counts above the job runs table.

screens.libraryChoicesFor.film.usage: Name of the menu beside Films in the navigation bar that picks which film library to show.

screens.libraryChoicesFor.programme.usage: Name of the menu beside Shows in the navigation bar that picks which TV library to show.

screens.likedView.couldNotReadWhat.usage: Fills the gap in the message shown when the Liked Songs page could not be loaded, saying what could not be read. Written to sit inside that sentence.

screens.likedView.emptyDetail.value: Press the heart beside any song to keep it.
screens.likedView.emptyDetail.usage: Explanation shown on the Liked Songs page when this person has liked nothing.

screens.likedView.emptyTitle.value: Songs you like will be here
screens.likedView.emptyTitle.usage: Heading shown on the Liked Songs page when this person has liked nothing.

screens.likedView.play.usage: Round play button on the Liked Songs page.

screens.likedView.playlist.usage: Small label above the title of the Liked Songs page.

screens.likedView.reading.usage: Read out by screen readers while the Liked Songs page is loading.

screens.likedView.shuffle.usage: Button on the Liked Songs page that plays them in a shuffled order.

screens.likedView.title.usage: Name of the automatic playlist of every song this person has liked; the title of its page, and the name shown for where the queue came from.

screens.listeningPartyFrom.theHost.usage: Used in place of the name of whoever started a listening party, when their name is not known. Fills a gap in messages about the party.

screens.listeningPartyPanel.howItWorks.value: Everybody hears what you play, where you are in it. Each of them keeps their own volume.
screens.listeningPartyPanel.howItWorks.usage: Explanation in the listening party panel, while something is playing, of what a listening party does.

screens.listeningPartyPanel.inWatchParty.value: Leave it before starting a party to listen together.
screens.listeningPartyPanel.inWatchParty.usage: Explanation in the listening party panel when this person is already in a watch party.

screens.listeningPartyPanel.inWatchParty.value: You are in a watch party
screens.listeningPartyPanel.inWatchParty.usage: Heading in the listening party panel when this person is already in a watch party.

screens.listeningPartyPanel.playFirst.value: Play something, then start a party and send the link to anybody with an account here.
screens.listeningPartyPanel.playFirst.usage: Explanation in the listening party panel when nothing is playing yet.

screens.listeningPartyPanel.start.usage: Button in the listening party panel that starts a party.

screens.listeningPartyPanel.title.usage: Heading in the listening party panel, before a party has started.

screens.logDetailDialog.happenedTerm.usage: Label of a row in the log record: how many times the same line was written in a row.

screens.logDetailDialog.levelTerm.usage: Label of a row in the log record: how serious it is, such as info or error.

screens.logDetailDialog.sourceTerm.usage: Label of a row in the log record: which part of the server wrote it.

screens.logDetailDialog.times.one.usage: How many times the same log line happened, when that is one.

screens.logDetailDialog.times.other.usage: How many times the same log line happened. {count} is that number.

screens.logDetailDialog.title.usage: Title of the side dialog showing everything known about one line of the server's log, and its name for screen readers.

screens.logDetailDialog.when.usage: When a log record was written. {day} is the day, such as “Today” or a date, and {time} the time of day.

screens.logDetailDialog.whenTerm.usage: Label of a row in the log record: when it was written.

screens.logExplorer.asFarAsItReads.value: That is as far back as this list reads — narrow it to see the rest.
screens.logExplorer.asFarAsItReads.usage: At the end of the log when there are more matching lines than the list will load.

screens.logExplorer.barsLabel.value: How many events the log holds at each level over time
screens.logExplorer.barsLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the bar chart above the log.

screens.logExplorer.busiestFirst.usage: Option in the menu that orders the log: the lines written most often first.

screens.logExplorer.busiestFirstDetail.usage: Short explanation under the Most repeated first ordering option.

screens.logExplorer.copied.usage: Brief notice after the log lines shown are copied.

screens.logExplorer.copiedLine.usage: Brief notice after one log line is copied.

screens.logExplorer.copyLines.usage: Menu item that copies every log line shown to the clipboard.

screens.logExplorer.cutLines.usage: Menu item that goes back to cutting long log lines to one line.

screens.logExplorer.downloadLines.usage: Menu item that saves every log line shown as a text file.

screens.logExplorer.emptyDetail.value: Try a longer time range, or take some filters off.
screens.logExplorer.emptyDetail.usage: Suggestion under the title when no log lines match.

screens.logExplorer.emptyTitle.usage: Title shown in place of the log when nothing matches the search and filters.

screens.logExplorer.eventsHeading.usage: Column heading in the lists of top sources and top jobs: how many log lines each wrote.

screens.logExplorer.everything.usage: At the end of the log when every matching line is shown.

screens.logExplorer.filterLabel.usage: Button that opens the menu narrowing the log by source, job or identifier.

screens.logExplorer.hideTime.usage: Menu item that hides the time at the start of each log line.

screens.logExplorer.identifierFilter.usage: Heading of a group in the log's filter menu listing identifiers the log is narrowed to.

screens.logExplorer.identifierItem.usage: An identifier the log is narrowed to, as in “Library 1a2b3c”. {field} is what it names and {value} the identifier.

screens.logExplorer.jobField.usage: Names a job run's identifier in the log's filter menu and its chips.

screens.logExplorer.jobFilter.usage: Heading of a group in the log's filter menu: which kind of job wrote the line.

screens.logExplorer.jobHeading.usage: Column heading in the list of top jobs.

screens.logExplorer.libraryField.usage: Names a library's identifier in the log's filter menu and its chips.

screens.logExplorer.linesHeading.usage: Heading of the section listing the log's lines.

screens.logExplorer.linesLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the list of the log's lines.

screens.logExplorer.live.usage: Toggle button that keeps reading new log lines every few seconds.

screens.logExplorer.loadingMore.usage: At the end of the log while older lines load.

screens.logExplorer.mediaField.usage: Names a media item's identifier in the log's filter menu and its chips.

screens.logExplorer.moreLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the ⋯ menu button above the log.

screens.logExplorer.newestFirst.usage: Option in the menu that orders the log: most recent lines first.

screens.logExplorer.newestFirstDetail.usage: Short explanation under the Newest first ordering option.

screens.logExplorer.oldestFirst.usage: Option in the menu that orders the log: earliest lines first.

screens.logExplorer.oldestFirstDetail.usage: Short explanation under the Oldest first ordering option.

screens.logExplorer.orderGroup.usage: Heading of the options in the menu that orders the log.

screens.logExplorer.orderLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the menu that orders the log.

screens.logExplorer.reading.usage: Shown while the log's lines load.

screens.logExplorer.refresh.usage: Read out by screen readers for the refresh button above the log.

screens.logExplorer.requestField.usage: Names a web request's identifier in the log's filter menu and its chips.

screens.logExplorer.searchLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the search field above the log.

screens.logExplorer.searchPlaceholder.value: Search — or filter with level:error  job:abc123  library:…  session:…
screens.logExplorer.searchPlaceholder.usage: Placeholder in the log's search field. The words before each colon (level, job, library, session) are typed filter codes and must stay in English; keep the double spaces between examples.

screens.logExplorer.sessionField.usage: Names a playback session's identifier in the log's filter menu and its chips.

screens.logExplorer.severestFirst.usage: Option in the menu that orders the log: errors before warnings before the rest.

screens.logExplorer.severestFirstDetail.usage: Short explanation under the Most serious first ordering option.

screens.logExplorer.showMore.usage: Button at the end of the log that loads older lines.

screens.logExplorer.showTime.usage: Menu item that shows the time at the start of each log line.

screens.logExplorer.showing.usage: Comes before the number of lines shown, as in “Showing 50 of 1,200”. Keep the trailing space.

screens.logExplorer.showingOf.usage: Between the number of lines shown and the number there are, as in “Showing 50 of 1,200”. Keep the spaces.

screens.logExplorer.sourceFilter.usage: Heading of a group in the log's filter menu: which part of the server wrote the line.

screens.logExplorer.sourceHeading.usage: Column heading in the list of top sources.

screens.logExplorer.topJobs.usage: Heading of the list of kinds of job that logged the most.

screens.logExplorer.topJobsEmpty.value: No job logged in this time.
screens.logExplorer.topJobsEmpty.usage: Shown in the top jobs list when no job logged in the chosen time.

screens.logExplorer.topJobsLabel.value: Kinds of job that logged the most
screens.logExplorer.topJobsLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the list of top jobs.

screens.logExplorer.topSources.usage: Heading of the list of parts of the server that logged the most.

screens.logExplorer.topSourcesEmpty.usage: Shown in the top sources list when nothing was logged in the chosen time.

screens.logExplorer.topSourcesLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the list of top sources.

screens.logExplorer.viewGroup.usage: Heading of the menu items that change how the log is laid out.

screens.logExplorer.wrapLines.usage: Menu item that lets long log lines wrap onto several lines.

screens.logExplorer.zoomedTo.usage: Button showing the stretch of time the graph was dragged across to; pressing it zooms back out. {from} and {until} are times of day.

screens.logLine.actionsLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the ⋮ menu button beside a log line.

screens.logLine.contextLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the row of identifiers shown when a log line is opened.

screens.logLine.copyLine.usage: Menu item on a log line that copies it to the clipboard as text.

screens.logLine.jobField.usage: Names a job run's identifier on a log line, in its menu and its expanded detail.

screens.logLine.kindField.usage: Names the kind of job a log line came from, in its menu and its expanded detail.

screens.logLine.libraryField.usage: Names a library's identifier on a log line, in its menu and its expanded detail.

screens.logLine.lineLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for a log line, which opens it when pressed. {level} is how serious it is, {source} the part of the server that wrote it and {message} what it said.

screens.logLine.mediaField.usage: Names a media item's identifier on a log line, in its menu and its expanded detail.

screens.logLine.narrowGroup.usage: Heading of the menu items that narrow the whole log to one thing about this line.

screens.logLine.narrowItem.usage: Menu item narrowing the log to one identifier, as in “Library 1a2b3c4d…”. {field} is what the identifier names and {value} the identifier.

screens.logLine.narrowTo.usage: Read out by screen readers for a button in an opened log line. {field} is what the identifier names, such as Library, and {value} the identifier.
