screens.logLine.onlySource.usage: Menu item narrowing the log to one source. {source} is the name of the part of the server that wrote the line.

screens.logLine.requestField.usage: Names a web request's identifier on a log line, in its menu and its expanded detail.

screens.logLine.sessionField.usage: Names a playback session's identifier on a log line, in its menu and its expanded detail.

screens.logLine.showDetails.usage: Menu item on a log line that opens everything known about it.

screens.logLine.traceJob.usage: Menu item on a log line that opens the timeline of the job run that wrote it.

screens.lyricLines.sync.usage: Button shown after scrolling away from the lyrics being sung; it scrolls back to follow the song again.

screens.lyricsView.noLyrics.usage: Shown on the lyrics page when the song playing has no lyrics.

screens.lyricsView.nothingPlayingDetail.value: Play a song to follow its words here.
screens.lyricsView.nothingPlayingDetail.usage: Explanation on the lyrics page when no song is playing.

screens.lyricsView.nothingPlayingTitle.usage: Heading on the lyrics page when no song is playing.

screens.lyricsView.reading.usage: Read out by screen readers while the lyrics are loading.

screens.lyricsView.regionLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the lyrics page. {title} is the song playing.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.actions.usage: Read out by screen readers as the name of the bar of actions at the bottom of the dialog.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.cast.usage: Heading over the list of performers, shown while it loads or when there are none.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.download.usage: Action that opens the dialog for downloading the title to this device, in the desktop app.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.extras.usage: Heading of the row of trailers, featurettes and other extras.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.hide.usage: Action that hides the title from the viewer.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.keep.usage: Read out by screen readers for the heart button on a title's artwork that adds it to the viewer's favourites. {title} is the title.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.moreFromSeason.usage: Heading of the row of other episodes of the same season. {season} is its number.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.moreFromSeries.usage: Heading of the row of other episodes, when the season is not known.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.noCast.value: Nobody is credited yet. A metadata provider supplies the cast.
screens.mediaDetailDialog.noCast.usage: Shown under Cast when no performers are known.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.noSynopsis.value: No synopsis yet. Configure a metadata provider and rescan to fill this in.
screens.mediaDetailDialog.noSynopsis.usage: Shown under Synopsis when the title has no description.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.original.usage: Shown on the version menu when the original version is chosen.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.play.usage: Main button that starts playing the title from the beginning.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.playOnTv.usage: Action that plays the title on one of the viewer's televisions instead of here.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.preparing.usage: Read out by screen readers for the spinner beside the download action while the download is prepared.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.preparingPerce.usage: Takes the place of Download while the download is being prepared. {percent} is how far along it is, such as 40%.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.previewMoment.usage: Action, for administrators, that picks the moment of the film its preview image is taken from.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.resumeFrom.usage: Main button that carries on playing from where the viewer stopped. {time} is a position such as 1:02:15.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.share.usage: Action that makes a link to the title to give to somebody.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.startAgain.usage: Action that plays the title from the beginning even though the viewer had started it.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.stopKeeping.usage: Read out by screen readers for the heart button on a title's artwork that removes it from the viewer's favourites. {title} is the title.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.synopsis.usage: Heading over the description of what the title is about.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.theRest.usage: Names what could not be loaded (the synopsis, cast and so on), in a message saying it could not be read.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.trailer.usage: Read out by screen readers as the name of the trailer player. {title} is the film or series.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.version.usage: Heading of the list of versions in the version menu.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.watchTogether.usage: Action that starts a watch party on the title.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.watchTrailer.usage: Action that plays the title's trailer.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.whichVersion.usage: Read out by screen readers for the menu choosing between versions of a film, such as a director's cut.

screens.mediaDetailDialog.whoMayWatch.usage: Action, for whoever runs the household, that decides which members may watch the title.

screens.mediaFacts.season.usage: Short fact in the line of facts about an episode, in its detail dialog. S abbreviates season; {season} is its number.

screens.mediaGrid.label.usage: Read out by screen readers as the name of the grid of cards on a browse page such as Films.

screens.mediaPreview.absent.usage: In the short preview clip that plays when a pointer rests on a card, or at the top of a title's detail dialog. Shown in place of the clip when there is none.

screens.mediaPreview.pause.usage: In the short preview clip that plays when a pointer rests on a card, or at the top of a title's detail dialog. Read out by screen readers for the button that pauses the clip.

screens.mediaPreview.play.usage: In the short preview clip that plays when a pointer rests on a card, or at the top of a title's detail dialog. Read out by screen readers for the button that plays the paused clip.

screens.mediaPreview.soundOff.usage: In the short preview clip that plays when a pointer rests on a card, or at the top of a title's detail dialog. Read out by screen readers for the button that mutes the clip.

screens.mediaPreview.soundOn.usage: In the short preview clip that plays when a pointer rests on a card, or at the top of a title's detail dialog. Read out by screen readers for the button that unmutes the clip.

screens.missingRow.notInLibrary.usage: Under an episode in a show's list that the catalogue knows of but the library does not have.

screens.motionChoices.reduced.usage: Choice of how much the screens animate, in the Profile tab of the account dialog and the account menu: as little movement as possible.

screens.motionChoices.system.usage: Choice of how much the screens animate, in the Profile tab of the account dialog and the account menu: follow the device's own reduced-motion setting.

screens.musicDiscover.nothingTitle.usage: Heading on the Music tab of the Requests page when there is nothing to suggest.

screens.musicDiscover.reading.value: Reading what music there is to ask for
screens.musicDiscover.reading.usage: Read out by screen readers while the Music tab of the Requests page is being fetched.

screens.musicFeature.newest.usage: Label above the large album at the top of the music home page when nothing is playing: it is the album added most recently.

screens.musicFeature.nowPlaying.usage: Label above the large song at the top of the music home page while it plays.

screens.musicFeature.pause.usage: Button at the top of the music home page that pauses the song playing.

screens.musicFeature.paused.usage: Label above the large song at the top of the music home page while it is paused.

screens.musicFeature.play.usage: Button at the top of the music home page that plays the newest album.

screens.musicFeature.resume.usage: Button at the top of the music home page that carries on playing a paused song.

screens.musicFeature.upNext.usage: Heading of the short list of the next songs in the queue, at the top of the music home page.

screens.musicFeature.watchVideo.usage: Button at the top of the music home page that opens the music video for the song.

screens.musicHome.artists.usage: Heading of the shelf of artists on the music home page.

screens.musicHome.emptyDetail.value: Once a music library has been added and scanned, its albums and artists will be here.
screens.musicHome.emptyDetail.usage: Explanation on the music home page when there is no music.

screens.musicHome.emptyTitle.usage: Heading on the music home page when there is no music.

screens.musicHome.reading.usage: Read out by screen readers while the music home page is loading.

screens.musicHome.recentlyAdded.usage: Heading of the shelf of the albums added most recently, on the music home page.

screens.musicHome.seeAll.usage: Button beside a shelf on the music home page that opens the page listing all of it.

screens.musicHome.seeAllAlbums.usage: Read out by screen readers for the See all button beside the Recently added shelf on the music home page.

screens.musicHome.seeAllArtists.usage: Read out by screen readers for the See all button beside the Artists shelf on the music home page.

screens.musicHome.seeAllPlaylists.usage: Read out by screen readers for the See all button beside the Your playlists shelf on the music home page.

screens.musicHome.sharedWithYou.usage: Heading of the shelf of playlists other people in the household have shared, on the music home page.

screens.musicHome.yourPlaylists.usage: Heading of the shelf of this person’s own playlists on the music home page.

screens.musicLibrary.albumBy.usage: Small line under an album in the library down the left of the music section. {artist} is its artist.

screens.musicLibrary.artist.usage: Small line under an artist in the library down the left of the music section.

screens.musicLibrary.heading.usage: Heading of the library down the left of the music section.

screens.musicLibrary.playlistBy.usage: Small line under a playlist in the library down the left of the music section. {owner} is who made it.

screens.musicLibrary.regionLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the library down the left of the music section.

screens.musicLibrary.searchMusic.usage: Button at the top of the music library that opens the music search page.

screens.musicMenuFor.shuffle.usage: Item in the menu for an album, artist or playlist that plays it in a shuffled order.

screens.musicPage.party.usage: Heading of the panel for listening to music together with other people.

screens.musicPage.yourLibrary.usage: Button, on narrow screens, that opens the music library as a drawer; also the name of that drawer.

screens.musicSearchView.artists.usage: Heading of the artists found by a music search.

screens.reencodeDialog.whatToDo.usage: Section heading in the re-encode dialog above the choice of what to do with the chosen files.

screens.reencodeDialog.whatToDoLabel.value: What to do with the encode
screens.reencodeDialog.whatToDoLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the row of Replace, Keep alongside and Audio only choices.

screens.reencodeDialog.whatToWorkOn.usage: Section heading in the re-encode dialog above the list of files to choose from.

screens.reencodeDialog.whichLibrary.usage: Read out by screen readers for the row of library names in the re-encode dialog.

screens.reencodeReview.confirm.usage: Button that accepts the new encode.

screens.reencodeReview.confirmAndFree.usage: Button that accepts the new encode. {size} is the disk space that disposing of the original frees, such as 16 GB.

screens.reencodeReview.detail.value: Both files are still here. Nothing is discarded until you say so.
screens.reencodeReview.detail.usage: Under the title of the re-encode review dialog.

screens.reencodeReview.dispose.usage: Button that deletes the original file.

screens.reencodeReview.disposeAndFree.usage: Button that deletes the original file. {size} is the disk space freed, such as 16 GB.

screens.reencodeReview.disposeDetail.value: The original file is deleted. What the encoder discarded cannot be recovered, and if this was the only copy, nothing brings it back.
screens.reencodeReview.disposeDetail.usage: Warning in the dialog confirming that the original file will be deleted.

screens.reencodeReview.disposeTitle.usage: Heading of the dialog confirming that the original file will be deleted.

screens.reencodeReview.encodeAlt.usage: Description of the still frame from the new encode, for screen readers. {at} is a time in the film such as 1:02:15.

screens.reencodeReview.encodeCaption.usage: Caption under the still frame from the new encode; its quality and format may follow. {size} is its size such as 8 GB, or the words for an unknown size.

screens.reencodeReview.label.usage: Read out by screen readers as the name of the dialog where an administrator compares a finished encode with its original.

screens.reencodeReview.lookHint.value: {at} — pick a scene with motion rather than the opening titles. Grain, banding and a grey picture all show up there and nowhere else.
screens.reencodeReview.lookHint.usage: Advice under the slider in the re-encode review dialog. {at} is the chosen time such as 1:02:15.

screens.reencodeReview.originalAlt.usage: Description of the still frame from the original file, for screen readers. {at} is a time in the film such as 1:02:15.

screens.reencodeReview.originalCaption.usage: Caption under the still frame from the original file. {size} is its size such as 24 GB.

screens.reencodeReview.reject.value: Reject and put the original back
screens.reencodeReview.reject.usage: Button that refuses the new encode and restores the original file.

screens.reencodeReview.sizeUnknown.usage: In the caption of the new encode's still frame, in place of its size when that is not known. Lower case because it follows other words.

screens.reencodeReview.stillLimitsBody.value: Compression that only shows while things move, and audio, need the real player. Both files are on disk, so nothing about this is final until you choose.
screens.reencodeReview.stillLimitsBody.usage: Body of the note in the re-encode review dialog about what still frames cannot show.

screens.reencodeReview.stillLimitsTitle.value: What a still cannot tell you
screens.reencodeReview.stillLimitsTitle.usage: Heading of the note in the re-encode review dialog about what still frames cannot show.

screens.reencodeReview.watch.usage: Button that opens the new encode in the player.

screens.reencodeReview.whereToLook.value: Where in the film to look
screens.reencodeReview.whereToLook.usage: Label of the slider that chooses the moment both still frames are taken from.

screens.releaseTypeChooser.description.value: Which of their releases are fetched, now and as new ones come out.
screens.releaseTypeChooser.description.usage: Explanation under the Releases label when requesting an artist.

screens.releaseTypeChooser.label.usage: Label of the choice of which kinds of an artist's releases to fetch, such as albums or singles.

screens.releaseTypeChooser.listLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the list of kinds of release that can be ticked.

screens.requestKindNames.album.usage: Badge or filter choice naming what kind of thing a request is for: a music album.

screens.requestKindNames.artist.usage: Badge or filter choice naming what kind of thing a request is for: a music artist.

screens.requestKindNames.book.usage: Badge or filter choice naming what kind of thing a request is for: a book.

screens.requestKindNames.film.usage: Badge or filter choice naming what kind of thing a request is for: a film.

screens.requestKindNames.series.usage: Badge or filter choice naming what kind of thing a request is for: a TV series.

screens.requestsList.askedBy.usage: Under a request in the list: who asked for it. {name} is that person's name.

screens.requestsList.askedByYou.usage: Under a request in the list, when the person looking asked for it.

screens.requestsList.cancel.usage: Button beside one of your requests that withdraws it (asks first).

screens.requestsList.cancelConfirm.usage: Button in the dialog that withdraws the request.

screens.requestsList.cancelDetail.value: It will not be fetched, and whatever it had started downloading is deleted. You can request it again whenever you like.
screens.requestsList.cancelDetail.usage: Body of the dialog confirming a request should be withdrawn.

screens.requestsList.cancelThisRequest.usage: Title of the dialog confirming a request should be withdrawn, when its title is not known.

screens.requestsList.cancelTitle.usage: Title of the dialog confirming a request should be withdrawn. {title} is what was requested.

screens.requestsList.coverOf.usage: Read out by screen readers for the artwork of a requested album or artist. {title} is its name.

screens.requestsList.details.usage: Button beside a request that has not arrived yet, showing its details.

screens.requestsList.emptyDetail.value: Find something on Discover, or search for it, and request it from its page.
screens.requestsList.emptyDetail.usage: Shown under “Nothing has been requested yet”. Discover names a tab of the same page.

screens.requestsList.emptyTitle.usage: Heading on the Requests tab when nobody has asked for anything.

screens.requestsList.filter.usage: Button opening the filters for the list of requests.

screens.requestsList.howMuchArrived.usage: Read out by screen readers for the progress bar of a request that is downloading. {title} is what was requested.

screens.requestsList.listLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the list of requests.

screens.requestsList.noneMatchDetail.value: Clear a filter, or search for something else.
screens.requestsList.noneMatchDetail.usage: Shown under “Nothing matches that” on the list of requests.

screens.requestsList.noneMatchTitle.usage: Heading shown in place of the list of requests when the filters or search leave nothing.

screens.requestsList.open.usage: Button beside a request that has arrived, opening it in the library.

screens.requestsList.reading.usage: Read out by screen readers while the list of requests is being fetched.

screens.requestsList.refused.usage: Under a request an administrator turned down. {reason} is what they wrote as the reason.

screens.requestsList.search.usage: Read out by screen readers for the search field above the list of requests.

screens.requestsList.searchPlaceholder.usage: Placeholder text in the search field above the list of requests.

screens.requestsList.theRequests.usage: Fills the gap in the sentence “{what} could not be read…”, shown when the list of requests could not be fetched. Starts the sentence.

screens.requestsPage.books.usage: Tab on the Requests page listing books that can be asked for.

screens.requestsPage.discover.usage: Tab on the Requests page showing what is trending, popular and coming soon.

screens.requestsPage.heading.usage: Heading of the Requests page, read out by screen readers only.

screens.requestsPage.mine.usage: Tab on the Requests page listing what has been requested and where each has got to.

screens.requestsPage.movies.usage: Tab on the Requests page listing films that can be asked for.

screens.requestsPage.music.usage: Tab on the Requests page listing music that can be asked for.

screens.requestsPage.shows.usage: Tab on the Requests page listing TV series that can be asked for.

screens.requestsPage.tabsLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the row of tabs at the top of the Requests page.

screens.scrollingPages.nextChapter.usage: Button at the end of a scrolling comic chapter that opens the next chapter.

screens.scrollingPages.pageAlt.usage: Description of one page's picture in a comic, for screen readers. {number} is the page number.

screens.scrollingPages.pages.usage: Read out by screen readers for the long scrolling strip of a comic's pages.

screens.scrollingPages.theEnd.usage: Shown at the end of the last chapter of a scrolling comic.

screens.searchArea.albums.usage: Heading of the row of albums among the search results.

screens.searchArea.artists.usage: Heading of the row of artists among the search results.

screens.searchArea.books.usage: Choice above the search results that searches only books.

screens.searchArea.booksRow.usage: Title of the row of books among the search results.

screens.searchArea.everything.usage: Choice above the search results that searches every kind of thing in the library.

screens.searchArea.films.usage: Choice above the search results that searches only films.

screens.searchArea.filter.usage: Button opening the filters on the Search page.

screens.searchArea.libraryEmpty.value: This library has nothing in it yet. Scanning one from the home page is where things come from.
screens.searchArea.libraryEmpty.usage: Shown on the Search page when the library has nothing in it at all.

screens.searchArea.music.usage: Choice above the search results that searches only music.

screens.searchArea.nothingHere.usage: Above the search results when there are none.

screens.searchArea.nothingMatches.value: Nothing matches all of that. Taking one of the filters off is usually the fastest way back.
screens.searchArea.nothingMatches.usage: Shown on the Search page when filters are set and nothing matches them.

screens.searchArea.placeholder.usage: Placeholder text in the large search field on the Search page.

screens.searchArea.results.usage: Read out by screen readers for the section holding the search results.

screens.searchArea.resultsSuffix.one.usage: Written straight after the number of search results, when that is one. Keep the space at the start; the number itself comes before it.

screens.searchArea.resultsSuffix.other.usage: Written straight after the number of search results. Keep the space at the start; the number itself comes before it.

screens.searchArea.searchLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the large search field on the Search page.

screens.searchArea.searching.usage: Read out by screen readers while a search is running.

screens.searchArea.shows.usage: Choice above the search results that searches only TV series.

screens.searchArea.theLibrary.usage: Fills the gap in the sentence “{what} could not be read…”, shown when searching failed. Starts the sentence.

screens.searchArea.typeABook.value: Type the name of a book, or who wrote it.
screens.searchArea.typeABook.usage: Shown on the Search page with Books chosen before anything has been typed.

screens.searchArea.whatToSearch.usage: Read out by screen readers for the row of choices of what kind of thing to search.

screens.searchPage.heading.usage: Heading of the Search page, read out by screen readers only.

screens.seasonChooser.asking.value: Asking the catalogue for its seasons
screens.seasonChooser.asking.usage: Read out by screen readers while a series' seasons are being fetched.

screens.seasonChooser.episodes.usage: Column heading in the table of a series' seasons: how many episodes each has.

screens.seasonChooser.everyOne.value: Every season, and any that come later.
screens.seasonChooser.everyOne.usage: Under the table of a series' seasons when every season is taken.

screens.seasonChooser.everySeason.usage: Read out by screen readers for the switch at the top of the seasons table that takes or drops every season at once.

screens.seasonChooser.firstAired.usage: Column heading in the table of a series' seasons: the year each was first shown.

screens.seasonChooser.noSeasons.value: The catalogue lists no seasons for this series.
screens.seasonChooser.noSeasons.usage: Shown in the table of a series' seasons when it has none.

screens.seasonChooser.noneTaken.usage: Under the table of a series' seasons when no season is taken.

screens.seasonChooser.season.usage: Column heading in the table of a series' seasons, in the dialog for requesting it.

screens.seasonChooser.seasons.usage: Label of the table of a series' seasons in the dialog for requesting it.

screens.seasonChooser.someTaken.one.usage: Under the table of a series' seasons: how many are taken. {ticked} is how many are taken, {count} how many the series has, when that is one.

screens.seasonChooser.someTaken.other.usage: Under the table of a series' seasons: how many are taken. {ticked} is how many are taken, {count} how many the series has.

screens.seasonChooser.status.usage: Column heading in the table of a series' seasons: whether each is in the library, requested and so on.

screens.seasonChooser.whichSeasons.usage: Read out by screen readers for the table of a series' seasons.

screens.seasonPicker.notInLibrary.usage: Beside a season in the menu of a show's seasons when none of its episodes are in the library.

screens.seasonPicker.season.usage: Heading of the menu of a show's seasons, for a show with many.

screens.seasonPicker.whichSeason.usage: Read out by screen readers for the choice of which season's episodes a show's dialog lists.

screens.seriesDialog.aSeries.usage: What screen readers call the dialog for a series of books, while its name is not yet known.

screens.seriesDialog.books.one.usage: Under the title of a series of books: how many books it has, when that is one.

screens.seriesDialog.books.other.usage: Under the title of a series of books: how many books it has.

screens.seriesDialog.close.usage: Read out by screen readers for the button that closes the dialog for a series of books.

screens.seriesDialog.inOrder.usage: Title of the row of a series' books, numbered in the order they are meant to be read.

screens.setupWizard.access.usage: Heading of the setup wizard's section about the addresses the server is reached at.

screens.setupWizard.administrator.usage: Heading of the setup wizard's section for the first administrator's account.

screens.setupWizard.alreadySetUp.value: This server has already been set up. Reload the page to sign in.
screens.setupWizard.alreadySetUp.usage: Error at the bottom of the setup wizard when somebody else finished setting the server up first.

screens.setupWizard.couldNotComplete.value: Setup could not be completed. Check the details and try again.
screens.setupWizard.couldNotComplete.usage: Error at the bottom of the setup wizard when the server refused what was filled in.

screens.setupWizard.couldNotReach.value: Could not reach the server. Check that it is still running.
screens.setupWizard.couldNotReach.usage: Error at the bottom of the setup wizard when the server did not answer.

screens.setupWizard.email.usage: Label of the field for the administrator's email address in the setup wizard.

screens.setupWizard.finish.usage: Button at the bottom of the setup wizard that creates the administrator and finishes setting the server up.

screens.setupWizard.heading.usage: Heading of the setup wizard shown the first time a new server is opened. Valence is the product's name.

screens.setupWizard.https.value: This server is reached over HTTPS
screens.setupWizard.https.usage: Checkbox in the setup wizard saying the server is reached over an encrypted connection.

screens.setupWizard.lede.value: Create the administrator account and confirm how this server is reached.
screens.setupWizard.lede.usage: Under the heading of the setup wizard.

screens.setupWizard.name.usage: Label of the field for the administrator's name in the setup wizard.

screens.setupWizard.password.usage: Label of the field for the administrator's password in the setup wizard.

screens.setupWizard.passwordHint.usage: Hint under the password field in the setup wizard.

screens.setupWizard.plainCookies.value: Cookies will not be marked secure, so Valence works over plain HTTP on your network.
screens.setupWizard.plainCookies.usage: Under the HTTPS checkbox in the setup wizard, when it is not ticked. Valence is the product's name.

screens.setupWizard.secureCookies.value: Secure cookies will be used. Login will not work over plain HTTP.
screens.setupWizard.secureCookies.usage: Under the HTTPS checkbox in the setup wizard, when it is ticked.

screens.setupWizard.trustedOrigins.usage: Label of the setup wizard's field listing the web addresses this server may be reached at.

screens.setupWizard.trustedOriginsHint.value: Detected {origin}. Add every address you use to reach Valence, separated by commas.
screens.setupWizard.trustedOriginsHint.usage: Hint under the trusted origins field in the setup wizard. {origin} is the address the browser reached the server at. Valence is the product's name.

screens.shareArea.askForANewOne.value: Ask whoever sent it for a new one.
screens.shareArea.askForANewOne.usage: Under the heading of the page shown for a share link that does not work.

screens.shareArea.keptOnThisDevice.value: Where you are up to is kept on this device only.
screens.shareArea.keptOnThisDevice.usage: Under the Read button on a shared book's page.

screens.shareArea.linkDoesNotWork.usage: Heading of the page shown for a share link that does not work, when it is not known why.

screens.shareArea.nothingToWatch.value: There is nothing here to watch.
screens.shareArea.nothingToWatch.usage: Shown on a share link's page when what was shared has nothing left in it to play.

screens.shareArea.opening.value: Opening what was shared with you on {name}
screens.shareArea.opening.usage: Read out by screen readers while a share link is being opened. {name} is what the server is called.

screens.shareArea.read.usage: Button on a shared book's page that opens it to read.

screens.shareArea.sharedWithYou.usage: Small label at the top of the page a share link opens. {name} is what the server is called.

screens.shareDialog.bookExplainer.value: Anybody holding the link can read this book, and nothing else. Where they are up to stays on their own device. You can withdraw it at any time.
screens.shareDialog.bookExplainer.usage: Explanation in the share dialog, when sharing a book, of what the link allows.

screens.shareDialog.copied.usage: Button in the share dialog, once the link has been copied.

screens.shareDialog.copyLink.usage: Button in the share dialog that copies the link just made.

screens.shareDialog.copyNow.value: Copy it now — this is the only time it is shown.
screens.shareDialog.copyNow.usage: Shown in the share dialog once the link has been made, above it.

screens.shareDialog.couldNotShare.value: That could not be shared. You may not have permission to hand out links.
screens.shareDialog.couldNotShare.usage: Error in the share dialog when a link could not be made.

screens.shareDialog.justThisEpisode.usage: Choice in the share dialog, opened from an episode, to share only that episode.

screens.shareDialog.lasts.usage: Label of the share dialog's choice of how long the link keeps working.

screens.shareDialog.makeLink.usage: Button in the share dialog that creates the share link.

screens.shareDialog.share.usage: What screen readers call the share dialog, and the small label above the title's name at the top of it.

screens.shareDialog.theLink.usage: Label of the field holding the share link once it has been made.

screens.shareDialog.watchExplainer.value: Anybody holding the link can watch what you shared, and nothing else. You can withdraw it at any time, including while somebody is watching.
screens.shareDialog.watchExplainer.usage: Explanation in the share dialog of what the link allows.

screens.shareDialog.whatToShare.usage: Label beside what a share link will lead to, or of the choice between one episode and the whole programme.

screens.shareDialog.whoCanRead.usage: Label of the share dialog's choice of how many people a book's link works for.

screens.shareDialog.whoCanWatch.usage: Label of the share dialog's choice of how many people a link works for.

screens.shareDialog.wholeBook.usage: In the share dialog, beside “What to share”, when a book is being shared.

screens.shareDialog.wholeProgramme.usage: In the share dialog: sharing every episode of a programme, shown beside “What to share” or as a choice there.

screens.sharePanel.empty.value: You have not handed out any links. Sharing something from its page makes one.
screens.sharePanel.empty.usage: Shown in the share-links table when there are none.

screens.sharePanel.heading.usage: Heading of the card listing share links this person made; also names what failed to load inside an error such as 'Could not read …'.

screens.sharePanel.lede.value: Anybody holding one of these can watch what it points at without an account here. Withdrawing a link stops it at once, including for anybody watching through it.
screens.sharePanel.lede.usage: Explanation at the top of the Your links card.

screens.sharePanel.linkToHeader.usage: Column header in the table of share links: what each link points at.

screens.sharePanel.loading.usage: Read out by screen readers while the share links load.

screens.sharePanel.madeWhen.usage: Under a share link's title: when it was made. {when} is a relative time such as '3 days ago'.

screens.sharePanel.openedHeader.usage: Column header in the table of share links: how many times each has been opened.

screens.sharePanel.standingHeader.usage: Column header in the table of share links: whether each link is live, spent or withdrawn.

screens.sharePanel.tableLabel.usage: Screen-reader name of the table of share links.

screens.sharePanel.wholeSeries.usage: Badge on a share link that shares a whole TV series rather than one title.

screens.sharePanel.withdrawBody.value: The link to {title} stops working at once, including for anybody watching through it right now.
screens.sharePanel.withdrawBody.usage: Body of the dialog confirming a share link should be withdrawn. {title} is what the link points at.

screens.sharePanel.withdrawConfirm.usage: Confirm button of the dialog that withdraws a share link.

screens.sharePanel.withdrawLabel.usage: Screen-reader name of the button that withdraws a share link. {title} is what the link points at.

screens.sharePanel.withdrawTitle.usage: Title of the dialog confirming a share link should be withdrawn.

screens.shelfMoreCard.seeMore.usage: On the last card of a shelf on the Discover tab of the Requests page, which opens the whole list.

screens.showDialog.aboutEpisode.usage: Action in a show's dialog that opens the details of the episode its play button would play.

screens.showDialog.close.usage: Read out by screen readers for the buttons that close a show's dialog.

screens.showDialog.download.usage: Action in a show's dialog that keeps episodes on this device, with a choice of which.

screens.showDialog.episodes.one.usage: At the top of a show's dialog: how many episodes it has, when that is one.

screens.showDialog.episodes.other.usage: At the top of a show's dialog: how many episodes it has.

screens.showDialog.episodesHeading.usage: Heading of the list of episodes in a show's dialog.

screens.showDialog.markAllUnwatched.usage: Button above a show's episodes, for a show with one season, that marks every episode as not watched.

screens.showDialog.markAllWatched.usage: Button above a show's episodes, for a show with one season, that marks every episode as watched.

screens.showDialog.markSeasonUnwatched.usage: Button above a show's episodes that marks every episode of the chosen season as not watched.

screens.showDialog.markSeasonWatched.usage: Button above a show's episodes that marks every episode of the chosen season as watched.

screens.showDialog.moreToDo.value: More to do with this programme
screens.showDialog.moreToDo.usage: Read out by screen readers for the bar of actions at the bottom of a show's dialog.

screens.showDialog.nextEpisode.usage: At the top of a show's dialog: the next episode to be aired. {season} and {episode} are numbers (S and E stand for season and episode); {when} says when it airs, such as “in 3 days”.

screens.showDialog.nothingYet.value: Nothing here yet. Episodes appear as they are scanned.
screens.showDialog.nothingYet.usage: Shown in place of a show's episodes when none are in the library yet.

screens.showDialog.seasons.one.usage: At the top of a show's dialog: how many seasons it has, when that is one.

screens.showDialog.seasons.other.usage: At the top of a show's dialog: how many seasons it has.

screens.showDialog.share.usage: Action in a show's dialog that makes a link to share it.

screens.showDialog.theEpisodes.usage: Fills the gap in the sentence “{what} could not be read…”, shown when a show's episodes could not be fetched. Starts the sentence.

screens.showDialog.trailer.usage: What screen readers call the dialog playing a show's trailer, and the video inside it. {title} is the show's title.

screens.showDialog.watchTrailer.usage: Action in a show's dialog that plays its trailer.

screens.showDialog.watched.usage: Badge at the top of a show's dialog when every episode has been watched.

screens.signedIn.loading.usage: Read out by screen readers on the splash screen while the app starts. {name} is what this server is called.

screens.signedIn.unreachableBody.value: The server did not respond. Check that it is running and reload the page.

screens.signedIn.unreachableHeading.usage: Heading of the page shown when the server did not answer while signing in. Valence is the product's name.

screens.spreadStage.pageAlt.usage: Description of one page's picture in a comic shown a page or two at a time, for screen readers. {number} is the page number.

screens.stillWatchingDialog.stopping.usage: Shown in the still watching dialog once its countdown has run out.

screens.stillWatchingDialog.stoppingIn.o.usage: Countdown in the still watching dialog, when one second is left.

screens.stillWatchingDialog.title.usage: Heading, and screen-reader name, of the dialog asked before playing another episode nobody chose.

screens.streamStats.audio.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: the audio format.

screens.streamStats.bitrate.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: how much data per second the stream uses.

screens.streamStats.bufferedAhead.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: how many seconds are loaded beyond where the viewer is.

screens.streamStats.clockJitter.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: how much the timing between this viewer and the watch party wobbles.

screens.streamStats.close.usage: Button, read out by screen readers, that closes the Stats for nerds panel in the player.

screens.streamStats.container.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: the file container format.

screens.streamStats.deciding.usage: Value in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream while the server is still working out how to serve the stream.

screens.streamStats.delivery.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: how and from what address the stream is delivered.

screens.streamStats.directDelivery.usage: Value in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream when the file is sent as it is. {url} is the address it comes from.

screens.streamStats.encodedSoFar.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: how many seconds the server has converted so far.

screens.streamStats.frameOnScreen.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: the point in the video of the picture showing now.

screens.streamStats.framesDropped.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: how many frames the browser skipped.

screens.streamStats.framesOf.usage: Value in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: how many frames were skipped out of how many were decoded. {dropped} and {decoded} are numbers.

screens.streamStats.fromTheServer.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: the warnings the server sent.

screens.streamStats.groupOutput.usage: Small heading over the facts about what is actually being sent to the browser in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream.

screens.streamStats.groupPlan.usage: Small heading over the facts about what the server decided to do with each part of the file in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream.

screens.streamStats.groupPlayback.usage: Small heading over the facts about how playback is going in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream.

screens.streamStats.groupSession.usage: Small heading over the facts about the playback session in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream.

screens.streamStats.groupSource.usage: Small heading over the facts about the original file in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream.

screens.streamStats.groupWarnings.usage: Small heading over the warnings the server gave about this stream, in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream.

screens.streamStats.groupWatchParty.usage: Small heading over the facts about the watch party this viewing is part of, in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream.

screens.streamStats.heading.usage: Heading of the Stats for nerds panel in the player, which shows technical details of the stream; also read out by screen readers as the panel's name.

screens.streamStats.held.usage: Value in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: the watch party is held while somebody catches up.

screens.streamStats.hertz.usage: Audio sample rate in the player's Stats for nerds panel, in hertz. {rate} is a whole number such as 48000.

screens.streamStats.hlsDelivery.usage: Value in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream when the stream is sent as HLS, a streaming format. {url} is the address it comes from.

screens.streamStats.mediaId.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: the internal id of what is playing.

screens.streamStats.mode.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: how the stream is being served, such as played directly or converted.

screens.streamStats.nobody.usage: Value in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream when the watch party is not waiting for anybody.

screens.streamStats.none.usage: Value in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream when there is none of that thing, such as no audio or no subtitles.

screens.streamStats.notApplicable.usage: Value in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream when the figure does not apply; short for "not applicable".

screens.streamStats.notReported.usage: Value in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream when the browser or server has not given that figure.

screens.streamStats.notStarted.usage: Value in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream when the playback session has not started yet.

screens.streamStats.nothingSelected.usage: Value in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream before the player has chosen which version of the stream to use.

screens.streamStats.outBy.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: how many seconds this viewer is ahead of or behind the watch party.

screens.streamStats.paused.usage: Value in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: the watch party is paused.

screens.streamStats.playing.usage: Value in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: the watch party is playing.

screens.streamStats.position.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: where the viewer is in the video.

screens.streamStats.presentedSize.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: how big the picture is drawn on screen.

screens.streamStats.reused.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: whether an earlier conversion of this file is being reused.

screens.streamStats.roomPosition.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: where in the video the watch party is.

screens.streamStats.roomState.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: whether the watch party is playing, paused or held.

screens.streamStats.session.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: the id of the playback session.

screens.streamStats.startsAt.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: the point in the video where the playback session began.

screens.streamStats.streamStartsAt.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: the point in the video where the current stream begins.

screens.streamStats.subtitleTracks.one.usage: Value in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: there is one subtitle track, and its format. {format} is a technical format name such as "srt".

screens.streamStats.subtitleTracks.other.usage: Value in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: how many subtitle tracks there are, and the format of the first one. {format} is a technical format name such as "srt".

screens.streamStats.subtitles.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: the subtitle tracks.

screens.streamStats.tabKeepsTime.usage: Value in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream when this browser tab is the one the watch party keeps time by.

screens.streamStats.title.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: the title of what is playing.

screens.streamStats.unknown.usage: Value in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream when that fact is not known.

screens.streamStats.video.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: the video format.

screens.streamStats.waitingFor.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: who the watch party is waiting for.

screens.streamStats.watchingTogether.usage: Row label in the player's Stats for nerds panel, which shows technical details of the stream: how many people are in the watch party.

screens.studiosRail.title.usage: Title of the row of film studios on the Discover tab of the Requests page.

screens.televisionHandoff.anotherCode.usage: Button on a television's phone sign-in screen, after something went wrong, that asks for a fresh code.

screens.televisionHandoff.asking.usage: Read out by screen readers while a television's phone sign-in screen waits for a code.

screens.televisionHandoff.expired.value: That code ran out. Ask for another one.
screens.televisionHandoff.expired.usage: Error on a television's phone sign-in screen when the code shown was not used in time.

screens.televisionHandoff.heading.usage: Heading of a television's screen that lets somebody sign it in from their phone.

screens.televisionHandoff.lede.value: Nobody should have to spell a password out with a remote. Open this on your phone and {name} will let this television in.

screens.televisionHandoff.qrLabel.usage: Read out by screen readers for the QR code a phone scans to sign the television in.

screens.televisionHandoff.refused.value: That was turned down on the other device.
screens.televisionHandoff.refused.usage: Error on a television's phone sign-in screen when somebody declined the request on their phone.

screens.televisionHandoff.unreachable.usage: Error on a television's phone sign-in screen when no code could be asked for. Valence is the product's name.

screens.televisionHandoff.waiting.value: Waiting for you to say yes.
screens.televisionHandoff.waiting.usage: Under the code on a television's phone sign-in screen while it waits for the phone to approve.

screens.textReader.howFar.usage: Read out by screen readers for the slider along the bottom of the book reader, which moves through the whole book.

screens.textReader.larger.usage: Choice in the book reader's text Size setting, bigger than Large.

screens.textReader.light.usage: Choice in the book reader's Page setting: dark text on a white page.

screens.textReader.loose.usage: Choice in the book reader's line Spacing setting: lines far apart.

screens.textReader.medium.usage: Choice in the book reader's text Size setting.

screens.textReader.narrow.usage: Choice in the book reader's Margins setting: small margins beside the text.

screens.textReader.nextChapter.usage: Read out by screen readers for the button beside the reader panel's contents picker that goes to the entry after.

screens.textReader.normal.usage: Choice in the book reader's line Spacing setting: ordinary spacing between lines.

screens.textReader.opening.usage: Read out by screen readers while an ebook's text is being fetched.

screens.textReader.page.usage: Title and label of the book reader's setting for the page's colours.

screens.textReader.previousChapter.usage: Read out by screen readers for the button beside the reader panel's contents picker that goes to the entry before.

screens.textReader.sepia.usage: Choice in the book reader's Page setting: brown text on a cream page.

screens.textReader.size.usage: Title and label of the book reader's text size setting.

screens.textReader.small.usage: Choice in the book reader's text Size setting.

screens.textReader.spacing.usage: Title and label of the book reader's setting for the space between lines.

screens.textReader.thatBook.usage: Fills {what} in “{what} could not be read…”, shown when the ebook being opened could not be fetched. Starts the sentence, so it is capitalised.

screens.textReader.theBeginning.usage: Shown in the reader panel's contents picker while the reader is before the first entry of the contents.

screens.textReader.tight.usage: Choice in the book reader's line Spacing setting: lines close together.

screens.textReader.wide.usage: Choice in the book reader's Margins setting: large margins beside the text.

screens.themeChoices.dark.usage: Choice of colour theme, in the Profile tab of the account dialog and the account menu: always dark.

screens.themeChoices.light.usage: Choice of colour theme, in the Profile tab of the account dialog and the account menu: always light.

screens.themeChoices.system.usage: Choice of colour theme, in the Profile tab of the account dialog and the account menu: follow the device's own light or dark setting.

screens.timeRangeMenu.groupName.usage: Heading of the options in the time range menu.

screens.timeRangeMenu.label.usage: Read out by screen readers for the menu choosing the stretch of time the page looks at.

screens.timeRangeMenu.time.usage: On the time range menu's button, when no known range is chosen.

screens.tourStops.homeTitle.usage: Heading of the welcome tour step that introduces the home page, which it also names in the navigation bar.

screens.tourStops.readDetail.value: Books and comics, with your place kept wherever you read them.

screens.tourStops.readTitle.usage: Heading of the welcome tour step that introduces the Books page, which it also names in the navigation bar.

screens.tourStops.requestsDetail.usage: Text of the welcome tour step that introduces the Requests page, saying what it is for.

screens.tourStops.requestsTitle.usage: Heading of the welcome tour step that introduces the Requests page, which it also names in the navigation bar.

screens.tourStops.searchDetail.usage: Text of the welcome tour step that introduces the Search page, saying what it is for.

screens.trackList.likeTrack.usage: Heart button in a track list, read out by screen readers, that adds a song to the liked songs. {title} is the song's title.

screens.trackList.lossless.usage: Small badge beside a song in a track list saying the file is lossless audio quality.

screens.trackList.playTrack.usage: Button over a song's number in a track list, read out by screen readers, that plays it. {title} is the song's title.

screens.trackMenu.goToAlbum.usage: Menu item in a song's menu that opens the album it is on.

screens.trackMenu.goToArtist.usage: Menu item in a song's menu that opens the page of the artist who made it.

screens.trackMenu.moreFor.usage: Button beside a song, read out by screen readers, that opens the menu of things to do with it. {title} is the song's title.

screens.trackMenu.watchTheVideo.usage: Menu item in a song's menu that plays the song's music video.

screens.videoPlayer.pressPlayToJoin.usage: Message shown in the player when the browser blocked a watch party's video from starting by itself.

screens.videoPlayer.waitingForMore.usage: Shown over the video, and read out by screen readers, while the player waits for more of the video to load. {title} is what is playing.

screens.videoPlayer.waitingForName.usage: Shown over the video while a watch party waits for one person to catch up. {name} is that person's name.

screens.videoPlayer.waitingForPeople.one.usage: Shown over the video while a watch party waits for people to catch up, when that is one person.

screens.videoPlayer.waitingForPeople.oth.usage: Shown over the video while a watch party waits for several people to catch up. {count} is how many.

screens.videoRemote.back.usage: Button in the remote dialog, read out by screen readers, that jumps the video back. {seconds} is how many seconds.

screens.videoRemote.forward.usage: Button in the remote dialog, read out by screen readers, that jumps the video forward. {seconds} is how many seconds.

screens.videoRemote.label.usage: Name of the remote dialog, read out by screen readers, before it knows which device it controls.

screens.videoRemote.labelFor.usage: Name of the remote dialog, read out by screen readers. {device} is the name of the device it controls.

screens.videoRemote.onDevice.usage: Under the remote dialog's title: which device the video is playing on. {device} is that device's name.

screens.videoRemote.pause.usage: Button in the remote dialog, read out by screen readers, that pauses the video on the other device.

screens.videoRemote.play.usage: Button in the remote dialog, read out by screen readers, that carries on playing the video on the other device.

screens.videoRemote.playHere.usage: Button in the remote dialog that stops the video on the other device and carries on playing it in this window.

screens.videoRemote.position.value: Where the film is up to
screens.videoRemote.position.usage: Slider in the remote dialog, read out by screen readers, that shows and moves how far through the video the other device is.

screens.videoRemote.starting.usage: Title of the remote dialog while the other device has not yet said what it is playing.

screens.videoRemote.stop.usage: Button in the remote dialog that stops the video playing on the other device.

screens.videoRemote.subtitleOnDevice.usage: Under the remote dialog's title: what is playing, such as a show's episode, then which device it plays on. {subtitle} is the episode or detail line and {device} is the device's name.

screens.videoRemoteBar.onDevice.usage: Under the title on the remote bar: which device the video is playing on. {device} is that device's name.

screens.videoRemoteBar.openRemote.usage: Button, read out by screen readers, on the small bar at the bottom of the window while this account plays a video on another device; it opens the remote. {device} is that device's name.

screens.videoRemoteBar.pause.usage: Button on the remote bar, read out by screen readers, that pauses the video on the other device.

screens.videoRemoteBar.play.usage: Button on the remote bar, read out by screen readers, that carries on playing the video on the other device.

screens.videoRemoteBar.starting.usage: Shown in place of a title on the remote bar while the other device has not yet said what it is playing.

screens.visualisers.ambience.usage: Name of a visualiser style, shown in the visualiser between the previous and next buttons.

screens.visualisers.barsAndWaves.usage: Name of a visualiser style, shown in the visualiser between the previous and next buttons.

screens.visualisers.halo.usage: Name of a visualiser style, shown in the visualiser between the previous and next buttons.

screens.visualisers.warp.usage: Name of a visualiser style, shown in the visualiser between the previous and next buttons.

screens.visualisers.waves.usage: Name of a visualiser style, shown in the visualiser between the previous and next buttons.

screens.watchPage.joiningParty.usage: Read out by screen readers on the splash screen shown while the player waits to join a watch party that is already playing.

screens.watchPage.loading.usage: Read out by screen readers on the splash screen shown while the player page loads. {name} is the name of this Valence server, normally "Valence".

screens.welcomeToValence.ready.value: {household} is ready. Everything else can be changed whenever you like.
screens.welcomeToValence.ready.usage: Under the heading of the welcome page shown once a new household has been set up. {household} is the name just given to the household.

screens.welcomeToValence.startWatching.usage: Button on the welcome page shown once a new household has been set up, which goes on to the home page.

screens.welcomeToValence.welcome.usage: Heading of the welcome page shown once a new household has been set up. {name} is what this server is called.

screens.welcomeTour.done.usage: Button on the last step of the welcome tour that closes it.

screens.welcomeTour.next.usage: Button in the welcome tour that goes on to the next step.

screens.welcomeTour.skip.usage: Button in the welcome tour that closes it without seeing the rest.

screens.welcomeTour.stepOfTotal.usage: Under the title of the welcome tour: which step of it this is. {step} is this step's number and {total} how many steps there are.

screens.welcomeTour.welcome.usage: Title of the first step of the welcome tour, and what screen readers call the tour's dialog. {name} is what this server is called.

screens.whatIsPlaying.episode.usage: Names an episode inside a sentence in the video player, as in “Waiting for more of the episode”.

screens.whatIsPlaying.film.usage: Names a film inside a sentence in the video player, as in “Waiting for more of the film”.

screens.whatIsPlaying.this.usage: Names a trailer or featurette inside a sentence in the video player, as in “Waiting for more of this”.

screens.whatIsWrongWithTheName.empty.usage: Error under the household name field when it is empty.

screens.whatIsWrongWithTheName.tooLong.o.usage: Error under the household name field when the name is too long, where the limit is one. {count} is the limit.
Error under the household name field when the name is too long. {count} is the most characters allowed.

screens.windowBar.updateAvailable.usage: Button in the desktop app's window bar, shown when a new version has been downloaded, that installs it.

server.books.chapterNumber.usage: Name given to a chapter of an audiobook or book that has no title of its own. {number} is its position.

server.books.partNumber.usage: Name given to a part of an ebook that has no title of its own. {number} is its position.

server.catalogue.episodeNumber.usage: Title given to an episode the film catalogue has not named yet. {number} is its number in the season.

server.defaults.aLibrary.usage: Stands in for the name of a library that has since been removed, in webhook messages such as “A library finished scanning”.

server.defaults.aRole.usage: Stands in for the name of a role that has since been deleted, in webhook messages such as “Sam no longer has a role”. Lower case, as it sits inside a sentence.

server.defaults.anAdministrator.usage: Name shown for who sent a command, such as “pause”, to a music player when an administrator sent it from the admin area.

server.defaults.anotherDevice.usage: Name shown for the device that sent a command, such as “play”, when it did not say what it is.

server.defaults.me.usage: Name given to a new profile when nobody gave it a name.

server.defaults.somebody.usage: Stands in for the name of a person the server cannot name, in webhook messages and lists of share links.

server.defaults.someone.usage: Stands in for the name of a person in a watch party whose name is not known.

server.defaults.something.usage: Stands in for the title of a download whose film or episode is no longer in the library.

server.defaults.unknownDevice.usage: Name shown for a device or browser that did not say what it is, in lists of signed-in devices and open tabs.

server.describeDevice.android.usage: Name shown in the list of signed-in devices for the app on an Android phone or TV.

server.describeDevice.app.usage: Name shown in the list of signed-in devices for the phone or TV app. {device} is the device’s own name, such as “iPhone 15”.

server.describeDevice.apple.usage: Name shown in the list of signed-in devices for the app on an iPhone, iPad or Apple TV.

server.describeDevice.browserOn.usage: Name shown in the list of signed-in devices for a web browser. {browser} is the browser, such as Firefox, and {system} the operating system, such as Windows.

server.describeDevice.desktop.usage: Name shown in the list of signed-in devices for the desktop app, when the computer it runs on is not known.

server.describeDevice.desktopOn.usage: Name shown in the list of signed-in devices for the desktop app. {system} is the computer’s operating system, such as macOS.

server.discord.account.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that says which account a viewer used.

server.discord.accountCreated.usage: Title of the Discord message sent when an account is made. {name} is the person’s name.

server.discord.accountDeleted.usage: Title of the Discord message sent when an account is deleted. {name} is the person’s name.

server.discord.added.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that says how many items a scan added.

server.discord.andMore.usage: Last line of the list of what arrived, in the Discord message sent when a scan finishes, when there were too many to list. {count} is how many more.

server.discord.arrivedIn.usage: Text of the Discord message sent when something arrives in a library and has no description of its own. {library} is the library.

server.discord.attempts.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that says how many times a background job has failed in a row.

server.discord.change.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that says whether a role was given or taken away.

server.discord.closed.usage: Title of the Discord message sent when somebody closes the app. {viewer} is who.

server.discord.device.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that says which device or browser somebody used.

server.discord.diskLow.usage: Title of the Discord message sent when a disk is nearly full. {disk} is where it is mounted.

server.discord.diskRecovered.usage: Title of the Discord message sent when a disk that was nearly full has room again. {disk} is where it is mounted.

server.discord.free.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that says how much room is left on a disk.

server.discord.from.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that gives the network address somebody connected from.

server.discord.genres.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that lists the genres of a film or series.

server.discord.given.usage: Value of the “Change” field in a Discord message when somebody was given a role.

server.discord.guestOf.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that says whose share link a viewer is watching through.

server.discord.howToFix.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that links to instructions for fixing a problem.

server.discord.jobFailed.usage: Title of the Discord message sent when a background job fails. {label} is the job’s name.

server.discord.jobFinished.usage: Title of the Discord message sent when a background job finishes. {label} is the job’s name.

server.discord.jobStalled.usage: Title of the Discord message sent when a background job keeps failing. {label} is the job’s name.

server.discord.kind.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that says whether something is a film, an episode or a track.

server.discord.libraries.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that lists the libraries that finished scanning.

server.discord.librariesScanned.one.usage: Title of the Discord message sent when several library scans started together finish. {count} is how many libraries.

server.discord.librariesScanned.other.usage: Title of the Discord message sent when several library scans started together finish. {count} is how many libraries.

server.discord.library.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that says which library something is in.

server.discord.libraryScanned.usage: Title of the Discord message sent when a library scan finishes. {library} is the library.

server.discord.noLongerIn.usage: Text of the Discord message sent when something leaves a library and has no description of its own. {library} is the library.

server.discord.of.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that gives the total size of a disk, following the “Free” field.

server.discord.opened.usage: Title of the Discord message sent when somebody opens the app. {viewer} is who.

server.discord.playing.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that says how a video is being played, such as unchanged or converted.

server.discord.quality.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that gives the picture quality of a video, such as 4K.

server.discord.rating.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that gives a film or series’ rating.

server.discord.removed.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that says how many items a scan removed.

server.discord.role.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that names a role.

server.discord.rolesChanged.usage: Title of the Discord message sent when somebody is given a role or has one taken away. {name} is who.

server.discord.runtime.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that gives how long a film or episode runs.

server.discord.signInRefused.usage: Title of the Discord message sent when somebody’s sign-in was refused.

server.discord.signedIn.usage: Title of the Discord message sent when somebody signs in. {name} is who.

server.discord.startedWatching.usage: Text of the Discord message sent when somebody starts watching; the title of what they watch is above it. {viewer} is who.

server.discord.stayed.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that says how long somebody had the app open.

server.discord.stoppedAt.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that says how far through a video somebody stopped watching.

server.discord.stoppedWatching.usage: Text of the Discord message sent when somebody stops watching; the title of what they watched is above it. {viewer} is who.

server.discord.takenAway.usage: Value of the “Change” field in a Discord message when a role was taken away from somebody.

server.discord.tried.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that gives the email address somebody tried to sign in with.

server.discord.unreadable.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that says how many files a scan could not read.

server.discord.updated.usage: Name of the field in a Discord message that says how many items a scan updated.

server.discovery.name.usage: The name a server announces itself by on the local network, which the phone and TV apps list when looking for a server. {host} is the computer’s name.

server.downloads.fallbackName.usage: The file name a kept film is saved under when its title has nothing that can be used in a file name.

server.downloads.gone.value: It is no longer in the library, so it cannot be prepared.
server.downloads.gone.usage: Shown beside a download that failed because its film or episode was removed from the library.

server.downloads.notPrepared.value: The media service could not prepare it. Ask again to try once more.
server.downloads.notPrepared.usage: Shown beside a download that failed because the media service could not prepare the file.

server.downloads.original.usage: Label of the choice, when keeping a film to watch offline, to keep the file as it is rather than a smaller copy.

server.downloads.wouldNotStart.value: The media service would not start it: {file}
server.downloads.wouldNotStart.usage: Shown beside a download that failed because the media service refused to prepare it. {file} is what it said.

server.errors.accountAdminElsewhere.usage: Error returned when a built-in account-administration address is used instead of the one the server provides. The address is left as it is.

server.errors.accountOutranks.value: That account is at or above your own rank.
server.errors.accountOutranks.usage: Error returned when an administrator tries to change an account whose role is as high as or higher than their own.

server.errors.addressHasAccount.value: That address already has an account.
server.errors.addressHasAccount.usage: Error returned when a profile is given an email address that already belongs to an account.

server.errors.addressInUse.value: That address is already in use.
server.errors.addressInUse.usage: Error returned when an email address is already used by another account.

server.errors.adminRoleUndeletable.value: A role granting administrator cannot be deleted. Change what it grants, or move its holders first.
server.errors.adminRoleUndeletable.usage: Error returned when somebody tries to delete a role that makes its holders administrators.

server.errors.administratorNotCreated.value: The administrator account could not be created.
server.errors.administratorNotCreated.usage: Error returned when the first-run setup could not make the administrator account.

server.errors.alreadyCalledThat.value: There is already something called that.
server.errors.alreadyCalledThat.usage: Error returned when a new folder would have the same name as something already there.

server.errors.alreadyInLibrary.value: It is in the library already, so there is nothing left to cancel.
server.errors.alreadyInLibrary.usage: Error returned when somebody cancels a request that has already arrived in the library.

server.errors.artworkUnreadable.value: That artwork could not be read.
server.errors.artworkUnreadable.usage: Error returned when the artwork file for an item could not be read.

server.errors.cannotGrantUnheld.value: You cannot grant a permission you do not hold.
server.errors.cannotGrantUnheld.usage: Error returned when somebody tries to give a role a permission they do not have themselves.

server.errors.catalogueKnowsNobody.value: The catalogue knows nobody by that identifier.
server.errors.catalogueKnowsNobody.usage: Error returned when a person (actor or crew) that was asked about is not in the film catalogue.

server.errors.catalogueUnknown.value: The catalogue does not know that, or cannot be asked just now.
server.errors.catalogueUnknown.usage: Error returned when the catalogue does not know what was asked about or could not be reached.

server.errors.catalogueUnknownSeries.value: The catalogue does not know that series, or cannot be asked.
server.errors.catalogueUnknownSeries.usage: Error returned when the film catalogue does not know a TV series or could not be reached.

server.errors.chooseProfileFirst.usage: Error returned when something needs a profile but the signed-in account has not chosen one.

server.errors.couldNotBeDone.usage: Error returned when a change to a file failed for a reason the server cannot name.

server.errors.deviceNotConnected.usage: Error returned when something is sent to a device that is no longer connected.

server.errors.deviceNotYours.value: That device is not one of yours, or is not there.
server.errors.deviceNotYours.usage: Error returned when a device that was asked to play something belongs to somebody else or is gone.

server.errors.entryNotInYourPlaylist.value: That entry is not in a playlist of yours.
server.errors.entryNotInYourPlaylist.usage: Error returned when somebody tries to remove a track from a playlist that is not theirs.

server.errors.entryNotMoved.value: That entry could not be moved.
server.errors.entryNotMoved.usage: Error returned when a track could not be moved within a playlist.

server.errors.fileAlreadyThere.value: There is already a file called that.
server.errors.fileAlreadyThere.usage: Error returned when an uploaded file would have the same name as a file already there.

server.errors.fileNotDeleted.value: The file could not be deleted.
server.errors.fileNotDeleted.usage: Error returned when a file could not be deleted for a reason the server cannot name.

server.errors.fileNotWritten.value: The file could not be written.
server.errors.fileNotWritten.usage: Error returned when an uploaded file could not be written for a reason the server cannot name.

server.errors.fileOutsideLibrary.value: That file is not inside its library, so Valence will not delete it.
server.errors.fileOutsideLibrary.usage: Error returned when an item is to be deleted but its file lies outside its library.

server.errors.folderIntoItself.value: A folder cannot be moved into itself.
server.errors.folderIntoItself.usage: Error returned when somebody tries to move a folder inside itself.

server.errors.folderNameSingle.value: A folder’s name is a single name, with no slashes in it.
server.errors.folderNameSingle.usage: Error returned when a new folder is given a name containing slashes.

server.errors.forAdministrators.usage: Error returned when somebody who is not an administrator tries something only administrators may do.

server.errors.forMusicAskers.value: That is for somebody who may ask for music.
server.errors.forMusicAskers.usage: Error returned when somebody who may not request music asks to hear samples of it.

server.errors.forWhoeverSetsUpRequesting.value: That is for whoever sets up requesting.
server.errors.forWhoeverSetsUpRequesting.usage: Error returned when somebody without permission to configure requesting tries to change it.

server.errors.giveWholePath.value: Give the whole path, starting from the root.
server.errors.giveWholePath.usage: Error returned when a folder path is given that does not start from the root of the disk.

server.errors.householdNoPicture.usage: Error returned when the household has no picture of its own.

server.errors.jobNeedsLibrary.usage: Error returned when a job that works on one library is started without naming it.

server.errors.libraryRootFolder.value: That is a library’s own folder. Change the library itself instead.
server.errors.libraryRootFolder.usage: Error returned when somebody tries to rename, move or delete the folder a library reads from.

server.errors.linkDoesNotWork.usage: Error shown when somebody opens a share link that does not exist.

server.errors.linkNoLongerWorks.usage: Error shown when somebody opens a share link that has ended.

server.errors.mayNotChangeFiles.value: Valence is not allowed to change files there.
server.errors.mayNotChangeFiles.usage: Error returned when the server lacks permission on the disk to change files.

server.errors.mayNotDelete.value: Valence is not allowed to delete files there.
server.errors.mayNotDelete.usage: Error returned when the server lacks permission on the disk to delete files.

server.errors.mayNotHoldApiKeys.value: This account may not hold API keys.
server.errors.mayNotHoldApiKeys.usage: Error returned when an account without permission tries to make or use API keys.

server.errors.mayNotMakeFolder.value: Valence is not allowed to make a folder there.
server.errors.mayNotMakeFolder.usage: Error returned when the server lacks permission on the disk to make a folder.

server.errors.mayNotManageWebhooks.value: This account may not manage webhooks.
server.errors.mayNotManageWebhooks.usage: Error returned when an account without permission tries to see or change webhooks.

server.errors.mayNotReadFolder.value: Valence is not allowed to read that folder.
server.errors.mayNotReadFolder.usage: Error returned when the server lacks permission on the disk to read a folder.

server.errors.mayNotSeeAllLinks.value: This account may not look at everybody’s links.
server.errors.mayNotSeeAllLinks.usage: Error returned when an account without permission asks to see every share link on the server.

server.errors.mayNotShare.usage: Error returned when an account without permission tries to make a share link.

server.errors.mayNotWithdrawLink.value: This account may not withdraw somebody else’s link.
server.errors.mayNotWithdrawLink.usage: Error returned when an account without permission tries to withdraw a share link someone else made.

server.errors.mayNotWrite.value: Valence is not allowed to write there.
server.errors.mayNotWrite.usage: Error returned when the server lacks permission on the disk to write an uploaded file.

server.errors.mediaServiceSilent.value: The media service did not answer.
server.errors.mediaServiceSilent.usage: Error returned when the separate media service that encodes video did not answer.

server.errors.mediaServiceUnreachable.value: The media service could not be reached.
server.errors.mediaServiceUnreachable.usage: Error returned when the server cannot reach the separate media service that encodes video.

server.errors.nameAlreadyThere.value: Something of that name is already there.
server.errors.nameAlreadyThere.usage: Error returned when a file or folder would be moved or renamed onto something already there.

server.errors.namePlain.value: A name is one plain name, with no slashes and no space at either end.
server.errors.namePlain.usage: Error returned when a file or folder is renamed to something that is not one plain name.

server.errors.noArtwork.usage: Error returned when an item has no artwork of the kind asked for.

server.errors.noCoverForAlbum.usage: Error returned when a music album has no cover picture.

server.errors.noCoverForBook.usage: Error returned when a book has no cover picture.

server.errors.noFileSent.usage: Error returned when an upload arrives with no file in it.

server.errors.noFolderToMakeItIn.value: There is no such folder to make it in.
server.errors.noFolderToMakeItIn.usage: Error returned when a new folder is to be made inside a folder that does not exist.

server.errors.noFrameThere.usage: Error returned when there is no preview picture for the moment in a video that was asked for.

server.errors.noLibraryForBooks.value: There is no library of books to put it in.
server.errors.noLibraryForBooks.usage: Error shown when somebody asks for a book but the server has no book library that takes requests.

server.errors.noLibraryForFilms.value: There is no library of films to put it in.
