server.errors.noLibraryForFilms.usage: Error shown when somebody asks for a film but the server has no film library that takes requests.

server.errors.noLibraryForMusic.value: There is no library of music to put it in.
server.errors.noLibraryForMusic.usage: Error shown when somebody asks for music but the server has no music library that takes requests.

server.errors.noLibraryForSeries.value: There is no library of series to put it in.
server.errors.noLibraryForSeries.usage: Error shown when somebody asks for a TV series but the server has no series library that takes requests.

server.errors.noLyrics.usage: Error returned when a track has no lyrics.

server.errors.noPictureOfArtist.usage: Error returned when a music artist has no picture.

server.errors.noPreviewYet.usage: Error returned when a preview clip has not been made yet.

server.errors.noSignInPicture.value: This server has no picture behind the way in.
server.errors.noSignInPicture.usage: Error returned when the server has no background picture for its sign-in page.

server.errors.noSuchAccount.usage: Error returned when an account that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchAlbum.usage: Error returned when a music album that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchApiKey.value: No such key on this account.
server.errors.noSuchApiKey.usage: Error returned when an API key that was asked about does not belong to the signed-in account.

server.errors.noSuchArtist.usage: Error returned when a music artist that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchBook.usage: Error returned when a book that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchChapter.usage: Error returned when a chapter of a book that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchDelivery.value: No such delivery, or the subscription is gone or turned off.
server.errors.noSuchDelivery.usage: Error returned when a past webhook delivery cannot be sent again.

server.errors.noSuchException.value: No such thing to make an exception of.
server.errors.noSuchException.usage: Error returned when an age-rating exception is made for something that does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchFolder.usage: Error returned when a folder that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchItem.usage: Error returned when a film, episode or other item that was asked about does not exist or is out of reach.

server.errors.noSuchJobKind.usage: Error returned when a kind of background job that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchJobWaiting.usage: Error returned when an administrator acts on a queued job that is no longer waiting.

server.errors.noSuchLibrary.usage: Error returned when a library that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchLink.usage: Error returned when a share link that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchMediaItem.usage: Error returned when a film, episode or track that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchPage.usage: Error returned when a page of a book that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchPartOfBook.value: No such part of that book.
server.errors.noSuchPartOfBook.usage: Error returned when a part of a reflowing book that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchPlaylist.usage: Error returned when a playlist that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchProfile.usage: Error returned when a profile that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchProfileOnAccount.value: No such profile on this account.
server.errors.noSuchProfileOnAccount.usage: Error returned when a profile that was asked about does not belong to the signed-in account.

server.errors.noSuchProfileOrLast.value: No such profile, or it is the only one left.
server.errors.noSuchProfileOrLast.usage: Error returned when a profile cannot be removed, either because it does not exist or because it is the last one on the account.

server.errors.noSuchProgramme.usage: Error returned when a TV series that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchReencode.usage: Error returned when a re-encode that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchRendition.usage: Error returned when a finished re-encode to review does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchRequest.usage: Error returned when a request that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchRole.usage: Error returned when a role that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchSeries.usage: Error returned when a TV series that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchSession.usage: Error returned when a playback session that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchSessionOrSegment.usage: Error returned when a piece of a video stream that was asked for does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchStyle.usage: Error returned when a drawn-avatar style that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchSubscription.usage: Error returned when a webhook subscription that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchSubscriptionOrOff.value: No such subscription, or it is turned off.
server.errors.noSuchSubscriptionOrOff.usage: Error returned when a test is sent to a webhook subscription that does not exist or is turned off.

server.errors.noSuchThumbnails.usage: Error returned when the seek bar preview pictures that were asked for do not exist.

server.errors.noSuchTrack.usage: Error returned when an audio or subtitle track that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchTrackInBook.value: No such track in that book.
server.errors.noSuchTrackInBook.usage: Error returned when an audiobook has no track by the number asked for.

server.errors.noSuchTrackToListenTo.value: No such track to listen to.
server.errors.noSuchTrackToListenTo.usage: Error returned when an audiobook track that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchTrigger.usage: Error returned when a schedule trigger for a job that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchUpload.usage: Error returned when an upload in progress that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.noSuchViewing.value: No such viewing for this profile.
server.errors.noSuchViewing.usage: Error returned when an entry in the viewing history that was asked about does not exist.

server.errors.notAPieceOfUpload.value: That is not a piece of this upload.
server.errors.notAPieceOfUpload.usage: Error returned when an upload sends a piece numbered beyond its end.

server.errors.notAReflowingBook.value: That is not a book that reflows.
server.errors.notAReflowingBook.usage: Error returned when reflowing text is asked of a book made of fixed pages.

server.errors.notCatalogueAddress.value: That does not look like a catalogue address or id.
server.errors.notCatalogueAddress.usage: Error returned when an administrator fixing a match types something that is neither a catalogue web address nor an id.

server.errors.notInThisBook.value: That is not in this book.
server.errors.notInThisBook.usage: Error returned when a file asked for is not part of the book.

server.errors.notInsideLibrary.value: That is not inside a library.
server.errors.notInsideLibrary.usage: Error returned when a file or folder that was asked about is outside every library.

server.errors.notPartOfShare.value: That is not part of what was shared.
server.errors.notPartOfShare.usage: Error returned when somebody watching through a share link asks for something the link does not cover.

server.errors.notReadByLibrary.value: That is not something this library reads.
server.errors.notReadByLibrary.usage: Error returned when a file uploaded to a library is of a kind that library does not read.

server.errors.notReadableDirectory.value: That path is not a readable directory.
server.errors.notReadableDirectory.usage: Error returned when a library is given a path that is not a folder the server can read.

server.errors.notSignedIn.usage: Error returned when something is asked of the server by somebody who is not signed in.

server.errors.notToOwnAccount.value: You cannot do that to your own account.
server.errors.notToOwnAccount.usage: Error returned when an administrator tries to do something to their own account that must be done by somebody else.

server.errors.notYourDevice.usage: Error returned when something is asked about a device that belongs to another account.

server.errors.nothingDecided.usage: Error returned when none of the chosen requests could be approved or refused.

server.errors.nothingPrepared.usage: Error returned when a prepared download that was asked for does not exist.

server.errors.nothingRunningThat.value: Nothing is running that under any id.
server.errors.nothingRunningThat.usage: Error returned when an administrator tries to stop a job that is not running.

server.errors.nothingRunningUnderId.value: Nothing is running under that id.
server.errors.nothingRunningUnderId.usage: Error returned when an administrator tries to stop a job run that is not running.

server.errors.nothingThere.usage: Error returned when a file or folder to change no longer exists.

server.errors.nothingToShare.value: There is nothing here to share.
server.errors.nothingToShare.usage: Error returned when a share link is asked for something that does not exist.

server.errors.oneQualityOnly.value: This server uses one quality for every request.
server.errors.oneQualityOnly.usage: Error returned when somebody asks for a quality on a server that uses one quality for every request.

server.errors.otherDisk.value: That would move it onto another disk, which Valence does not do. Copy it across on the machine instead.
server.errors.otherDisk.usage: Error returned when a file would be moved from one disk to another.

server.errors.passwordRequired.usage: Error returned when a password-protected profile is chosen without giving its password.

server.errors.pastTheEnd.one.value: That is past the end — the file runs {count} second.
server.errors.pastTheEnd.one.usage: Error shown when an administrator chooses a moment for a preview that is beyond the end of the video. {count} is how many seconds the video runs.

server.errors.pastTheEnd.other.value: That is past the end — the file runs {count} seconds.
server.errors.pastTheEnd.other.usage: Error shown when an administrator chooses a moment for a preview that is beyond the end of the video. {count} is how many seconds the video runs.

server.errors.phoneSignsInElsewhere.usage: Error returned when a one-time sign-in address is used instead of the phone sign-in. The address is left as it is.

server.errors.pickingReleaseForManagers.value: Picking a release is for whoever manages requesting.
server.errors.pickingReleaseForManagers.usage: Error returned when somebody without permission tries to choose which release of a request to download.

server.errors.pieceWrongSize.one.value: That piece was {count} byte, where {expected} were expected.
server.errors.pieceWrongSize.one.usage: Error returned when a piece of an upload arrives at the wrong size. {count} is how many bytes arrived and {expected} how many should have.

server.errors.pieceWrongSize.other.value: That piece was {count} bytes, where {expected} were expected.
server.errors.pieceWrongSize.other.usage: Error returned when a piece of an upload arrives at the wrong size. {count} is how many bytes arrived and {expected} how many should have.

server.errors.piecesMissing.one.value: {count} of its pieces has not arrived yet.
server.errors.piecesMissing.one.usage: Error returned when an upload is finished before all its pieces arrived. {count} is how many are still missing.

server.errors.piecesMissing.other.value: {count} of its pieces have not arrived yet.
server.errors.piecesMissing.other.usage: Error returned when an upload is finished before all its pieces arrived. {count} is how many are still missing.

server.errors.playlistNotYoursToChange.value: That playlist is not yours to change.
server.errors.playlistNotYoursToChange.usage: Error returned when somebody tries to change a playlist that belongs to somebody else.

server.errors.playlistNotYoursToDelete.value: That playlist is not yours to delete.
server.errors.playlistNotYoursToDelete.usage: Error returned when somebody tries to delete a playlist that belongs to somebody else.

server.errors.profileNoPicture.usage: Error returned when a profile has no picture of its own.

server.errors.profileNotAdded.value: That profile could not be added.
server.errors.profileNotAdded.usage: Error returned when a new profile could not be added to the account.

server.errors.qualityNotAvailable.value: That quality is not available to you.
server.errors.qualityNotAvailable.usage: Error returned when somebody asks for a quality they may not choose.

server.errors.readOnlyChangeFiles.value: That disk is read-only to Valence. Give it read-write access to change files there.
server.errors.readOnlyChangeFiles.usage: Error returned when a file cannot be changed because the server can only read that disk.

server.errors.readOnlyDelete.value: That disk is read-only to Valence. Give it read-write access to delete media there.
server.errors.readOnlyDelete.usage: Error returned when a file cannot be deleted because the server can only read that disk.

server.errors.readOnlyMakeFolders.value: That disk is read-only to Valence. Give it read-write access to make folders there.
server.errors.readOnlyMakeFolders.usage: Error returned when a folder cannot be made because the server can only read that disk.

server.errors.readOnlyUpload.value: That disk is read-only to Valence. Give it read-write access to upload media there.
server.errors.readOnlyUpload.usage: Error returned when a file cannot be uploaded because the server can only read that disk.

server.errors.releaseNotFetched.value: It was asked for, but that release could not be fetched: {reason}
server.errors.releaseNotFetched.usage: Error shown when an administrator picks a release for a request but the download could not start. {reason} is what the requests service said, in English.

server.errors.requestingOff.usage: Error returned when something about requesting is asked of a server that has requesting turned off.

server.errors.roleOutranks.value: That role is at or above your own.
server.errors.roleOutranks.usage: Error returned when an administrator tries to change a role as high as or higher than their own.

server.errors.runNotInHistory.value: That run is not in the history.
server.errors.runNotInHistory.usage: Error returned when a past job run that was asked about is not in the job history.

server.errors.sayFilmOrSeries.value: Say whether that id is a series or a film — the same number is both.
server.errors.sayFilmOrSeries.usage: Error returned when a catalogue number given to fix a match could mean either a film or a series.

server.errors.sayWhichPartsToClear.value: Say which parts of the library to clear.
server.errors.sayWhichPartsToClear.usage: Error returned when the clear-and-fetch-again job is started without choosing what to clear.

server.errors.sayWhichRelease.usage: Error returned when an administrator asks to fetch a release without choosing one.

server.errors.sessionBelongsToSomebodyEl.value: That session belongs to somebody else.
server.errors.sessionBelongsToSomebodyEl.usage: Error returned when a playback session belongs to another account.

server.errors.setupDone.usage: Error returned when the first-run setup is tried again on a server already set up.

server.errors.signInExpired.value: That sign-in has expired. Try again.
server.errors.signInExpired.usage: Error returned when a phone sign-in code has run out of time.

server.errors.tabNotOpen.usage: Error returned when an administrator acts on a browser tab or device that has since closed.

server.errors.tabNotWatching.value: That tab is not watching anything.
server.errors.tabNotWatching.usage: Error returned when an administrator tries to pause a tab that is not playing anything.

server.errors.thereIsNoSuchLibrary.usage: Error returned when a request names a library that does not exist.

server.errors.thumbnailsNotRendered.value: The thumbnails could not be rendered.
server.errors.thumbnailsNotRendered.usage: Error returned when the preview pictures along the seek bar could not be made.

server.errors.trackNoStyling.value: That track carries no styling of its own.
server.errors.trackNoStyling.usage: Error returned when styled subtitles are asked of a subtitle track that has no styling.

server.errors.trackUnreadable.value: That track could not be read.
server.errors.trackUnreadable.usage: Error returned when the file behind an audio track could not be read.

server.errors.uploadPathPlain.value: A file goes at a plain path inside the library, with no dots or empty names.
server.errors.uploadPathPlain.usage: Error returned when an upload is given a path that is not a plain path inside the library.

server.errors.wontDeliverThere.value: Valence will not send deliveries to that address.
server.errors.wontDeliverThere.usage: Error shown when a webhook is given an address the server refuses to send to, such as one on its own network.

server.errors.wouldLeaveNoAdministrator.value: That would leave nobody able to administer this server.
server.errors.wouldLeaveNoAdministrator.usage: Error returned when a change would leave the server with no administrator.

server.issues.bookReadsAnotherWay.value: That book already reads another way, so this was left out of it.
server.issues.bookReadsAnotherWay.usage: Issue recorded against a file left out of a book because the book is already read from a file of another kind.

server.issues.catalogueAnswered.usage: Issue recorded against a piece of artwork when the address it comes from answered with an error. {status} is the HTTP status number.

server.issues.catalogueSilent.usage: Issue recorded in the job history when the film catalogue did not answer.

server.issues.catalogueSilentKept.value: The catalogue did not answer. Keeping what was already known about this file.
server.issues.catalogueSilentKept.usage: Issue recorded in the job history against a file when the film catalogue did not answer during a scan.

server.issues.chapterNamesNotFound.value: its chapter names could not be looked up
server.issues.chapterNamesNotFound.usage: Issue recorded against a comic or manga when the names of its chapters could not be looked up. Lower case, as it follows the file’s name.

server.issues.detectionFailed.usage: Issue recorded in the job history when finding the intro and outro of an episode failed without saying why.

server.issues.downloadsNotFollowed.value: The downloads could not be followed.
server.issues.downloadsNotFollowed.usage: Shown in the server’s log when the server could not check on downloads in progress.

server.issues.eventNotPublished.value: An event could not be published.
server.issues.eventNotPublished.usage: Shown in the server’s log when an event could not be handed to webhook subscribers.

server.issues.failedSilently.value: It failed, and said nothing about why.
server.issues.failedSilently.usage: Shown in the job history and log when something failed without giving any reason.

server.issues.householdNotTold.value: The household could not be told.
server.issues.householdNotTold.usage: Shown in the server’s log when a notification could not be sent to the people on the server.

server.issues.imageTooLarge.value: That image is {megabytes}MB, which is too large to be artwork.
server.issues.imageTooLarge.usage: Issue recorded against a piece of artwork that is too large to keep. {megabytes} is its size, as a number.

server.issues.libraryFolderEmpty.value: Nothing was found where this library reads from, so what it already held has been left alone. Check the folder is still there — a network share that is not mounted looks exactly like an empty one.
server.issues.libraryFolderEmpty.usage: Shown in the job history when a scan found nothing at all in a library’s folder.

server.issues.noVideoStream.usage: Issue recorded in the job history against a file in a film or series library that has no picture in it.

server.issues.notABook.value: That file could not be opened as a book.
server.issues.notABook.usage: Issue recorded in the job history against a file in a book library that could not be opened.

server.issues.notATrack.value: That file could not be read as a track.
server.issues.notATrack.usage: Issue recorded in the job history against a file in a music library that could not be read.

server.issues.notAnImage.usage: Issue recorded against a piece of artwork when what arrived was not a picture. {type} is the kind of file it was.

server.issues.notListenedTo.usage: Issue recorded against an episode in the job history when its sound could not be analysed.

server.issues.notMoved.usage: Issue recorded when a profile photograph could not be moved to where the server now keeps them.

server.issues.pictureSubtitle.value: A subtitle held as pictures rather than text, which cannot be shown yet.
server.issues.pictureSubtitle.usage: Issue recorded against a subtitle file made of pictures rather than text.

server.issues.probeFailed.usage: Issue recorded in the job history against a file that could not be examined, for no reason given.

server.issues.providerFailed.usage: Issue recorded against a file in the job history when a source of film and series details failed without saying why.

server.issues.providerFailedWith.usage: Issue recorded against a file in the job history when a source of film and series details failed. {name} is the source and {reason} what went wrong.

server.issues.scanGaveUp.value: The media service stopped answering, so this scan gave up rather than reporting the rest of the library as unreadable. Nothing was deleted, and the files it never reached are still waiting to be read.
server.issues.scanGaveUp.usage: Shown in the job history when a scan stopped because the media service stopped answering.

server.issues.scanStopped.value: This scan was stopped before it finished. What it had already read is kept; nothing was deleted, and the library still counts as unscanned.
server.issues.scanStopped.usage: Shown in the job history when an administrator stopped a scan before it finished.

server.issues.unnamed.value: No metadata provider could name this file.
server.issues.unnamed.usage: Issue recorded in the job history against a file no source of film and series details could identify.

server.issues.unreachable.usage: Issue recorded against a piece of artwork when the address it comes from could not be reached.

server.issues.unreadable.usage: Issue recorded against a file when it could not be read, for no reason given.

server.jobs.aBackgroundJob.usage: Stands in for the name of a background job whose kind is not known, in the server’s log.

server.jobs.added.usage: Progress line shown under a scan of one folder once it has finished. {added} is how many items it added. Lower case, as it follows the job’s name.

server.jobs.askingCatalogue.usage: Progress line shown under a running background job while it asks the film catalogue about each request. Lower case, as it follows the job’s name.

server.jobs.broughtUpToDate.usage: Progress line shown under the job that brings requests up to date with the catalogue, once it has finished. {done} is how many requests it checked.

server.jobs.checkCatalogueConnectivity.d.value: Verifies the configured catalogue key can actually reach the catalogue.
server.jobs.checkCatalogueConnectivity.d.usage: Description of the background job “Check catalogue connectivity”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.checkCatalogueConnectivity.l.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.checkDiskSpace.description.value: Asks how much room is left on the filesystems Valence writes to, so a disk about to fill is something an operator hears about rather than something a scan discovers.
server.jobs.checkDiskSpace.description.usage: Description of the background job “Check disk space”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.checkDiskSpace.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.checkRequests.description.value: Asks the requests service whether it is still answering, and whether the VPN it downloads through is up, so an operator hears about either going quiet from a notification.
server.jobs.checkRequests.description.usage: Description of the background job “Check the requests service”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.checkRequests.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.checkTranscoder.description.value: Asks the transcoder whether it is still answering, so an operator hears about it going quiet from a notification rather than from somebody pressing play.
server.jobs.checkTranscoder.description.usage: Description of the background job “Check the transcoder”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.checkTranscoder.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.cleanupArtefactCache.descrip.value: Removes preview clips and scrub previews nothing addresses any more, freeing the space left behind by a reset or a change to how they are made.
server.jobs.cleanupArtefactCache.descrip.usage: Description of the background job “Clean up cached previews”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.cleanupArtefactCache.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.cleanupImageCache.descriptio.value: Removes cached artwork and profile photos nothing references any more, and the kept pages of books nobody has opened for 30 days.
server.jobs.cleanupImageCache.descriptio.usage: Description of the background job “Clean up cached images”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.cleanupImageCache.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.cleanupSessions.description.value: Clears out expired sign-in sessions and device-authorization codes.
server.jobs.cleanupSessions.description.usage: Description of the background job “Clean up sessions”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.cleanupSessions.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.clearLibraryParts.descriptio.value: Erases the chosen parts of a library, such as descriptions, artwork, trailers or preview clips, then fetches or makes them again from scratch. Everything else is left alone.
server.jobs.clearLibraryParts.descriptio.usage: Description of the background job “Clear and fetch again”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.clearLibraryParts.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.clearOldDownloads.descriptio.value: Deletes files prepared for keeping once they have gone unasked for as long as the server keeps them. A device that already fetched one keeps its copy.
server.jobs.clearOldDownloads.descriptio.usage: Description of the background job “Clear out old downloads”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.clearOldDownloads.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.detectSegments.description.value: Finds the intro and the recap in each episode by comparing the audio across a season, so viewers can skip them. Skips seasons already done.
server.jobs.detectSegments.description.usage: Description of the background job “Detect missing intros and outros”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.detectSegments.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.failed.usage: Reason shown in the job history for a background job that failed without saying why.

server.jobs.fetchLogos.description.value: Collects the lettering each title is written in, so a hero shows the programme's own logo rather than its name set in the interface's typeface. Skips items that already have one, and items no catalogue has named.
server.jobs.fetchLogos.description.usage: Description of the background job “Fetch missing logos”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.fetchLogos.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.found.usage: Progress line shown under the job that looks for a newly downloaded request in the library, when it was found. Lower case, as it follows the job’s name.

server.jobs.interrupted.value: The server restarted while this was running, so it was stopped.
server.jobs.interrupted.usage: Reason shown in the job history for a background job that was stopped because the server restarted while it ran.

server.jobs.lookedUp.usage: Progress line shown under a running background job that looks things up one by one. {done} is how many are done and {total} how many there are.

server.jobs.notFound.usage: Progress line shown under the job that looks for a newly downloaded request in the library, when it was not found. Lower case, as it follows the job’s name.

server.jobs.pruneHistory.description.value: Forgets viewings older than a year. What each profile has watched recently stays; the rest is removed, because this log grows every evening and nobody reads back that far.
server.jobs.pruneHistory.description.usage: Description of the background job “Prune old viewing history”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.pruneHistory.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.pruneJobHistory.description.value: Forgets job runs older than thirty days, and the per-item issues recorded against them.
server.jobs.pruneJobHistory.description.usage: Description of the background job “Prune old job history”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.pruneJobHistory.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.pruneLogs.description.value: Forgets log records past the age their level is kept for, so errors outlive the ordinary chatter. A retention policy nobody enforces is a table that grows until the disk fills.
server.jobs.pruneLogs.description.usage: Description of the background job “Prune old log records”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.pruneLogs.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.pruneResourceHistory.descrip.value: Forgets server load samples older than a week.
server.jobs.pruneResourceHistory.descrip.usage: Description of the background job “Prune old server load history”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.pruneResourceHistory.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.pruneWebhookDeliveries.descr.value: Forgets what was sent to webhook subscribers more than a week ago. Recent deliveries stay, so a receiver that has started failing is still visible; the rest goes, because this table gains a row for every event sent to everybody.
server.jobs.pruneWebhookDeliveries.descr.usage: Description of the background job “Prune old webhook deliveries”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.pruneWebhookDeliveries.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.reencode.description.value: Produces the encodes an administrator asked for, one file at a time. Each replacement waits for somebody to watch it and say it is fine before the original is disposed of, so this pauses rather than continuing once too many are waiting to be judged.
server.jobs.reencode.description.usage: Description of the background job “Work through the re-encoding queue”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.reencode.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.refreshRequests.description.value: Asks the catalogue again about every film not yet fetched and every series still running, so a new episode is wanted the day it is announced and a film is held until the release date it has now.
server.jobs.refreshRequests.description.usage: Description of the background job “Bring requests up to date with the catalogue”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.refreshRequests.label.value: Bring requests up to date with the catalogue
server.jobs.refreshRequests.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.regeneratePreviews.descripti.value: Renders preview clips for items that have none, using each library's forced audio language. Skips items that already have one.
server.jobs.regeneratePreviews.descripti.usage: Description of the background job “Generate missing previews”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.regeneratePreviews.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.regenerateTrickplay.descript.value: Renders the strip of images shown when scrubbing the seek bar, for items that have none. Skips items that already have one.
server.jobs.regenerateTrickplay.descript.usage: Description of the background job “Generate missing scrub previews”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.regenerateTrickplay.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.resetLibrary.description.value: Deletes every item in every library and starts again from nothing: scanning, then everything each item needs made for it. Hours of work on a large library.
server.jobs.resetLibrary.description.usage: Description of the background job “Reset and rebuild”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.resetLibrary.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.scanLibrary.description.value: Finds new, changed and removed files, then makes whatever they are still missing.
server.jobs.scanLibrary.description.usage: Description of the background job “Scan for changes”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.scanLibrary.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.scanned.usage: Progress line shown under a library scan once it has finished. Each gap is a number of items. Lower case, as it follows the job’s name.

server.jobs.sendMediaDigest.description.value: Collects what has been imported since the last time and says it once, so a scan of four hundred files is one notification rather than four hundred.
server.jobs.sendMediaDigest.description.usage: Description of the background job “Tell the household about new media”, shown under its name in the list of jobs.

server.jobs.sendMediaDigest.label.value: Tell the household about new media
server.jobs.sendMediaDigest.label.usage: Name of a background job, shown in the list of jobs an administrator can run or schedule.

server.jobs.transcoderSilent.value: {address} did not answer a health check.
server.jobs.transcoderSilent.usage: Reason given in the notification that the media service stopped answering. {address} is its network address.

server.music.unknownArtist.usage: Artist name given to a track whose file does not name its artist.

server.music.variousArtists.usage: Artist name given to an album whose tracks are by several different artists.

server.newMedia.and.usage: Joins the counts in the notification about what is new, such as “3 episodes and 1 film”. {joined} is the counts so far and {next} the next one.

server.newMedia.andLast.usage: The titles named in the notification about what is new. {names} is a comma-separated list of titles and {last} the final one.

server.newMedia.andMore.usage: The titles named in the notification about what is new, when there are too many to name. {names} is the named titles and {count} how many more.

server.newMedia.body.usage: Body of the notification about what is new. {counts} is how many of each kind arrived, such as “2 films”, and {names} their titles.

server.newMedia.episodes.one.usage: Part of the notification about what is new: how many episodes arrived.

server.newMedia.episodes.other.usage: Part of the notification about what is new: how many episodes arrived.

server.newMedia.films.one.usage: Part of the notification about what is new: how many films arrived.

server.newMedia.films.other.usage: Part of the notification about what is new: how many films arrived.

server.newMedia.something.usage: Title of the notification sent when both new music and new films or episodes arrive.

server.newMedia.songs.one.usage: Part of the notification about what is new: how many songs arrived.

server.newMedia.songs.other.usage: Part of the notification about what is new: how many songs arrived.

server.newMedia.toListenTo.usage: Title of the notification sent when new music arrives in the libraries.

server.newMedia.toWatch.usage: Title of the notification sent when new films or episodes arrive in the libraries.

server.notifications.downloadReadyBody.value: {title} has been prepared, and the device you asked on is fetching it.
server.notifications.downloadReadyBody.usage: Body of the notification sent when a film or episode somebody chose to keep offline has been prepared. {title} is its title.

server.notifications.downloadReadyTitle.usage: Title of the notification sent when a film or episode somebody chose to keep offline has been prepared. {title} is its title.

server.notifications.linkWithdrawnBody.value: {name} withdrew your link to {title}. Anybody watching through it has stopped.
server.notifications.linkWithdrawnBody.usage: Body of the notification sent when an administrator withdraws somebody’s share link. {name} is the administrator and {title} what the link was to.

server.notifications.linkWithdrawnTitle.value: A link you handed out was withdrawn
server.notifications.linkWithdrawnTitle.usage: Title of the notification sent to somebody when an administrator withdraws a share link they made.

server.notifications.listenInviteTitle.usage: Title of the notification inviting somebody to a listening party. {name} is who invited them.

server.notifications.listeningPartyRunni.value: They have a listening party running.
server.notifications.listeningPartyRunni.usage: Body of the notification inviting somebody to a listening party, when what is playing is not known.

server.notifications.listeningTo.usage: Body of the notification inviting somebody to a listening party. {title} is what is playing.

server.notifications.requestReadyBody.value: {title}, which you asked for, is in the library now.
server.notifications.requestReadyBody.usage: Body of the notification sent to somebody when a film, series or album they asked for arrives. {title} is its title.

server.notifications.requestReadyTitle.usage: Title of the notification sent to somebody when a film, series or album they asked for arrives. {title} is its title.

server.notifications.watchInviteTitle.usage: Title of the notification inviting somebody to a watch party. {name} is who invited them.

server.notifications.watchPartyRunning.value: They have a watch party running.
server.notifications.watchPartyRunning.usage: Body of the notification inviting somebody to a watch party, when what is playing is not known.

server.notifications.watching.usage: Body of the notification inviting somebody to a watch party. {title} is the film or episode playing.

server.parties.cannotRemoveYourself.value: You cannot remove yourself from a party you can simply leave.
server.parties.cannotRemoveYourself.usage: Shown when the host of a watch party tries to remove themselves rather than leave.

server.parties.left.usage: Shown to somebody who has left a watch party when they try to act in it.

server.parties.notAllowed.value: The host has not given you that.
server.parties.notAllowed.usage: Shown when somebody in a watch party tries something, such as pausing for everyone, that the host has not allowed them.

server.parties.notInAParty.value: You are not in a party.
server.parties.notInAParty.usage: Shown when somebody tries to act in a watch party while not in one.

server.parties.notInThatParty.value: You are not in that party.
server.parties.notInThatParty.usage: Shown when somebody tries to act in a watch party they are not part of.

server.parties.notRunning.usage: Shown when somebody tries to join or act in a watch party that has ended.

server.parties.removed.value: The host has removed you from that party.
server.parties.removed.usage: Shown to somebody the host removed from a watch party.

server.pictures.notAPicture.value: A picture has to be a JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF or GIF.
server.pictures.notAPicture.usage: Error shown when somebody uploads a profile or household picture that is not an image file.

server.pictures.tooDetailed.value: A picture has to be {edge} by {edge} or smaller.
server.pictures.tooDetailed.usage: Error shown when an uploaded picture has too many pixels. {edge} is the most pixels allowed along each side.

server.pictures.tooLarge.value: A picture has to be {megabytes} MB or smaller.
server.pictures.tooLarge.usage: Error shown when an uploaded picture is too large. {megabytes} is the largest size allowed, as a number.

server.pictures.unreadable.value: That file could not be read as a picture.
server.pictures.unreadable.usage: Error shown when an uploaded picture could not be opened.

server.playback.mediaServiceFailed.usage: Reason shown when a video could not be started because the media service failed without saying why.

server.playback.notSegmentable.value: The source cannot be cut into segments a player can start at, so it is encoded instead
server.playback.notSegmentable.usage: Reason shown to an administrator for why a stream is being converted rather than sent as it is.

server.presence.pausedByAdmin.value: This stream was paused by an admin.
server.presence.pausedByAdmin.usage: Message shown to a viewer whose video an administrator paused from the admin area.

server.presence.stoppedByAdmin.value: This stream was stopped by an admin.
server.presence.stoppedByAdmin.usage: Message shown to a viewer whose video an administrator stopped from the admin area.

server.reencode.alreadyQueued.value: This one is already queued or being worked on.
server.reencode.alreadyQueued.usage: Reason shown for why a file cannot be re-encoded when it is already waiting or being worked on.

server.reencode.alreadySmaller.value: This file is already at or below what was chosen, so re-encoding it would throw away a generation of quality and save nothing.
server.reencode.alreadySmaller.usage: Reason shown for why a file cannot be re-encoded to a quality it is already at or below.

server.reencode.beingWatched.value: Somebody started watching it, so it was left alone.
server.reencode.beingWatched.usage: Reason shown for a re-encode that was not replaced because somebody began watching the file.

server.reencode.cannotWrite.value: Valence cannot write to the folder this file is in.
server.reencode.cannotWrite.usage: Reason shown for a re-encode that failed because the server cannot write to the file’s folder.

server.reencode.failed.usage: Reason shown for a re-encode that failed without saying why.

server.reencode.fileGone.value: That file is no longer in the library.
server.reencode.fileGone.usage: Reason shown for a re-encode that failed because its file was removed from the library.

server.reencode.folderReadOnly.value: Valence cannot write to the folder this file is in. Media is usually mounted read only, which is sensible and means this cannot work until it is mounted read and write.
server.reencode.folderReadOnly.usage: Reason shown for why a file cannot be re-encoded when the server may not write to its folder.

server.reencode.gone.value: A file that is no longer in the library
server.reencode.gone.usage: Stands in for the title of a re-encode whose file has been removed from the library.

server.reencode.sameAsItIs.value: This would be the same picture in the same codec as the file itself, so it would be a second copy of what is already there.
server.reencode.sameAsItIs.usage: Reason shown for why a file cannot be re-encoded to what it already is.

server.reencode.subtitlesWouldBeLost.value: This file carries subtitles that a {container} file cannot hold, and the container is never changed. Re-encoding it would lose them.
server.reencode.subtitlesWouldBeLost.usage: Reason shown for why a file cannot be re-encoded without losing its subtitles. {container} is the file type, such as mp4.

server.reencode.unreadable.value: That file could not be read.
server.reencode.unreadable.usage: Reason shown for why a file cannot be re-encoded when it could not be read.

server.reencode.watchedNow.value: Somebody is watching this now. Replacing a file underneath a stream would end it.
server.reencode.watchedNow.usage: Reason shown for why a file cannot be re-encoded while somebody is watching it.

server.requests.clientNotAnswering.usage: Shown beside a download client that is not answering, when it did not say why.

server.requests.closedStream.usage: Shown in the server’s log when the requests service closed its report of download progress. {address} is its network address.

server.requests.didNotAnswer.usage: Shown when the requests service did not answer. {address} is its network address.

server.requests.notTheRequestsService.value: {address} answered, but not as the requests service
server.requests.notTheRequestsService.usage: Shown when something answered at the requests service’s address but was not it. {address} is the network address.

server.requests.refused.usage: Error shown when the requests service refused something without saying why.

server.requests.refusedToSay.value: {address} refused to say how it is
server.requests.refusedToSay.usage: Shown when the requests service refused to report its state. {address} is its network address.

server.requests.secretRefused.value: {address} refused the secret; REQUESTS_SECRET must be the same on both
server.requests.secretRefused.usage: Shown when the requests service refused the shared password. {address} is its network address; REQUESTS_SECRET is a setting’s name and stays as it is.

server.requests.stoppedStreaming.usage: Shown in the server’s log when the requests service stopped reporting download progress. {address} is its network address.

server.requests.tunnelDown.usage: Reason given in the notification that the VPN the downloads go through is down, when the requests service did not say why.

server.sharing.gone.usage: Stands in for the title of a share link whose film, series or book has been removed from the library.

server.shelves.comingSoon.usage: Heading of a row of films or series to ask for on the Requests page.

server.shelves.fantasy.usage: Heading of a row of books to ask for on the Requests page.

server.shelves.history.usage: Heading of a row of books to ask for on the Requests page.

server.shelves.mystery.usage: Heading of a row of books to ask for on the Requests page.

server.shelves.onTheAir.usage: Heading of a row of films or series to ask for on the Requests page.

server.shelves.popularAlbums.usage: Heading of a row of music to ask for on the Requests page.

server.shelves.popularArtists.usage: Heading of a row of music to ask for on the Requests page.

server.shelves.popularFilms.usage: Heading of a row of films or series to ask for on the Requests page.

server.shelves.popularSeries.usage: Heading of a row of films or series to ask for on the Requests page.

server.shelves.scienceFiction.usage: Heading of a row of books to ask for on the Requests page.

server.shelves.trendingBooks.usage: Heading of a row of books to ask for on the Requests page.

server.shelves.trendingFilms.usage: Heading of a row of films or series to ask for on the Requests page.

server.shelves.trendingSeries.usage: Heading of a row of films or series to ask for on the Requests page.

server.signIn.noAddress.usage: Stands in for the email address in the webhook message that a sign-in was refused, when none was typed. Lower case, as it sits inside a sentence.

server.signIn.refused.usage: Reason given in the webhook message that a sign-in was refused. Lower case, as it follows a dash in “A sign-in as sam@example.com was refused on Firefox — those details were not accepted.”

server.subtitles.trackNumber.usage: Name shown in the subtitle menu for a subtitle track that says neither its name nor its language. {number} is its position.

server.subtitles.unknownLanguage.usage: Name shown in the subtitle menu for a subtitle file that does not say what language it is in.

server.webhook.accountCreated.usage: Webhook message sent when an account is made. {name} is the person’s name.

server.webhook.accountDeleted.usage: Webhook message sent when an account is deleted. {name} is the person’s name.

server.webhook.andMore.usage: The list of what arrived, in the webhook message sent when a scan finishes, when there were too many to name. {names} is the named titles and {count} how many more.

server.webhook.approvedAsAsked.value: {title} was approved as it was asked for.
server.webhook.approvedAsAsked.usage: Webhook message sent when a request is approved automatically. {title} is what was asked for.

server.webhook.approvedBy.usage: Webhook message sent when somebody approves a request. {name} is who approved it and {title} what was asked for.

server.webhook.arrivalEpisodes.one.usage: One line of the webhook message listing what arrived: a series and how many of its episodes. {title} is the series.

server.webhook.arrivalEpisodes.other.usage: One line of the webhook message listing what arrived: a series and how many of its episodes. {title} is the series.

server.webhook.askedForAlbum.usage: Webhook message sent when somebody asks for an album. {name} is who asked and {title} the album.

server.webhook.askedForArtist.usage: Webhook message sent when somebody asks for a music artist. {name} is who asked and {title} the artist.

server.webhook.askedForBook.usage: Webhook message sent when somebody asks for a book. {name} is who asked and {title} the book.

server.webhook.askedForFilm.usage: Webhook message sent when somebody asks for a film. {name} is who asked and {title} the film.

server.webhook.askedForSeries.usage: Webhook message sent when somebody asks for a TV series. {name} is who asked and {title} the series.

server.webhook.available.value: {title} is ready to watch, as {name} asked.
server.webhook.available.usage: Webhook message sent when a request arrives in the library. {title} is what was asked for and {name} who asked.

server.webhook.catalogueReachable.value: The catalogue can be reached again. Nothing needs doing.
server.webhook.catalogueReachable.usage: Message sent to webhook subscribers when the film catalogue can be reached again.

server.webhook.catalogueUnreachable.value: The catalogue could not be reached. Scans will import files without matching them.
server.webhook.catalogueUnreachable.usage: Message sent to webhook subscribers when the film catalogue cannot be reached.

server.webhook.directPlay.usage: How a video is being played, at the end of the webhook message “Sam started watching Alien on Firefox, sent as it lies.”: the file is sent unchanged.

server.webhook.directStream.usage: How a video is being played, at the end of the webhook message “Sam started watching Alien on Firefox, with only the sound converted.”

server.webhook.diskLow.value: {disk} is running out of room — {free} left of {total}.
server.webhook.diskLow.usage: Webhook message sent when a disk is nearly full. {disk} is where it is mounted, {free} and {total} sizes such as “2 GB”.

server.webhook.diskRecovered.value: {disk} has room again — {free} free. Nothing needs doing.
server.webhook.diskRecovered.usage: Webhook message sent when a disk that was nearly full has room again. {disk} is where it is mounted and {free} a size such as “20 GB”.

server.webhook.downloadFailed.usage: Webhook message sent when a download fails. {title} is what was asked for, {client} the download program and {problem} what went wrong.

server.webhook.downloadStarted.usage: Webhook message sent when a request starts downloading. {title} is what was asked for and {client} the download program.

server.webhook.episodeName.usage: How an episode is named in webhook messages. {series} is the series, {season} and {episode} two-digit numbers and {title} the episode’s own title.

server.webhook.filed.usage: Webhook message sent when a download is moved into a library. {title} is what was asked for and {folder} where it went.

server.webhook.guestOf.usage: Stands in for the name of a viewer watching through a share link in webhook messages. {host} is who made the link.

server.webhook.howToFix.usage: A webhook message followed by a link to instructions. {sentence} is the message and {docs} the web address of the instructions.

server.webhook.indexerFailing.usage: Webhook message sent when a site the requests service searches for releases keeps failing. {name} is the site and {problem} what went wrong.

server.webhook.indexerWorking.value: The indexer {name} is answering again. Nothing needs doing.
server.webhook.indexerWorking.usage: Webhook message sent when a site the requests service searches for releases answers again. {name} is the site.

server.webhook.jobFailed.usage: Webhook message sent when a background job fails. {label} is the job’s name and {reason} why, in English.

server.webhook.jobFailedFor.usage: Webhook message sent when a background job for one library fails. {label} is the job’s name, {subject} the library and {reason} why.

server.webhook.jobFinished.usage: Webhook message sent when a background job finishes. {label} is the job’s name, such as “Scan for changes”.

server.webhook.jobFinishedFor.usage: Webhook message sent when a background job for one library finishes. {label} is the job’s name and {subject} the library.

server.webhook.jobWorking.value: {label} has run without failing. Nothing needs doing.
server.webhook.jobWorking.usage: Webhook message sent when a background job that kept failing works again. {label} is the job’s name.

server.webhook.mediaAdded.usage: Webhook message sent when something arrives in a library. {item} is its name and {library} the library.

server.webhook.mediaRemoved.usage: Webhook message sent when something leaves a library. {item} is its name and {library} the library.

server.webhook.neverSucceeded.one.value: {label} has never once succeeded — {count} attempt, most recently: {reason}
server.webhook.neverSucceeded.one.usage: Webhook message sent when a background job has never worked. {label} is the job’s name, {count} how many attempts and {reason} the latest failure.

server.webhook.neverSucceeded.other.value: {label} has never once succeeded — {count} attempts, most recently: {reason}
server.webhook.neverSucceeded.other.usage: Webhook message sent when a background job has never worked. {label} is the job’s name, {count} how many attempts and {reason} the latest failure.

server.webhook.playbackStarted.usage: Webhook message sent when somebody starts watching. {viewer} is who, {item} what, {device} the device and {how} how it is being played, such as “transcoded”.

server.webhook.playbackStopped.usage: Webhook message sent when somebody stops watching. {viewer} is who and {item} what.

server.webhook.playbackStoppedPart.value: {viewer} stopped watching {item} {percent}% of the way through.
server.webhook.playbackStoppedPart.usage: Webhook message sent when somebody stops watching part-way. {viewer} is who, {item} what and {percent} how far through, as a number.

server.webhook.refused.usage: Webhook message sent when a request is refused without a reason. {title} is what was asked for.

server.webhook.refusedBecause.usage: Webhook message sent when a request is refused. {title} is what was asked for and {reason} why.

server.webhook.releaseChosen.usage: Webhook message sent when a release is chosen for a request. {release} is the release’s name and {title} what was asked for.

server.webhook.remux.usage: How a video is being played, at the end of the webhook message “Sam started watching Alien on Firefox, repackaged but not re-encoded.”

server.webhook.requestsReachable.value: The requests service is answering again. Nothing needs doing.
server.webhook.requestsReachable.usage: Message sent to webhook subscribers when the requests service answers again.

server.webhook.requestsUnreachable.value: The requests service could not be reached — {reason}
server.webhook.requestsUnreachable.usage: Webhook message sent when the requests service stops answering. {reason} is why, in English.

server.webhook.roleGiven.usage: Webhook message sent when somebody is given a role. {name} is who and {role} the role.

server.webhook.roleTaken.usage: Webhook message sent when a role is taken from somebody. {name} is who and {role} the role.

server.webhook.scanCounts.usage: What a library scan changed, in the webhook message sent when it finishes. Each gap is a number of items.

server.webhook.scanCountsUnreadable.usage: What a library scan changed, in the webhook message sent when it finishes, when some files could not be read. Each gap is a number of items.

server.webhook.scannedLibrary.usage: One line of the webhook message sent when a scan finishes. {library} is the library’s name and {counts} what changed, such as “3 added, 0 updated, 1 removed”.

server.webhook.sessionEnded.usage: Webhook message sent when somebody closes the app. {viewer} is who and {device} the device or browser.

server.webhook.sessionEndedAfter.usage: Webhook message sent when somebody closes the app. {viewer} is who, {device} the device or browser and {span} how long they stayed, such as “1h 5m”.

server.webhook.sessionStarted.usage: Webhook message sent when somebody opens the app. {viewer} is who and {device} the device or browser.

server.webhook.sessionStartedFrom.usage: Webhook message sent when somebody opens the app. {viewer} is who, {device} the device or browser and {address} the network address.

server.webhook.shareViewer.usage: Stands in for the name of a viewer watching through a share link whose maker is not known, in webhook messages.

server.webhook.signInRefused.value: A sign-in as {identifier} was refused on {device} — {reason}
server.webhook.signInRefused.usage: Webhook message sent when a sign-in is refused. {identifier} is the email address tried, {device} the device or browser and {reason} why.

server.webhook.signInRefusedFrom.value: A sign-in as {identifier} was refused on {device} from {address} — {reason}
server.webhook.signInRefusedFrom.usage: Webhook message sent when a sign-in is refused. {identifier} is the email address tried, {device} the device or browser, {address} the network address and {reason} why.

server.webhook.signedIn.usage: Webhook message sent when somebody signs in. {name} is who and {device} the device or browser.

server.webhook.signedInFrom.usage: Webhook message sent when somebody signs in. {name} is who, {device} the device or browser and {address} the network address.

server.webhook.spanHours.usage: How long something lasted, in webhook messages. {hours} and {minutes} are numbers; “h” and “m” are short for hours and minutes.

server.webhook.spanMinutes.usage: How long something lasted, in webhook messages, when under an hour. {minutes} is a number; “m” is short for minutes.

server.webhook.spanSeconds.usage: How long something lasted, in webhook messages, when under a minute. {seconds} is a number; “s” is short for seconds.

server.webhook.stalledSinceWorked.one.value: {label} has failed every time it has run since it last worked — {count} attempt, most recently: {reason}
server.webhook.stalledSinceWorked.one.usage: Webhook message sent when a background job keeps failing. {label} is the job’s name, {count} how many attempts and {reason} the latest failure.

server.webhook.stalledSinceWorked.other.value: {label} has failed every time it has run since it last worked — {count} attempts, most recently: {reason}
server.webhook.stalledSinceWorked.other.usage: Webhook message sent when a background job keeps failing. {label} is the job’s name, {count} how many attempts and {reason} the latest failure.

server.webhook.test.value: Valence can reach this subscription. Nothing has gone wrong; somebody pressed test.
server.webhook.test.usage: Message sent to a webhook subscriber when an administrator presses the test button.

server.webhook.transcode.usage: How a video is being played, at the end of the webhook message “Sam started watching Alien on Firefox, transcoded.”: the picture is being converted.

server.webhook.transcoderReachable.value: The transcoder is answering again. Nothing needs doing.
server.webhook.transcoderReachable.usage: Message sent to webhook subscribers when the media service that encodes video answers again.

server.webhook.transcoderUnreachable.value: The transcoder could not be reached — {reason}
server.webhook.transcoderUnreachable.usage: Webhook message sent when the media service that encodes video stops answering. {reason} is why, in English.

server.webhook.vpnDown.value: The VPN the requests service downloads through is down — {reason}
server.webhook.vpnDown.usage: Webhook message sent when the VPN that downloads go through goes down. {reason} is why, in English.

server.webhook.vpnUp.value: The VPN the requests service downloads through is up.
server.webhook.vpnUp.usage: Message sent to webhook subscribers when the VPN the downloads go through comes back up.

server.webhook.vpnUpFrom.value: The VPN the requests service downloads through is up, leaving from {where}.
server.webhook.vpnUpFrom.usage: Webhook message sent when the VPN that downloads go through comes back up. {where} is its public address and country.

server.webhooks.deliveryFailed.value: The delivery could not be made.
server.webhooks.deliveryFailed.usage: Error shown in a webhook’s delivery history when a delivery failed without saying why.

server.webhooks.eventUnreadable.value: The queued event could not be read.
server.webhooks.eventUnreadable.usage: Error shown in a webhook’s delivery history when a queued event could not be read.

server.webhooks.receiverAnswered.usage: Error shown in a webhook’s delivery history when the receiver answered with an error. {status} is the HTTP status number.

tv.account.allRequests.usage: Button on the television’s Account page that opens the list of every request.

tv.account.differentServer.usage: Button that leaves this server so the television can be pointed at another one.

tv.account.signOut.usage: Button on the television’s Account page that signs this viewer out.

tv.account.signOutDetail.usage: Smaller words on the Sign out button, saying what signing out lets somebody do.

tv.account.watchingOn.usage: Under the viewer’s name on the television’s Account page. {server} is the address of the server the television watches from.

tv.account.watchingOnThis.usage: Under the viewer’s name on the television’s Account page, when the server’s address is not known.

tv.albumItem.detail.usage: Under an album’s cover on a music shelf. {artist} is who made it.

tv.arrivalBanner.pressToWatch.usage: On the banner that slides in when a requested title arrives. {icon} is replaced by a picture of the remote’s Play button, so keep it where the button belongs in the sentence.

tv.artistItem.detail.usage: Under an artist’s picture on a music shelf, saying what the tile is.

tv.askPage.cancelRequest.usage: Button on a request page that takes back the viewer’s own request.

tv.askPage.couldNotRequest.usage: Error shown on a request page when asking for the title failed and the server gave no reason.

tv.askPage.inTheLibrary.usage: After a season on a programme’s request page, saying the library has all of it.

tv.askPage.notFound.value: This title could not be found.
tv.askPage.notFound.usage: Shown in place of a request page when the film or programme could not be found.

tv.askPage.notNow.usage: Button that backs out of choosing a quality to request in.

tv.askPage.open.usage: Button on a film’s request page, once the library has it, that opens its own page.

tv.askPage.partlyHere.usage: After a season on a programme’s request page, saying the library has some of its episodes.

tv.askPage.request.usage: Button on a film’s request page that asks for it.

tv.askPage.requestIn.usage: Button on a request page that asks for the title in one quality. {quality} is the quality’s name, such as “4K”.

tv.askPage.requestSeasons.one.usage: Button on a programme’s request page that asks for the season chosen.

tv.askPage.requestSeasons.other.usage: Button on a programme’s request page that asks for the seasons chosen. {count} is how many.

tv.askPage.requested.usage: After a season on a programme’s request page, saying somebody has asked for it.

tv.askPage.requesting.usage: Button text while a request is being sent.

tv.askPage.seasonLine.one.usage: One season of a programme on its request page, when it has one episode. {season} is the season’s number.

tv.askPage.seasonLine.other.usage: One season of a programme on its request page. {season} is the season’s number and {count} how many episodes it has.

tv.askPage.seasonWithStanding.usage: A season on a programme’s request page, with where it stands after it. {season} is the season line, such as “Season 2 · 10 episodes”; {standing} is such as “Requested”.

tv.askPage.series.usage: Among the facts about a title on its request page, saying it is a programme rather than a film.

tv.bookPage.audiobook.usage: Small heading above an audiobook’s title on its page, saying what kind of thing it is.

tv.bookPage.chapters.one.usage: Among the facts about an audiobook, when it has one chapter.

tv.bookPage.chapters.other.usage: Among the facts about an audiobook: how many chapters it has.

tv.bookPage.nothingToListenTo.value: This book has nothing to listen to.
tv.bookPage.nothingToListenTo.usage: Shown in place of an audiobook’s page when it has no sound files, or could not be found.

tv.bookPage.startAgain.usage: Button on a half-listened audiobook’s page that plays it from the beginning.

tv.books.continueListening.usage: Heading of the row of audiobooks the viewer is part way through.

tv.books.empty.value: There are no audiobooks here yet.
tv.books.empty.usage: Shown on the Books tab when the library has no audiobooks.

tv.books.everyAudiobook.usage: Heading above the grid of every audiobook in the library.

tv.books.heading.usage: Large heading at the top of the Books tab, shown until an audiobook is focused and its title replaces it.

tv.catalogue.films.usage: Heading of the Films tab’s wall of posters.

tv.catalogue.noFilms.value: There are no films here yet.
tv.catalogue.noFilms.usage: Shown on the Films tab when the library has no films.

tv.catalogue.noShows.value: There are no shows here yet.
tv.catalogue.noShows.usage: Shown on the Shows tab when the library has no programmes.

tv.catalogue.shows.usage: Heading of the Shows tab’s wall of posters.

tv.catalogueCard.watched.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the tick on a poster the viewer has watched.

tv.chooseServer.addressLabel.usage: Label of the box for typing the address of a server.

tv.chooseServer.anotherAddress.usage: Name on the tile that lets somebody type in a server’s address.

tv.chooseServer.connect.usage: Button that tries the address typed in.

tv.chooseServer.couldNotReach.value: Valence at {address} could not be reached.
tv.chooseServer.couldNotReach.usage: Shown when the server this television used stops answering. {address} is its address.

tv.chooseServer.found.one.usage: Under the row of servers, when one has been found on the home network.

tv.chooseServer.found.other.usage: Under the row of servers: how many have been found on the home network.

tv.chooseServer.lead.value: Choose the server this Apple TV watches from.
tv.chooseServer.lead.usage: Under the heading of the screen for choosing a server.

tv.chooseServer.looking.usage: Under the row of servers while the television is still searching the home network for one.

tv.chooseServer.lookingForIt.usage: Button text while the television checks the address typed in.

tv.chooseServer.nothingAnswered.value: Nothing answered at {address}. Check the address and that Valence is running.
tv.chooseServer.nothingAnswered.usage: Error when no server answered at the address given. {address} is that address.

tv.chooseServer.title.usage: Heading of the screen for choosing which server the television watches from.

tv.chooseServer.typeItIn.usage: Under “Another address” on its tile, saying the address is typed.

tv.chooseServer.usedBefore.usage: Under a server’s address on its tile, saying this television has used it before.

tv.describeThisBuild.client.usage: At the foot of the television’s Account page, naming this build of the app for bug reports. {version} is the release number; {commit} is the code revision it was built from.

tv.describeThisBuild.server.usage: At the foot of the television’s Account page, naming the server’s build. {commit} is the code revision the server runs.

tv.devicesPanel.controlling.usage: A device in the list of places to play music, when this television is controlling it. {device} is its name, such as “Kitchen iPad”.

tv.devicesPanel.empty.value: Open Valence on another device, signed in as you, and it will be here.
tv.devicesPanel.empty.usage: Shown when the viewer has no other devices to play music on.

tv.devicesPanel.notPlaying.usage: A device in the list of places to play music, when nothing is playing on it. {device} is its name.

tv.devicesPanel.otherDevices.usage: Heading above the viewer’s other devices in the list of places to play music.

tv.devicesPanel.pausedOn.usage: A device in the list of places to play music, paused. {device} is its name and {title} the song it is paused on.

tv.devicesPanel.playing.usage: A device in the list of places to play music, playing. {device} is its name and {title} the song playing.

tv.devicesPanel.thisTv.usage: The first choice in the list of places to play music: this television.

tv.devicesPanel.thisTvPlaying.usage: The first choice in the list of places to play music, when music is already playing on this television.

tv.devicesPanel.title.usage: Heading of the panel listing the devices music can be played on.

tv.downloadPanel.downloaded.usage: Label for how much of a download has arrived, in the download panel on a title’s page.

tv.downloadPanel.speed.usage: Label for how fast a download is arriving, in the download panel on a title’s page.

tv.downloadPanel.timeLeft.usage: Label for how long a download has still to go, in the download panel on a title’s page.

tv.enterPassword.codeLabel.usage: Label of the box for the six-digit code from an authenticator app, asked for after the password.

tv.enterPassword.or.usage: Between the password form and the phone sign-in code, offering one or the other.

tv.enterPassword.passwordLabel.usage: Label of the box for a profile’s password.

tv.enterPassword.signingIn.usage: Button text while the password is being checked.

tv.enterPassword.someoneElse.usage: Button that goes back to the screen of faces to choose a different one.

tv.enterPassword.useYourPhone.usage: Heading above the code for signing in with a phone instead of a password.

tv.enterPassword.watch.usage: Button that signs in with the password typed and starts watching.

tv.enterPassword.wrongCode.usage: Error when the code from the authenticator app is wrong.

tv.episodeCard.watched.usage: Among the facts under an episode, saying the viewer has watched it.

tv.filmPage.addToMyList.usage: Button on a film’s page that keeps it in the viewer’s own list.

tv.filmPage.notFound.value: This film could not be found.
tv.filmPage.notFound.usage: Shown in place of a film’s page when it could not be found.

tv.filmPage.play.usage: Button on a film’s page that starts it.

tv.filmPage.playFromBeginning.usage: Button on a part-watched film’s page that plays it from the start.

tv.filmPage.removeFromMyList.usage: Button on a film’s page that takes it out of the viewer’s own list.

tv.filmPage.resumeFrom.usage: Button on a part-watched film’s page that carries on. {when} is how far in it was left, such as “1:02:15”.

tv.hero.moreInfo.usage: Button on the featured title at the top of the Home screen that opens its page.

tv.hero.play.usage: Button on the featured title at the top of the Home screen that starts it.

tv.hero.resume.usage: Button on the featured title that carries on watching it. {when} is how far in it was left, such as “1:02:15”.

tv.hero.series.usage: Among the facts about the featured title at the top of the Home screen, saying it is a programme rather than a film.

tv.home.empty.value: There is nothing to watch here yet.
tv.home.empty.usage: Shown on the Home tab when the library has nothing in it yet.

tv.likedSongs.detail.usage: Under the Liked Songs tile, saying what is in it.

tv.likedSongs.title.usage: Name of the playlist holding every song the viewer has liked.

tv.listening.backSeconds.one.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the audiobook player’s button that skips back, when by one second.

tv.listening.backSeconds.other.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the audiobook player’s button that skips back. {count} is by how many seconds.

tv.listening.bookBy.usage: Under the chapter’s name in the audiobook player: the book and who wrote it. {title} is the book’s title; {authors} its authors’ names.

tv.listening.chapterBefore.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the audiobook player’s button that goes to the previous chapter.

tv.listening.chapters.usage: Button in the audiobook player that lists its chapters, and the heading of that list.

tv.listening.endOfChapter.usage: On the sleep timer button, when it is set to stop at the end of the chapter.

tv.listening.leftInTheBook.usage: Under the audiobook player’s progress bar. {length} is how long is left, such as “3 hr 12 min”.

tv.listening.nextChapter.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the audiobook player’s button that goes to the next chapter.

tv.listening.onSeconds.one.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the audiobook player’s button that skips forward, when by one second.

tv.listening.onSeconds.other.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the audiobook player’s button that skips forward. {count} is by how many seconds.

tv.listening.pause.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the audiobook player’s button that pauses.

tv.listening.play.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the audiobook player’s button that plays.

tv.listening.sleepMinutes.usage: On the sleep timer button: how many minutes until playing stops.

tv.listening.sleepTimer.usage: Button in the audiobook player that sets when playing stops by itself, and the heading of its choices.

tv.listening.speed.usage: Heading of the choices of playing speed in the audiobook player.

tv.music.artists.usage: Heading of the row of artists on the Music tab.

tv.music.empty.value: There is no music here yet.
tv.music.empty.usage: Shown on the Music tab when the library has no music.

tv.music.heading.usage: Large heading at the top of the Music tab, shown until something is focused and its name replaces it.

tv.music.playlists.usage: Heading of the row of playlists on the Music tab.

tv.music.recentlyAdded.usage: Heading of the row of the latest music added to the library.

tv.musicCollection.album.usage: Small heading above an album’s title on its page.

tv.musicCollection.albums.usage: Heading of the row of an artist’s albums at the foot of their page.

tv.musicCollection.artist.usage: Small heading above an artist’s name on their page.

tv.musicCollection.play.usage: Button on an album, artist or playlist page that plays it from the start.

tv.musicCollection.playlist.usage: Small heading above a playlist’s name on its page.

tv.musicCollection.shuffle.usage: Button on an album, artist or playlist page that plays it in a random order.

tv.nowPlaying.artistsAndAlbum.usage: Under the song’s name on the now-playing screen. {artists} is who made it, and {album} the album it is from.

tv.nowPlaying.hideWords.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the button that hides a song’s lyrics.

tv.nowPlaying.like.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the heart that likes the song playing. {title} is the song’s name.

tv.nowPlaying.next.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the button that skips to the next song.

tv.nowPlaying.pause.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the button that pauses the music.

tv.nowPlaying.play.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the button that plays the music.

tv.nowPlaying.playOnAnotherDevice.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the button that opens the list of devices to play the music on.

tv.nowPlaying.playingOn.usage: On the now-playing screen, when the music is playing on another device. {device} is its name.

tv.nowPlaying.previous.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the button that goes back to the start of the song, or the song before.

tv.nowPlaying.repeat.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the repeat button, when nothing repeats.

tv.nowPlaying.repeating.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the repeat button, when the whole list repeats.

tv.nowPlaying.repeatingThisSong.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the repeat button, when the one song repeats.

tv.nowPlaying.showWords.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the button that shows a song’s lyrics beside it.

tv.nowPlaying.shuffle.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the shuffle button, when shuffle is off.

tv.nowPlaying.shuffleIsOn.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the shuffle button, when shuffle is on.

tv.nowPlaying.unlike.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the filled heart that takes back liking the song playing. {title} is the song’s name.

tv.nowPlaying.upNext.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the button that opens the list of songs queued next.

tv.nowPlayingChip.label.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the small chip in the corner that says what music is playing. {title} is the song’s name.

tv.partsOfDownload.arrivedOf.usage: How much of a download has arrived. {done} is how much has, and {size} how big it is altogether, each such as “1.2 GB”.

tv.partsOfDownload.underAMinute.usage: How long a download has left, when it is less than a minute.

tv.phoneSignIn.andEnter.usage: Second of the lines beside the code, between the web address to visit and the code to type there.

tv.phoneSignIn.couldNotStart.value: This Valence would not start a sign-in.
tv.phoneSignIn.couldNotStart.usage: Shown in place of the code when the server refused to begin signing in with a phone.

tv.phoneSignIn.expired.value: That code ran out. Here is a new one.
tv.phoneSignIn.expired.usage: Shown when the code to scan took too long to be used, as a new code replaces it.

tv.phoneSignIn.qrLabel.value: A code to scan with your phone's camera
tv.phoneSignIn.qrLabel.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the square code on screen.

tv.phoneSignIn.refused.usage: Shown when somebody declined, on their phone, to sign this television in.

tv.phoneSignIn.scanOrGoTo.value: Scan the code with your phone, or go to
