tv.phoneSignIn.scanOrGoTo.usage: First of three lines beside the code, followed on its own line by a web address, then “and enter”, then the code to type.

tv.player.audio.usage: In the player’s settings, the choice of sound track, and the heading of its list.

tv.player.couldNotPlay.usage: Shown in place of the picture when the player could not play something. {message} is the player’s own reason, usually in English.

tv.player.episodeLine.usage: An episode’s place and name, such as “S1: E3 · The Long Night”. {season} and {episode} are numbers; {title} is the episode’s name.

tv.player.goBack.usage: Button under an error in the player that leaves it.

tv.player.noReason.usage: Fills the gap in “This could not be played. (…)” when the player said nothing about why.

tv.player.normalSpeed.usage: The ordinary playing speed, in the player’s settings.

tv.player.off.usage: In the player’s settings: that subtitles, or Stats for nerds, are switched off.

tv.player.on.usage: In the player’s settings: that Stats for nerds is switched on.

tv.player.original.usage: The quality choice that plays the file as it is, without converting it.

tv.player.quality.usage: In the player’s settings, the choice of picture quality, and the heading of its list.

tv.player.speed.usage: In the player’s settings, the choice of playing speed, and the heading of its list.

tv.player.speedTimes.usage: A playing speed as a multiple, such as “1.5×”.

tv.player.statsForNerds.usage: In the player’s settings, switches on a panel of technical details about the stream.

tv.player.subtitles.usage: In the player’s settings, the choice of subtitles, and the heading of its list.

tv.player.turnedAway.value: This Valence turned the television away. Its sign-in may have run out, so go back and sign in again.
tv.player.turnedAway.usage: Shown in place of the picture when the server refused to stream to the television.

tv.playerControls.nextEpisode.usage: Button in the player that plays the next episode.

tv.playerControls.pause.usage: Button in the player that pauses.

tv.playerControls.play.usage: Button in the player that plays.

tv.playerControls.settings.usage: Button in the player that opens its settings.

tv.playerControls.skipSeconds.usage: On the player’s buttons that skip back or forward: by how many seconds, written short, such as “10s”.

tv.playlistItem.mine.usage: Under a playlist’s cover on a music shelf, for one of the viewer’s own.

tv.playlistItem.theirs.usage: Under a playlist’s cover on a music shelf, for somebody else’s. {owner} is whose it is.

tv.progressLine.watched.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the line under a poster showing how much of it has been watched.

tv.queuePanel.empty.usage: Shown in the Up next panel when nothing is queued after the song playing.

tv.queuePanel.title.usage: Heading of the panel listing the songs queued to play next.

tv.requestCard.whereAndHowFar.usage: Under a request’s poster while it downloads. {where} says where the request stands, such as “Downloading to library”; {percent} is how far through it is, such as “42%”.

tv.requestRow.askedForBy.usage: Beside where a request stands, when somebody else made it. {name} is who.

tv.requests.downloadingToLibrary.usage: Says a requested title is being downloaded into the library. Shown on its request card and above its download progress.

tv.requestsPage.empty.value: Nothing has been asked for yet.
tv.requestsPage.empty.usage: Shown on the Requests page when there are no requests.

tv.requestsPage.emptyHint.value: Find something in Search, and request it from its page.
tv.requestsPage.emptyHint.usage: Under “Nothing has been asked for yet.”, saying how to make a request.

tv.requestsPage.heading.usage: Heading of the page listing every request.

tv.scrubber.positionOf.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the bar showing how far through something is. {position} is the time reached and {duration} its whole length, such as “12:04 of 1:45:00”.

tv.scrubber.scrub.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the player’s progress bar, which can be dragged to move through the film.

tv.search.albums.usage: Heading of the row of albums found by a search.

tv.search.artists.usage: Heading of the row of artists found by a search.

tv.search.inYourLibrary.usage: Heading above what a search found in the library, shown when it also found titles the library does not have.

tv.search.notInYourLibrary.usage: Heading of the row of titles found by a search that the library does not have and could request.

tv.search.nothingCalled.usage: Shown when a search finds nothing. {query} is what was typed.

tv.search.placeholder.usage: Placeholder in the search box, saying what can be searched for.

tv.search.placeholderWithMusic.usage: Placeholder in the search box on a server with music, saying what can be searched for.

tv.search.playlists.usage: Heading of the row of playlists found by a search.

tv.search.songs.usage: Heading of the row of songs found by a search.

tv.serverCard.available.usage: Under a server found on the home network, saying it can be chosen.

tv.settingsMenu.title.usage: Heading of the player’s settings panel.

tv.showPage.episodes.usage: Heading above the row of episodes on a programme with only one season.

tv.showPage.markEveryUnwatched.usage: Button on a programme’s page, when every episode has been watched, that marks them all unwatched.

tv.showPage.markEveryWatched.usage: Button on a programme’s page that marks every episode as watched.

tv.showPage.markSeasonUnwatched.usage: Button on a programme’s page, when the season showing has been watched, that marks it unwatched.

tv.showPage.markSeasonWatched.usage: Button on a programme’s page that marks every episode of the season showing as watched.

tv.showPage.notFound.value: This programme could not be found.
tv.showPage.notFound.usage: Shown in place of a programme’s page when it could not be found.

tv.showPage.place.usage: An episode’s place in its programme, written short. {season} is the season number and {episode} the episode number, such as “S1: E3”.

tv.showPage.play.usage: Button on a programme’s page that plays the next episode. {place} is where it is, such as “S1: E3”.

tv.showPage.playFromFirst.usage: Button on a programme’s page that plays it from its very first episode.

tv.showPage.resumeFrom.usage: Button on a programme’s page that carries on with a part-watched episode. {place} is such as “S1: E3”; {when} is how far in it was left.

tv.showPage.seasons.one.usage: Among the facts about a programme, when it has one season.

tv.showPage.seasons.other.usage: Among the facts about a programme: how many seasons it has.

tv.streamStats.bitrate.usage: Name of a row in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.bufferedAhead.usage: Name of a row in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.container.usage: Name of a row in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.deciding.usage: A value in the Stats for nerds panel over the player, meaning the thing is still being decided by the server.

tv.streamStats.delivery.usage: Name of a row in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.direct.usage: A value in the Stats for nerds panel over the player, meaning the thing is sent as the file is (delivery method).

tv.streamStats.frameRate.usage: Name of a row in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.fromTheServer.usage: Name of a row in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.heading.usage: Heading of the panel of technical details about the stream, shown over the player.

tv.streamStats.hls.usage: A value in the Stats for nerds panel over the player, meaning the thing is sent as an HLS stream (a streaming format; normally left as is).

tv.streamStats.mediaId.usage: Name of a row in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.mode.usage: Name of a row in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.none.usage: A value in the Stats for nerds panel over the player, meaning the thing is absent.

tv.streamStats.notReported.usage: A value in the Stats for nerds panel over the player, meaning the thing is not reported by the player.

tv.streamStats.notStarted.usage: A value in the Stats for nerds panel over the player, meaning the thing is not started yet.

tv.streamStats.outputGroup.usage: Heading of a group of rows in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.planGroup.usage: Heading of a group of rows in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.playbackGroup.usage: Heading of a group of rows in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.position.usage: Name of a row in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.qualityAsked.usage: Name of a row in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.range.usage: Name of a row in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.reused.usage: Name of a row in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.session.usage: Name of a row in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.sessionGroup.usage: Heading of a group of rows in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.size.usage: Name of a row in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.sourceGroup.usage: Heading of a group of rows in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.startsAt.usage: Name of a row in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.subtitles.usage: Name of a row in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.title.usage: Name of the row in the Stats for nerds panel that gives the title playing.

tv.streamStats.tracks.one.usage: In the Stats for nerds panel, how many subtitle tracks the file has, when one.

tv.streamStats.tracks.other.usage: In the Stats for nerds panel, how many subtitle tracks the file has.

tv.streamStats.unknown.usage: A value in the Stats for nerds panel over the player, meaning the thing is not known.

tv.streamStats.video.usage: Name of a row in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.streamStats.warningsGroup.usage: Heading of a group of rows in the Stats for nerds panel, a technical panel over the player.

tv.titleSpread.starring.usage: Under a title’s description, naming the first few actors in it. {names} is their names, separated by commas.

tv.topBar.books.usage: Tab in the bar along the top of the television screen, for audiobooks.

tv.topBar.films.usage: Tab in the bar along the top of the television screen.

tv.topBar.home.usage: Tab in the bar along the top of the television screen.

tv.topBar.music.usage: Tab in the bar along the top of the television screen.

tv.topBar.profile.usage: Read out by VoiceOver for the viewer’s face at the right-hand end of the bar, which opens their Account page. {name} is the profile’s name.

tv.topBar.shows.usage: Tab in the bar along the top of the television screen, for television programmes.

tv.trackRow.explicit.usage: Under a song’s name in a list: the E marks it as explicit, followed by who made it. {artists} is the artists’ names.

tv.upNext.keepWatching.usage: Button on the card asking whether anybody is still watching, which plays on.

tv.upNext.playIn.usage: Button on the card offering the next episode, counting down. {seconds} is how many seconds until it plays by itself.

tv.upNext.stay.usage: Button on the next-episode card that stays on this episode.

tv.upNext.stillWatching.usage: Heading of the card shown after several episodes in a row, asking whether anybody is still there.

tv.upNext.upNext.usage: Heading of the card offering the next episode.

tv.useCollection.albums.other.usage: How many albums an artist has; part of the facts on their page.

tv.useCollection.artistFacts.usage: Facts on an artist’s page. {albums} is such as “4 albums” and {songs} such as “52 songs”.

tv.useCollection.lengthInMinutes.usage: How long an album or playlist lasts, under an hour. {songs} is such as “12 songs”; {minutes} is a number of minutes.

tv.useCollection.songs.one.usage: How many songs there are, when it is one; part of the facts on a music page.

tv.useCollection.songs.other.usage: How many songs there are; part of the facts on a music page.

tv.whoIsWatching.couldNotReach.value: This Valence could not be reached.
tv.whoIsWatching.couldNotReach.usage: Shown in place of the faces when the server did not answer.

tv.whoIsWatching.differentServer.usage: Button that leaves this server so the television can be pointed at another one.

tv.whoIsWatching.footer.usage: At the foot of the screen of faces. {server} is the server’s address, such as “192.168.1.10:8420”.

tv.whoIsWatching.footerNoServer.usage: At the foot of the screen of faces, when the server’s address is not known.

tv.whoIsWatching.signInWithPhone.usage: Heading of the screen when the server hides its faces and asks for a phone to sign in.

tv.whoIsWatching.title.usage: Heading of the screen of faces, where each viewer chooses their own.

tv.yourRequests.heading.usage: Heading of the row of this viewer’s own latest requests, on the television’s Account page.

ui.button.working.usage: Read out by screen readers for the spinner on a button while what it started is still happening.

ui.captionColours.cyan.usage: A colour that can be chosen for captions’ text or background in the player’s caption settings.

ui.captionColours.green.usage: A colour that can be chosen for captions’ text or background in the player’s caption settings.

ui.captionColours.red.usage: A colour that can be chosen for captions’ text or background in the player’s caption settings.

ui.captionColours.white.usage: A colour that can be chosen for captions’ text or background in the player’s caption settings.

ui.captionColours.yellow.usage: A colour that can be chosen for captions’ text or background in the player’s caption settings.

ui.commandPalette.emptyLabel.usage: Shown in the quick search dialog in place of results when nothing matches what was typed.

ui.couldNotRead.body.value: {what} could not be read. The server may be unreachable, or this session may have ended.

ui.dataTable.previousPage.usage: Read out by screen readers, and shown as a tooltip, for the arrow button that shows the table’s previous page.

ui.dataTable.showingSome.usage: Under a table that loads more rows as it scrolls. {shown} is how many rows are drawn so far; {total} is how many there are.

ui.filePicker.working.usage: Read out by screen readers for the spinner on a file-choosing button while the chosen file is being sent.

ui.filterMenu.clearFilters.usage: Last item in the filter menu, which takes every chosen filter off at once.

ui.filterMenu.filters.usage: Button text of the menu that narrows a list, such as the films in the library.

ui.mediaCard.watched.usage: Tooltip, and screen-reader text, for the tick on a poster when the viewer has watched all of it.

ui.navBar.here.usage: Shown beside the section the viewer is already on, in the narrow-screen sections menu.

ui.navBar.places.usage: Read out by screen readers for the menu button that opens the app’s sections on a narrow screen.

ui.navBar.sections.usage: Read out by screen readers to name the top navigation bar that holds the app’s sections.

ui.pageDots.showNamed.usage: Read out by screen readers for one of the dots under a slideshow. {name} is the name of what that slide shows, such as a film title.

ui.pageDots.showPage.usage: Read out by screen readers for one of the dots under a slideshow of featured titles. {page} is the number of the slide it shows.

ui.rail.backAPage.usage: Read out by screen readers for the arrow button that scrolls a row of posters back by a page. {title} is the row’s heading, such as “Continue watching”.

ui.rail.forwardAPage.usage: Read out by screen readers for the arrow button that scrolls a row of posters on by a page. {title} is the row’s heading, such as “Continue watching”.

ui.readMore.less.usage: Button under a passage shown in full, which shortens it again.

ui.readMore.more.usage: Button under a shortened passage, such as a person’s biography, that shows the rest of it.

ui.sidebar.close.usage: Read out by screen readers, and shown as a tooltip, for the button that folds the admin area’s side menu away.

ui.timeBars.dragToZoom.value: Drag across the bars to zoom in
ui.timeBars.dragToZoom.usage: Hint under a bar chart of events over time, telling somebody they can drag across it to look at a shorter period.

ui.timeBars.empty.usage: Shown in place of a bar chart of events over time when nothing happened in the period chosen.

ui.trendChart.empty.usage: Shown in place of a small chart on the admin overview when nothing has been measured for it yet.

web.pushWorker.defaultBody.usage: Text of a push notification when the server sent none of its own.
